source.title: Serre's modularity conjecture (II)
source.read: The authors' copy proofs.pdf from the first author's UCLA page (98 pages, PDF dated 30 May 2009, SHA-256 53f45f8be3b3c7de19f42417920d34a809e908412826490ebed90f07c8e86ed4), fetched 29 September 2026 without TLS certificate verification (the UCLA chain is incomplete) and checked against the hash that the atlas's GL2ModularityLifting, GlobalGaloisDeformations, LocalGaloisDeformationRings and PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems packets record for the same file. It contains the refereeing changes (Diamond's observation on fixing determinants for p = 2, §1.1) and is taken to be the accepted version; the Springer text was not available and was not compared. Locators are the copy's own pages. The earlier ESI preprint 1892 (2007) was not read.
readSections: §3 Structure of certain local deformation rings (3.1–3.3)
§4 Global deformation rings: basics and presentations (4.1–4.2)
§5 Galois cohomology: auxiliary primes and twists (5.1–5.6)
§6 Taylor's potential version of Serre's conjecture
§7 p-adic modular forms on definite quaternion algebras (7.1–7.6)
§8 Modular lifts with prescribed local properties (8.1–8.4)

summary: KW II proves the two technical theorems stated in KW I: Theorem 4.1 (modularity lifting for odd lifts of modular residual representations, including the new 2-adic case) and Theorem 5.1 (existence of p-adic lifts of four prescribed types, placed in almost strictly compatible systems). The route is Kisin's framed deformation theory: §2 builds the algebra of framed and unframed deformation rings, quotients by diagonalisable groups and inertia-rigid deformations; §3 computes the local deformation rings at ∞, above p and away from p (domains or flat with regular generic fibre, of the right dimension); §4 gives global presentations and the lower bound on dimension from Wiles' formula with fixed determinant; §5 constructs Taylor–Wiles auxiliary primes, with the new twisting and class-group argument for p = 2; §6 extends Taylor's potential modularity (Theorem 6.1); §7 develops forms on definite quaternion algebras over totally real fields with ∆_Q-freeness in the presence of isotropy; §8 constructs modular lifts with prescribed local properties after allowable base change (Theorems 8.2, 8.4); §9 proves R = T by Taylor–Wiles–Kisin patching, with determinants fixed only locally for p = 2 (Propositions 9.2, 9.3, Theorem 9.7); §10 deduces finiteness of deformation rings from potential modularity (Theorem 10.1) and Theorems 4.1 and 5.1 of KW I, with compatible systems by Brauer induction. Almost all of this is planned in the atlas, node by node, across LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08, GlobalGaloisDeformations R04, DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03, GL2ModularityLifting R22, PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23–R24, HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18 and AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19. The missing items are general inputs these layers use without stating them (commutative algebra of CNL algebras and regularity, Grunwald–Wang, cohomology of SL₂ in characteristic 2, Khare's lemmas, Taylor's neatness lemma) and the totally real level-lowering and lifting theorems of §8; all go to existing layers as sources. The extraction records 33 source issues, among them four gaps that affect proofs: the comparison maps in the proof of Theorem 10.1 exist only modulo p; the §3.3.3 construction for p = 2 needs ε^{q+1} = 1; Lemma 7.2(i) misses the case N(v) ≡ −1 mod p; and Theorem 6.1(iii)(b) is proved only for ℓ_i ≠ 2.

items.name: §1: standing hypotheses on ρ̄
items.statement: ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝔽), 𝔽 a finite field of characteristic p, is of S-type (odd and absolutely irreducible), with 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1 if p > 2; ρ̄ has non-solvable image when p = 2, and ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ(µ_p)}} is absolutely irreducible when p > 2. For a number field F, ρ̄_F := ρ̄|_{G_F}.
items.locator: §1, p. 2, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: S-type is AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.6/s-type-arises-from-and-modular; the image hypotheses (non-solvable for p = 2, cyclotomic absolute irreducibility for p > 2) are GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/image-hypotheses.

items.name: Notation 1.2: the p-adic cyclotomic character χ_p
items.statement: χ_p : G_ℚ → ℤ_p^× is the p-adic cyclotomic character (g(ζ) = ζ^{χ_p(g)} for all p-power roots of unity ζ); its reduction mod p is the mod p cyclotomic character χ̄_p. For a number field F the restriction to G_F is denoted by the same symbol.
items.locator: §1.2, p. 4, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Mathlib's cyclotomicCharacter L p : (L ≃+* L) →* ℤ_[p]ˣ (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/CyclotomicCharacter.lean) applied to L = ℚ̄ is χ_p on G_ℚ = Aut(ℚ̄); restriction to G_F is precomposition. Continuity is not part of the definition there.

items.name: Notation 1.2: the Teichmüller character ω_p and the level-2 fundamental character ω_{p,2}
items.statement: ω_p is the Teichmüller lift of the mod p cyclotomic character χ̄_p; ω_{p,2} is a fundamental character of level 2 of I_p (valued in 𝔽_{p²}^×, factoring through the quotient of I_p isomorphic to 𝔽_{p²}^×), and the same symbols denote their Teichmüller lifts and all their ℓ-adic incarnations ι_ℓ ι_p^{−1}(ω_p), ι_ℓ ι_p^{−1}(ω_{p,2}).
items.locator: §1.2, p. 4, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R01.2 plans tame and fundamental characters of levels one and two; node FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.5/tame-inertia-characters. Ingredients in the library: tauceti:TauCeti.teichmuller (Teichmüller section 𝓀[K]ˣ →* 𝒪[K]ˣ of a local field) and mathlib:modularCyclotomicCharacter, but no declaration of ω_p or ω_{p,2} as a Galois character.

items.name: Notation 1.2: modular p-adic representations over a totally real field
items.statement: Let F be totally real. ρ : G_F → GL₂(𝒪), 𝒪 the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p, is modular if it is isomorphic to (an integral model of) ρ_π for a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL₂(𝔸_F) that is discrete series at infinity of parallel weight (k, …, k), k ≥ 2.
items.locator: §1.2, p. 4, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: ρ_π is AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.2 (node R19.2/hilbert-modular-compatible-system-carayol-theorem-A); 'modular' is the conclusion of GL2ModularityLifting:R22.5/kw-odd-prime-lifting and R22.6/kw-dyadic-lifting.

items.name: External [61] (Taylor; Carayol, Wiles, Blasius–Rogawski): Galois representations of Hilbert modular forms
items.statement: For F totally real and π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(𝔸_F) that is discrete series at infinity of parallel weight k ≥ 2, there is an associated 2-dimensional p-adic representation ρ_π of G_F (compatible with π at unramified places).
items.locator: §1.2, p. 4 (cites [61]), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node R19.2/hilbert-modular-compatible-system-carayol-theorem-A is Carayol's Theorem (A), which assumes a discrete-series finite place when [F:ℚ] is even; the stage R19.2 description requires the parity and auxiliary-place cases (Taylor [61]) to be handled explicitly.

items.name: Notation 1.2: ordinary local component π_v
items.statement: For v | p, the local component π_v of π is ordinary if L(π_v, s) = 1/((1 − α_v q^{−s})(1 − β_v q^{−s})), q the cardinality of the residue field at v, with one of ι_p(α_v), ι_p(β_v) ∈ ℚ̄_p a unit.
items.locator: §1.2, pp. 4–5, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Nodes AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.5/hilbert-local-behaviour-at-p and OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.2/nearly-ordinary-representations.

items.name: §1.2 (external, Wiles): ordinary π_v gives ordinary ρ_π|_{D_v}
items.statement: If π_v (v | p) is ordinary, then ρ_π|_{D_v} is ordinary in the sense of Definition 3.4.
items.locator: §1.2, p. 5, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R19.5/hilbert-local-behaviour-at-p (i) (π_v unramified and ordinary ⇒ ρ_π|_{I_v} ≅ (χ_p^{k−1} ∗; 0 1)) and R19.2/wiles-ordinary-hilbert-representation.

items.name: §1.2: modular compatible systems
items.statement: A compatible system of 2-dimensional representations of G_F is modular if one member of the system is modular; then all members are also modular.
items.locator: §1.2, p. 5, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/compatible-system-predicates defines 'automorphic' for a system via Frobenius polynomials, which is the 'all members' form; the passage from one modular member is not separately stated.

items.name: §1.2: modular residual representations over F
items.statement: ρ̄ : G_F → GL₂(𝔽) (𝔽 finite of characteristic p) is modular if either it is irreducible and isomorphic to the reduction modulo the maximal ideal of 𝒪 of (an integral model of) some ρ_π as above, or it is reducible and totally odd (det ρ̄(c) = −1 for all complex conjugations c ∈ G_F).
items.locator: §1.2, p. 5, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.5/kw-residual-modularity (conditions (α), (β) over totally real F) and AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.6/s-type-arises-from-and-modular (over ℚ). The convention that reducible totally odd ρ̄ count as modular is not stated in any node.

items.name: §1.2: Ad(ρ̄) and Ad⁰(ρ̄)
items.statement: Ad(ρ̄) = M₂(𝔽) with G_F acting through ρ̄ composed with the conjugation action of GL₂(𝔽); Ad⁰(ρ̄) ⊂ Ad(ρ̄) is the subspace of trace-zero matrices.
items.locator: §1.2, p. 5, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.1/tangent-spaces (ad ρ̄, and ad⁰ for fixed determinant) and LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.1/local-fixed-determinant.

items.name: §1.2: normalisation of local class field theory
items.statement: For a local field F, the isomorphism F^× ≃ W_F^{ab} of local class field theory is normalised so that a uniformiser is sent to an arithmetic Frobenius; characters of W_F and of F^× are identified through it.
items.locator: §1.2, p. 5, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Layer 6 proves localArtinMap(π_K) = arithmeticFrobenius; Layer 7 gives the absolute map; Layer 9 the Weil group.

items.name: External: global class field theory
items.statement: For a number field F there is an isomorphism 𝔸_F^×/F^×(F_∞^×)⁰ ≃ G_F^{ab}, compatible with the local isomorphisms of local class field theory.
items.locator: §1.2, p. 5, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 11 (global class formation and global Artin reciprocity).

items.name: §1.2: arithmetic characters ψ and ρ_ψ
items.statement: For 𝒪 the integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p, an arithmetic character is ψ : 𝔸_F^×/F^×(F_∞^×)⁰ → 𝒪^× such that for some open compact U ⊂ (𝔸_F^∞)^× and integer t, ψ(u) = N(u_p)^t for u ∈ U (u_p the projection to the places above p, N the product of local norms). It gives a Galois character ρ_ψ : G_F → 𝒪^× of the form εχ_p^{−t} with ε of finite order. When F^×(F_∞^×) ⊂ ker ψ, ψ is viewed as ψ : F^×\(𝔸_F^∞)^× → 𝒪^× and ρ_ψ is totally even. For F′/F finite, ψ ∘ N_{F′/F} is denoted ψ or ψ_{F′}.
items.locator: §1.2, p. 5, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.0/galois-character-of-an-algebraic-hecke-character (the ℓ-adic character of an algebraic Hecke character; note it normalises Art_F to geometric Frobenius, opposite to KW).

items.name: §2.1: the category CNL_𝒪
items.statement: CNL_𝒪 is the category of complete Noetherian local 𝒪-algebras A with a fixed isomorphism of the residue field with 𝔽, with local 𝒪-algebra homomorphisms as morphisms; m_A denotes the maximal ideal.
items.locator: §2.1, p. 5, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1/complete-local-coefficient-category (Ĉ_Λ).

items.name: §2.1: functors of points Sp_A (Yoneda)
items.statement: For A ∈ CNL_𝒪 let Sp_A(B) = Hom_{CNL_𝒪}(A, B); A → 𝔽 gives the unique point ξ_{A,𝔽} ∈ Sp_A(𝔽). A ↦ Sp_A is a contravariant equivalence of CNL_𝒪 onto the full subcategory of representable functors CNL_𝒪 → Sets; A(X) denotes the algebra representing X, and X has a property P (e.g. X → Y smooth) if A(X) (resp. A(Y) → A(X), formally smooth) has it.
items.locator: §2.1, p. 6, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: General Yoneda: coyoneda : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ (C ⥤ Type) is fully faithful, hence an anti-equivalence onto corepresentable functors. The category CNL_𝒪 itself is planned (R03.1).

items.name: §2.1: tangent and cotangent spaces t_A, t_A^*
items.statement: For A ∈ CNL_𝒪, t_A := Sp_A(𝔽[ε]) (ε² = 0), naturally in bijection with Hom_𝔽(m_A/(m_A² + πA), 𝔽), an 𝔽-vector space (zero = ξ_{A,𝔽} composed with 𝔽 → 𝔽[ε]), identified with the 𝒪-derivations A → 𝔽; t_A^* := Hom_𝔽(t_A, 𝔽) is the cotangent space.
items.locator: §2.1, p. 6, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R03.2/schlessinger-conditions-and-tangent-spaces: T F = Der_Λ(S, k), dual of the relative cotangent space. Mathlib has IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace (m/m², absolute), not the relative version.

items.name: §2.1: finite tangent spaces and presentations by power series
items.statement: For A ∈ CNL_𝒪, t_A and t_A^* are finite-dimensional. If x_i ∈ m_A are finitely many elements whose images generate t_A^*, then (x_i) topologically generates A as an 𝒪-algebra and A is the quotient of 𝒪[[X_i]] by the morphism X_i ↦ x_i.
items.locator: §2.1, p. 6, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R03.1/complete-local-coefficient-category: a map in Ĉ_Λ is surjective iff it is surjective on relative cotangent spaces; dim Der_Λ(S, k) < ∞.

items.name: §2.1: relative tangent and cotangent spaces
items.statement: For f : A → B in CNL_𝒪, f induces t(f) : t_B → t_A and t^*(f) : t_A^* → t_B^*; the relative tangent space t_{B/A} is ker t(f) and the relative cotangent space is coker t^*(f); t_{B/A} identifies with the A-derivations of B with values in 𝔽.
items.locator: §2.1, p. 6, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Elementary. R03.1/R03.2 give only the absolute tangent space Der_Λ(S, k); no node states the relative version over A.

items.name: §2.1: completed tensor products in CNL_𝒪
items.statement: For A → B₁, A → B₂ in CNL_𝒪, C := B₁ ⊗̂_A B₂ is a CNL_𝒪-algebra (its quotient by m_{B₁} ⊗ B₂ + B₁ ⊗ m_{B₂} is 𝔽, it is local and complete, and a quotient of 𝒪[[X₁, …, X_{d₁+d₂}]], d_i = dim_𝔽 t_{B_i}), and for D ∈ CNL_𝒪, Sp_C(D) = Sp_{B₁}(D) ×_{Sp_A(D)} Sp_{B₂}(D).
items.locator: §2.1, p. 6, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R03.1/complete-local-coefficient-category: pushouts in Ĉ_Λ are the m-adic completion of S₁ ⊗_R S₂, Noetherian complete local with residue field k.

items.name: §2.1: tangent space of a completed tensor product
items.statement: With C = B₁ ⊗̂_A B₂, an A-derivation of C into 𝔽 is the same as a pair of A-derivations of B₁ and B₂ (d_C(b₁ ⊗ b₂) = b₂d_{B₁}(b₁) + b₁d_{B₂}(b₂)); hence t_{C/A} ≅ t_{B₁/A} ⊕ t_{B₂/A}.
items.locator: §2.1, p. 6, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Elementary consequence of the fibre-product description; not stated in R03.1, which plans only the pushout construction.

items.name: §2.1: closed immersions
items.statement: A morphism f : B → C of CNL_𝒪-algebras is a closed immersion if it is surjective. f is a closed immersion if and only if Sp_C(A) → Sp_B(A) is injective for every CNL_𝒪-algebra A (for the converse it suffices to take A = 𝔽[ε]).
items.locator: §2.1, p. 6, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R03.1/complete-local-coefficient-category: 'if Der_Λ(S, k) → Der_Λ(R, k) is injective then R → S is surjective'. The printed proof says 'surjectivity' where injectivity is meant (sourceIssues E1; atlas GlobalGaloisDeformations/E2).

items.name: §2.2: Mazur's p-finiteness condition
items.statement: A profinite group G satisfies the p-finiteness property (1.1 of [45]) if for every open subgroup G₀ ⊂ G there are only finitely many continuous homomorphisms G₀ → ℤ/pℤ.
items.locator: §2.2, p. 7, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.2/phi-p-condition.

items.name: §2.2: lifts (framed deformations) and the functor D^□
items.statement: For G profinite with the p-finiteness property, d ≥ 1 and ρ̄ : G → GL_d(𝔽) continuous, a lift of ρ̄ with values in A ∈ CNL_𝒪 is a continuous ρ : G → GL_d(A) reducing to ρ̄; D^□(A) is the set of lifts (also called framed deformations).
items.locator: §2.2, p. 7, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.1/lifting-functor.

items.name: §2.2 (Grothendieck, 18 of [45]): the universal lifting ring R^□
items.statement: D^□ is represented by a CNL_𝒪-algebra R^□ with universal lift ρ^□_univ : G → GL_d(R^□). Its relative tangent space is the space of 1-cocycles Z¹(G, Ad), Ad the adjoint representation of ρ̄, and the matrix entries of ρ^□_univ(g), g ∈ G, topologically generate R^□ over 𝒪.
items.locator: §2.2, p. 7, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.2/universal-lifting-ring, R04.2/universal-continuous-lift, R04.1/tangent-spaces. Topological generation by matrix entries is not stated for R^□ (only for R_𝒟 in OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.3/matrix-entry-subring).

items.name: §2.2: deformations and the functor D
items.statement: A deformation of ρ̄ to A is an equivalence class of lifts, two lifts being equivalent if conjugate by an element of GL_d(A)¹ = ker(GL_d(A) → GL_d(𝔽)); D(A) is the set of deformations, identified with the set of orbits of GL_d(A)¹ on D^□(A), and D^□ → D is the natural morphism.
items.locator: §2.2, p. 7, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.1/strict-deformation-functor.

items.name: §2.2 (Mazur): the hull of D
items.statement: D has a hull, unique up to isomorphism: a CNL_𝒪-algebra R with a versal deformation ρ_vers : G → GL_d(R) such that Sp_R → D is smooth, every deformation ρ ∈ D(A) is the pushforward of ρ_vers along some ξ ∈ Sp_R(A), and Sp_R(𝔽[ε]) → D(𝔽[ε]) is bijective (R is universal for lifts to dual numbers); t_R ≅ H¹(G, Ad).
items.locator: §2.2, p. 7, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R04.2/universal-deformation-ring ('without the Schur hypothesis Def_ρ̄ has a hull'), R03.2/versal-minimal-versal-objects-and-hulls, R04.1/tangent-spaces. The printed source of ρ_vers is G_F (sourceIssues E2).

items.name: Proposition 2.1: framed rings are formally smooth over the hull
items.statement: Let ξ ∈ Sp_R(R^□) be a point given by versality applied to ρ^□_univ, and f_ξ : D^□ → Sp_R the induced morphism (compatible with D^□ → D). Then f_ξ is smooth and ξ : R → R^□ is formally smooth of relative dimension d² − dim H⁰(G, Ad).
items.locator: §2.2, Proposition 2.1, p. 7, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.2/framed-unframed-comparison and LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.1/local-forget-framing plan only the Schur case (R_ρ̄ representable, n² − 1 variables). The general hull statement would follow from R03.2/versal-minimal-versal-objects-and-hulls (versal = minimal versal ⊗ power series) and R04.1/tangent-spaces, but no node states it. KW say §2.2 is not used in their modularity proof; §3.2.3–3.2.4 use only its Schur case.

items.name: §2.2: deformation conditions, framed version
items.statement: For a deformation condition X (18 of [45]), the subfunctor D_X ⊂ D is relatively representable and D^□_X := D^□ ×_D D_X is represented by a quotient R^□_X of R^□.
items.locator: §2.2, p. 8, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3/local-deformation-problem and R04.3/deformation-problem-ideal (deformation problems ↔ Γ̂_n-invariant ideals of R^□).

items.name: §2.2: deformation conditions, comparison with the hull
items.statement: Sp_{R,X} := Sp_R ×_D D_X is represented by a quotient R_X of the hull R, and R_X → R^□_X is formally smooth of relative dimension d² − dim H⁰(G, Ad).
items.locator: §2.2, p. 8, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Depends on Proposition 2.1 in the non-Schur case, which is not planned (see that item).

items.name: Proposition 2.2(i), first part: points of flat CNL_𝒪-algebras
items.statement: Let R be a flat CNL_𝒪-algebra. Then there is a finite extension E′ of E such that R has a point with values in the ring of integers 𝒪′ of E′.
items.locator: §2.3, Proposition 2.2(i), p. 9, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Stated as a proof step of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/local-nonemptiness ('A nonzero flat complete local Noetherian 𝒪-algebra has an 𝒪′-point (KW II Proposition 2.2(i))'). The finite-algebra step of the proof (R′/Q finite over 𝒪 of dimension 1) is DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.4/characteristic-zero-points-from-finiteness-and-dimension.

items.name: Proposition 2.2(i), second part: maximal ideals of R[1/p]
items.statement: Let R be a flat CNL_𝒪-algebra. Every maximal ideal of R[1/p] is the image of the generic point of a local morphism Spec(𝒪′) → Spec(R) over Spec(𝒪), 𝒪′ the ring of integers of a finite extension of E.
items.locator: §2.3, Proposition 2.2(i), p. 9, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Not stated in any node; R03.4 plans characteristic-zero points only for finite 𝒪-algebras of positive dimension. Needed for Corollary 2.3.

items.name: Proposition 2.2(ii): completed tensor products of flat domains with regular generic fibre
items.statement: Let I be a finite set and R_i (i ∈ I) CNL_𝒪-algebras which have a point with values in 𝒪, are domains (hence flat over 𝒪), and have R_i[1/p] regular. Then the completed tensor product ⊗̂_{i∈I} R_i has the same properties.
items.locator: §2.3, Proposition 2.2(ii), p. 9, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Missing: no node states it. It is consumed, not stated, by LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-completed-tensor-product and GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/kw-deformation-data, which assign it to DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3. But R03.1 plans only when completed tensor products 'remain Noetherian and local'. It is routed to R03.1 on route 1 (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/7); R03.1 precedes R08.6.

items.name: External (Chevalley; Zariski–Samuel VIII §5 Thm 13 Cor. 5): comparison of ideal topologies
items.statement: For a complete Noetherian local domain R_i with a prime P_i = ker(ξ_i : R_i → 𝒪), the P_i-adic topology on R_i coincides with the topology defined by the ideals P̃_i^n := P_i^n[1/p] ∩ R_i.
items.locator: §2.3, proof of Proposition 2.2(ii), p. 9 (cites [69]), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R03.1/complete-local-coefficient-category includes Stacks Lemma 90.4.7 (decreasing J_n ⊃ m^n define the adic topology on R/J), which needs J_n ⊃ m^n and does not cover symbolic powers. Not in Mathlib.

items.name: External (Matsumura [41] 33.B, with 24.B): descent of regularity along faithfully flat local maps
items.statement: A Noetherian local ring is regular if it admits a faithfully flat local homomorphism to a regular local ring. (In §2.8 it is applied to the local ring of R_X[1/p] at ℘ and the local ring of the completion at a prime ℘̂ above ℘, which exists by 24.B. The completion half of the former item is /342.)
items.locator: §2.8 proof of Proposition 2.12, p. 17, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Missing. General descent of regularity along flat local maps (Matsumura 23.7, 33.B) is planned nowhere. Tau Ceti ModularCurves Layer 4D plans descent only 'along the finite faithfully flat covers occurring in KM's Notes Added in Proof', and Mathlib has IsRegularLocalRing (Mathlib/RingTheory/RegularLocalRing/Defs.lean) without flat descent. The completion half, which Layer 4D does plan, is split off as /342 (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/10). Route 1.

items.name: Corollary 2.3: flat reduced quotients are determined by their points
items.statement: Let R be a CNL_𝒪-algebra and R′ a quotient of R which is flat and reduced, with kernel I. Then I is the intersection of the kernels of the local 𝒪-algebra morphisms R → 𝒪′ (𝒪′ rings of integers of finite extensions of E) which factor through R′.
items.locator: §2.3, Corollary 2.3, pp. 9–10, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Invoked (not stated) in the proof step of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/kw-local-conditions and the hypotheses of GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/factorization-through-local-conditions; no node states the general lemma.

items.name: External (EGA IV₃ Cor. 10.5.8): R′[1/p] is a Jacobson ring
items.statement: If R′ is Noetherian and p lies in its Jacobson radical, then R′[1/p] is a Jacobson ring.
items.locator: §2.3, proof of Corollary 2.3, p. 10, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Mathlib has IsJacobsonRing and isJacobsonRing_localization for localizations of Jacobson rings, but a local ring is not Jacobson; the EGA statement is not in the library or the atlas.

items.name: Definition 2.4: quotients classifying a set of points
items.statement: Let R be a CNL_𝒪-algebra and X a set of local 𝒪-algebra morphisms R → 𝒪′, 𝒪′ running through the rings of integers of finite extensions of Frac 𝒪. A flat and reduced quotient R′ = R/I classifies the morphisms in X if the set of local 𝒪-algebra morphisms R′ → 𝒪′ is identified with X; then (Corollary 2.3) I is the intersection of the kernels of the elements of X.
items.locator: §2.3, Definition 2.4, p. 10, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Used as the defining property in LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/kw-local-conditions and GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/factorization-through-local-conditions.

items.name: §2.4: group functors, actions and free actions on CNL_𝒪
items.statement: A group structure on a functor G representable by A(G) is a group structure on each G(A), functorial in A, given by morphisms A(G) → A(G) ⊗̂_𝒪 A(G), A(G) → A(G), A(G) → 𝒪 with the usual compatibilities; actions on a representable X are defined similarly. The action is free if G × X → X × X, (g, x) ↦ (x, gx), is a closed immersion, i.e. for every A, G(A) acts on X(A) without fixed points.
items.locator: §2.4, p. 10, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/free-action-quotient.

items.name: §2.4: the orbit functor O and invariant functions A(X)⁰
items.statement: O is the functor A ↦ G(A)\X(A). A(X)⁰ ⊂ A(X) is the subalgebra of a with γ(a) = 1 ⊗ a, γ : A(X) → A(G) ⊗̂_𝒪 A(X) the coaction; equivalently a(gx) = a(x) for all A, g ∈ G(A), x ∈ X(A).
items.locator: §2.4, p. 10, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/free-action-quotient.

items.name: §2.4: tangent maps of a group action
items.statement: The product G × G → G induces addition t_G ⊕ t_G → t_G (with t_G = G(𝔽[ε])). The action G × X → X induces t_G ⊕ t_X → t_X, (l, x) ↦ o(l) + x, where o : t_G → t_X is l ↦ l·ξ_{X,𝔽[ε]}. If the action is free, o is injective, giving t_G ↪ t_X, and t_X/t_G is the largest quotient of t_X on which t_G acts trivially.
items.locator: §2.4, pp. 10–11, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R04.4/free-action-quotient states t_O = t_X/t_G; the injectivity of t_G → t_X is implicit there.

items.name: Proposition 2.5(a): representability of the orbit functor
items.statement: Let a smooth representable group G act freely on a representable X in CNL_𝒪. Then A(X)⁰ is a CNL_𝒪-algebra and represents the orbit functor O, and the tangent space t_O is naturally isomorphic to t_X/t_G, t_X → t_O being the quotient map.
items.locator: §2.4, Proposition 2.5, p. 11, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/free-action-quotient; Schlessinger's criterion from R03.2.

items.name: Proposition 2.5(b): X is a trivial torsor over the orbit space
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of 2.5(a), X → O is smooth; with G_O = O × G, the map G_O ×_O X → X makes X a torsor over O with group G_O (G_O ×_O X → X ×_O X is an isomorphism); this torsor is trivial and X ≅ O × G.
items.locator: §2.4, Proposition 2.5, p. 11, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/free-action-quotient ('X ≅ O × G as a trivial G-torsor over O').

items.name: External (Schlessinger [55], Thm 2.11 and Lemma 2.10): pro-representability criterion
items.statement: A functor F on Artinian CNL_𝒪-algebras with F(𝔽) a point is pro-representable if F(B₁ ×_A B₂) → F(B₁) ×_{F(A)} F(B₂) is bijective whenever B₁ → A is surjective, and the 𝔽-vector space F(𝔽[ε]) (whose structure comes from the first condition) is finite-dimensional.
items.locator: §2.4, proof of Proposition 2.5, p. 11, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.2/rim-schlessinger-condition-and-prorepresentability and R03.2/schlessinger-conditions-and-tangent-spaces.

items.name: §2.5: diagonalizable groups (a)^* in CNL_𝒪
items.statement: For a finitely generated abelian group a whose torsion has p-power order, the diagonalizable group (a)^* in CNL_𝒪 is the completion of the diagonalizable group scheme with character group a ([15] exp. VIII) at the neutral element of its special fibre. For an action of (a)^* on a representable X, A(X)⁰ is the algebra of functions constant on orbits.
items.locator: §2.5, p. 12, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/diagonalizable-groups.

items.name: Proposition 2.6(1): quotients by free diagonalizable actions
items.statement: Let X be representable in CNL_𝒪 and D = (a)^* a diagonalizable group acting freely on X. Then a quotient D\X exists in CNL_𝒪 (X → D\X is universal for D-morphisms X → Y with D acting trivially on Y), X → D\X makes X a torsor under D_{D\X}, and the affine algebra of D\X is A(X)⁰.
items.locator: §2.5, Proposition 2.6, p. 12, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/free-action-quotient (its hypotheses record that KW call the general case 'dévissage de routine').

items.name: Proposition 2.6(2): quotients in stages
items.statement: If a → a′ is surjective, so D′ = (a′)^* is a closed subgroup of D = (a)^*, then D′\X has a natural free action of D/D′ and D\X is naturally isomorphic to the quotient of D′\X by D/D′.
items.locator: §2.5, Proposition 2.6, p. 12, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/free-action-quotient ('for a ↠ a′ the quotient can be taken in stages').

items.name: External (SGA 3 [15], Exp. VIII, Thm 5.1): quotients by free actions of finite diagonalizable groups
items.statement: If a finite diagonalizable group scheme acts freely on an affine scheme, the fppf quotient exists, is affine with ring of invariants as its algebra, and the quotient map is a torsor.
items.locator: §2.5, proof of Proposition 2.6, p. 13, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Requested by GlobalGaloisDeformations (request to Tau Ceti ModularCurves 0C, 'affine free-action quotient').

items.name: §2.6: truncations
items.statement: For m ≥ 1, CNL_𝒪^{[m]} is the full subcategory of A ∈ CNL_𝒪 with m_A^m = 0 (these are Artinian); A^{[m]} := A/m_A^m. Sp_A and Sp_{A^{[m]}} agree on CNL_𝒪^{[m]}; if A represents X, X^{[m]} is the functor represented by A^{[m]}. If X = X^{[m]}, every map X → Y factors through Y^{[m]}. For A₁, A₂ ∈ CNL_𝒪^{[m]}, Sp_{A₁} × Sp_{A₂} restricted to CNL_𝒪^{[m]} is represented by (A₁ ⊗̂_𝒪 A₂)^{[m]}.
items.locator: §2.6, p. 13, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/truncated-actions.

items.name: §2.6: closed immersions and truncations
items.statement: A map X → Y is a closed immersion iff X^{[m]} → Y^{[m]} is one for all m, iff X^{[m]} → Y^{[m]} is one for some m ≥ 2; equivalently A(Y) → A(X) is surjective iff A(Y)^{[m]} → A(X)^{[m]} is surjective for some m ≥ 2.
items.locator: §2.6, p. 13, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Follows from R03.1/complete-local-coefficient-category (surjectivity is detected on m/m²); not stated in truncated form.

items.name: §2.6: group chunks and group action chunks of level m
items.statement: A group chunk of level m is a CNL_𝒪^{[m]}-algebra A(G) with maps (G × G)^{[m]} → G, g ↦ g^{−1} and a neutral element in G(𝒪^{[m]}) satisfying the group-scheme diagrams; it defines a group functor on CNL_𝒪^{[m]}. A group action chunk of G on a representable X of level m is a map (G × X)^{[m]} → X with the usual compatibilities; it is free if (G × X)^{[m]} → (X × X)^{[m]}, (g, x) ↦ (gx, x), is a closed immersion. A representable group in CNL_𝒪 (and an action) gives group (action) chunks G^{[m]} by reduction.
items.locator: §2.6, p. 13, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/truncated-actions.

items.name: §2.6: actions are determined by their truncations
items.statement: For a group G acting on X (representable in CNL_𝒪), the truncated actions of all levels m determine G, X and the action (A(G), A(X) are the projective limits of A(G^{[m]}), A(X^{[m]})), and the action is free iff all the truncated action chunks are free.
items.locator: §2.6, p. 13, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Implicit in GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/truncated-actions.

items.name: Proposition 2.7: actions from compatible action chunks
items.statement: Let G be a representable group in CNL_𝒪; for each m let A_m be a CNL_𝒪^{[m]}-algebra with π_m : A_{m+1} → A_m, X_m = Sp_{A_m}, with a CNL_𝒪-algebra C and compatible surjections C → A_m; let A_∞ = lim A_m (a CNL_𝒪-algebra), X_∞ = Sp_{A_∞}, with the natural immersions X_m → X_∞^{[m]}. Given for each m a group action chunk of level m of G^{[m]} on X_m, compatible with G^{[m]} → G^{[m+1]} and X_m → X_{m+1}, there is a unique action of G on X_∞ whose level-m chunk on X_∞^{[m]} is compatible with the given chunk on X_m; if the chunks are free, so is the action.
items.locator: §2.6, Proposition 2.7, p. 14, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/truncated-actions.

items.name: Proposition 2.8: truncations of the torus and its p^m-torsion
items.statement: Let T = (ℤ^t)^* be the split torus of dimension t, m ≥ 0, and T_{p^m} = ((ℤ/p^mℤ)^t)^* ↪ T. Then this closed immersion induces an isomorphism of truncated group schemes T_{p^m}^{[m+1]} ≃ T^{[m+1]} (because (1 + X)^{p^m} − 1 ∈ (p, X)^{m+1}).
items.locator: §2.6, Proposition 2.8, p. 14, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/diagonalizable-groups.

items.name: §2.7: the scheme of inertia-rigid data M_φ, M_{φ,0}, M_{φ,0,fl} and R^□_{φ,0,fl}
items.statement: Let G be profinite with a finite normal subgroup I such that G/I ≅ ℤ̂, F ∈ G mapping to a generator of G/I, ρ̄ : G → GL_d(𝔽) continuous, ρ₀ : G → GL_d(𝒪) a fixed lift and φ = det ρ₀. M_φ is the affine 𝒪-scheme of finite type whose A-points are pairs (ρ_I : I → GL_d(A) a homomorphism, f ∈ GL_d(A)) with int(f)(ρ_I(τ)) = ρ_I(int(F)(τ)) for τ ∈ I, det ρ_I = φ|_I and det f = φ(F); (ρ_I(τ))_τ, f embeds M_φ as a closed subscheme of GL_d^{|I|+1}. M_{φ,0} ⊂ M_φ is cut out by P_{ρ_I(τ)} = P_{ρ₀(τ)} (characteristic polynomials) for all τ ∈ I, with algebra A_{φ,0}; M_{φ,0,fl} has algebra A_{φ,0}/(p-torsion); R^□_{φ,0,fl} is the completion of A_{φ,0,fl} at the maximal ideal of the point ξ_ρ̄, a faithfully flat local 𝒪-algebra with residue field 𝔽 (an object of CNL_𝒪). The tautological DATA extends to a lift ρ_X : G → GL_d(R^□_{φ,0,fl}) of ρ̄.
items.locator: §2.7, pp. 14–16, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/inertia-rigid-deformations.

items.name: Lemma 2.9: ξ_ρ̄ lies on the flat part
items.statement: The point ξ_ρ̄ of M_{φ,0} defined by ρ̄ is a point of M_{φ,0,fl}.
items.locator: §2.7, Lemma 2.9, p. 15, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/inertia-rigid-deformations.

items.name: Proposition 2.10: structure of R^□_{φ,0,fl}
items.statement: Each irreducible component of Spec(R^□_{φ,0,fl}) is faithfully flat over 𝒪 of absolute dimension d², and R^□_{φ,0,fl}[1/p] is regular.
items.locator: §2.7, Proposition 2.10, p. 15, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/inertia-rigid-deformations. The proof first shows M_{φ,0}[1/p] is smooth over E of dimension d² − 1 (a torsor under C₁^* over M_I ≅ GL_d/C^*, C the commutant of ρ₀|_I), then uses excellence (see the external item) and equidimensionality.

items.name: Proposition 2.11: points of R^□_{φ,0,fl}
items.statement: For 𝒪′ the integers of a finite extension E′ of E and ξ : R^□_{φ,0,fl} → 𝒪′ local, let ρ_ξ be ρ_X composed with GL_d(R^□_{φ,0,fl}) → GL_d(𝒪′). The lifts ρ_ξ are exactly the lifts ρ of ρ̄ with values in GL_d(𝒪′) which have determinant φ and whose restriction ρ ⊗ E′ to I is conjugate to (ρ₀)|_I ⊗ E′.
items.locator: §2.7, Proposition 2.11, p. 16, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/inertia-rigid-deformations.

items.name: §2.7 Remark: R^□_{φ,0,fl} as a quotient of R^□
items.statement: By Corollary 2.3 and Proposition 2.11, R^□_{φ,0,fl} is the quotient of the universal lifting ring R^□ of ρ̄ classifying (Definition 2.4) the lifts with determinant φ whose restriction to I is conjugate over E′ to ρ₀|_I.
items.locator: §2.7, Remark after Proposition 2.11, p. 16, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/inertia-rigid-deformations ('So it is the quotient of R^□ classifying these lifts').

items.name: External: characters determine representations of finite groups in characteristic 0
items.statement: For a finite group I and a field E′ of characteristic 0, two finite-dimensional representations of I over E′ with the same character are isomorphic.
items.locator: §2.7, proof of Proposition 2.11, p. 16, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTable/Determined.lean: [Field k] [Group G] [Finite G] [CharZero k], finite-dimensional V, W, equal characters ⇒ Nonempty (ρ.Equiv σ). Read and matches.

items.name: External (Grothendieck; Matsumura [41] §34 and Thm 79, [42] Thm 31.6): excellence and equidimensionality
items.statement: A finitely generated 𝒪-algebra is excellent, so the completion morphism at a maximal ideal is regular (regularity of the generic fibre passes to the completion); if all irreducible components of a local ring essentially of finite type over 𝒪 have the same dimension, its completion is equidimensional.
items.locator: §2.7, proof of Proposition 2.10, p. 15, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Missing. GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/inertia-rigid-deformations requests it from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3 in its hypotheses. But R03.3's text plans only to 'State hypotheses on catenarity and excellence', and no node proves that finitely generated 𝒪-algebras are excellent, or that the completion of an equidimensional local ring essentially of finite type is equidimensional. It is routed to R03.3 on route 1 (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/7).

items.name: §2.8: smooth resolutions of framed deformation conditions
items.statement: Let G, ρ̄, R^□ be as in §2.2 and R^□_X a nontrivial quotient of R^□ by an ideal stable under the conjugation action of (GL_d)₁, defining D^□_X. A smooth resolution of D^□_X is a flat 𝒪-scheme ℛ with an 𝒪-morphism f : ℛ → Spec(R^□_X) such that (1) f is proper with injective O_{Spec R^□_X} → f_*(O_ℛ) (hence f surjective); (2) ℛ[1/p] → Spec(R^□)[1/p] is a closed immersion; (3) the inverse image 𝒴 ⊂ ℛ of the closed point of Spec(R^□_X) is geometrically connected; (4) ℛ → Spec(𝒪) has a smooth algebraization: an 𝒪-scheme ℛ₀ smooth of finite type, a closed subscheme 𝒴₀ ⊂ ℛ₀ and an 𝒪-morphism ℛ → ℛ₀ sending 𝒴 to 𝒴₀ and inducing an isomorphism of the formal completions of ℛ along 𝒴 and ℛ₀ along 𝒴₀.
items.locator: §2.8, p. 16, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/smooth-resolution-criterion.

items.name: §2.8 Remark: scheme-theoretic closure and generic fibre
items.statement: Property (1) implies Spec(R^□_X) is the scheme-theoretic closure of ℛ in Spec(R^□) and Spec(R^□_X[1/p]) that of ℛ[1/p] in Spec(R^□[1/p]); with (2), f induces an isomorphism ℛ[1/p] ≅ Spec(R^□_X[1/p]); as ℛ is flat over 𝒪, R^□_X is flat over 𝒪.
items.locator: §2.8, Remark, pp. 16–17, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof step of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/smooth-resolution-criterion.

items.name: Proposition 2.12(a): R^□_X is a domain
items.statement: If D^□_X has a smooth resolution ℛ, then R^□_X is a domain.
items.locator: §2.8, Proposition 2.12, p. 17, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/smooth-resolution-criterion.

items.name: Proposition 2.12(b): relative dimension
items.statement: If D^□_X has a smooth resolution ℛ, the relative dimension of R^□_X over 𝒪 equals the relative dimension of ℛ over 𝒪.
items.locator: §2.8, Proposition 2.12, p. 17, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/smooth-resolution-criterion.

items.name: Proposition 2.12(c): regular generic fibre
items.statement: If D^□_X has a smooth resolution ℛ, then R^□_X[1/p] is regular.
items.locator: §2.8, Proposition 2.12, p. 17, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/smooth-resolution-criterion.

items.name: Proposition 2.12(d): points via the resolution
items.statement: Let 𝒪̄ be the ring of integers of an algebraic closure of E and ℛ(𝒪̄)_c the 𝒪̄-points of ℛ sending the closed point of Spec 𝒪̄ into 𝒴. Then the set D^□_X(𝒪̄) of framed deformations of ρ̄ with values in 𝒪̄ satisfying X is the image of ℛ(𝒪̄)_c in D^□(𝒪̄).
items.locator: §2.8, Proposition 2.12, p. 17, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/smooth-resolution-criterion.

items.name: External (EGA III): Stein factorization and the theorem on formal functions
items.statement: A proper morphism f : ℛ → Spec(R) factors as ℛ → Spec Γ(ℛ, O_ℛ) → Spec(R) with Γ(ℛ, O_ℛ) finite over R; for R complete local, Γ(ℛ, O_ℛ) is the ring of global sections of the completion of ℛ along the fibre over the closed point.
items.locator: §2.8, proof of Proposition 2.12, p. 17, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Named as inputs from AdicSpacesPartII F0 (formal functions) in the hypotheses of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/smooth-resolution-criterion; the F0 stage text plans formal functions but does not mention Stein factorization.

items.name: §3: the local deformation rings R̄_v^{□,ψ}
items.statement: For a local field F_v (finite over ℚ_q), D_v = Gal(ℚ̄_q/F_v), ρ̄_v : D_v → GL₂(𝔽) and a fixed determinant φ = ψχ_p, R̄_v^{□,ψ} is the quotient of the fixed-determinant framed deformation ring R_v^{□,ψ} which classifies, in the sense of Definition 2.4, the lifts satisfying the prescribed condition X_v (odd; low weight crystalline; weight 2; semistable weight 2; inertia-rigid; twist of semistable), so that local morphisms R̄_v^{□,ψ} → 𝒪′ correspond to lifts satisfying X_v.
items.locator: §3 opening, p. 18, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/kw-local-conditions.

items.name: Theorem 3.1, case v = ∞
items.statement: (Hypotheses of Theorem 3.1.) For v = ∞ and odd deformations, R̄_v^{□,ψ} is a domain, flat over 𝒪 of relative dimension 2, and R̄_v^{□,ψ}[1/p] is regular.
items.locator: §3, Theorem 3.1, p. 18, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-archimedean; R08.1/archimedean-rings-p-odd and R08.1/archimedean-odd-ring-p2.

items.name: Theorem 3.1, case v | p
items.statement: Assume F_v/ℚ_p unramified and F_v = ℚ_p if ρ̄_v is irreducible. For low weight crystalline deformations, semistable weight 2 deformations, and weight 2 deformations crystalline over ℚ_p^{nr}(µ_p), R̄_v^{□,ψ} is a domain, flat over 𝒪 of relative dimension 3 + [F_v : ℚ_p], and R̄_v^{□,ψ}[1/p] is regular.
items.locator: §3, Theorem 3.1, p. 18, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-fontaine-laffaille-irreducible, export-weight-two-irreducible, export-ordinary, export-semistable-weight-two-at-p, export-endpoint-weight.

items.name: Theorem 3.1, case v ∤ p semistable
items.statement: For v a finite place not above p and semistable deformations (§3.3.4), R̄_v^{□,ψ} is a domain, flat over 𝒪, of relative dimension 3, and R̄_v^{□,ψ}[1/p] is regular.
items.locator: §3, Theorem 3.1, p. 18, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-away-from-p (a).

items.name: Theorem 3.1, case v ∤ p inertia-rigid
items.statement: For v a finite place not above p and inertia-rigid deformations (§3.3.1–3.3.3, with F_v = ℚ_q in case 3.3.3), R̄_v^{□,ψ} is flat over 𝒪, each component has relative dimension 3, and R̄_v^{□,ψ}[1/p] is regular.
items.locator: §3, Theorem 3.1, p. 19, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-away-from-p (b), via GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/inertia-rigid-deformations with d = 2.

items.name: Theorem 3.1, consequence: local nonemptiness
items.statement: In each case of Theorem 3.1, by Proposition 2.2, R̄_v^{□,ψ} has points with values in the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p.
items.locator: §3, after Theorem 3.1, p. 19, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/local-nonemptiness.

items.name: Proposition 3.2(i): the completed tensor product of the local rings
items.statement: Suppose each X_v (v ∈ S) is one of the conditions of Theorem 3.1. After possibly replacing 𝒪 by the ring of integers of a finite extension of E, R̄^{□,loc,ψ} := ⊗̂_{v∈S} R̄_v^{□,ψ} is flat over 𝒪, each of its components has relative dimension 3|S|, and R̄^{□,loc,ψ}[1/p] is regular.
items.locator: §3, Proposition 3.2(i), p. 19, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-completed-tensor-product; GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/kw-deformation-data. The count 3|S| uses F totally real with all infinite places and places above p in S. The printed proof cites Proposition 2.2, which needs domains (sourceIssues E10).

items.name: Proposition 3.2(ii): domain when all finite places away from p are semistable
items.statement: If moreover for the finite places in S not above p the deformation problem is of semistable type, then R̄^{□,loc,ψ} is also a domain.
items.locator: §3, Proposition 3.2(ii), p. 19, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-completed-tensor-product.

items.name: Proposition 3.3(a): the odd archimedean ring exists
items.statement: Let D_∞ = Gal(ℂ/ℝ), c complex conjugation, ρ̄_∞ : D_∞ → GL₂(𝔽) odd (det ρ̄(c) = −1). There is a flat and reduced CNL_𝒪-algebra R_∞^{□,ψ} classifying (Definition 2.4) the odd lifts of ρ̄_∞ (lifts ρ with ρ(c) of characteristic polynomial X² − 1); it is the completion of the ring of the affine scheme of 2 × 2 matrices with characteristic polynomial X² − 1 at the point ρ̄_∞(c).
items.locator: §3.1, Proposition 3.3, p. 20, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-archimedean, R08.1/archimedean-odd-ring-p2; GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6/dyadic-oddness (oddness at p = 2 is a condition on the lift).

items.name: Proposition 3.3(b): formally smooth case
items.statement: If ρ̄(c) ≠ id (always the case if p ≠ 2), R_∞^{□,ψ} is formally smooth over 𝒪 of relative dimension 2.
items.locator: §3.1, Proposition 3.3, p. 20, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-archimedean; R08.1/archimedean-rings-p-odd.

items.name: Proposition 3.3(c): the case p = 2, ρ̄(c) = id
items.statement: If p = 2 and ρ̄(c) = id, R_∞^{□,ψ} is a domain, (faithfully) flat over 𝒪 of relative dimension 2, with regular generic fibre.
items.locator: §3.1, Proposition 3.3, p. 20, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-archimedean and R08.6/smooth-resolution-criterion (acceptance: the resolution by pairs (M, L)).

items.name: §3.1: the resolution by pairs (M, L) at p = 2
items.statement: For p = 2, M₂ is the 𝒪-scheme of automorphisms of V with square id and M(X² − 1) ⊂ M₂ those of characteristic polynomial X² − 1 (the quadric X₁₁² + X₁₂X₂₁ = 1, integral). ℛ₀ ⊂ M(X² − 1) ×_𝒪 ℙ¹_𝒪 represents pairs (M, L), L ⊂ V with V/L locally free of rank 1, M(L) = L and M|_L = id. The first projection is projective, an isomorphism over the locus M ≠ id (which contains the generic fibre), contracts {id} × ℙ¹ in the special fibre; the second projection makes ℛ₀ a torsor over ℙ¹ under Hom(V/L, L), so ℛ₀ is smooth over 𝒪 of relative dimension 2; the base change ℛ to Spec R_∞^{□,ψ} is a smooth resolution in the sense of §2.8 when ρ̄(c) = id.
items.locator: §3.1, proof of Proposition 3.3, pp. 20–21, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof step of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-archimedean and acceptance item of R08.6/smooth-resolution-criterion. The printed flatness claim refers to M₂ instead of M(X² − 1) (sourceIssues E6).

items.name: §3.1 Remark: the dyadic odd ring at ρ̄(c) = id
items.statement: If p = 2 and ρ̄(c) = Id, R_∞^{□,ψ} ≅ 𝒪[[X₁, X₂, X₃]]/(X₁² + X₂X₃ + 2X₁); in particular it is a relative complete intersection.
items.locator: §3.1, Remark after Proposition 3.3, p. 21, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-archimedean; R08.1/archimedean-odd-ring-p2.

items.name: Definition 3.4(1): representations of weight k
items.statement: Let E, F be finite extensions of ℚ_p and V a 2-dimensional continuous representation of G_F with coefficients in E. V is of weight k if for all embeddings ι : E ↪ ℂ_p, V ⊗_{E,ι} ℂ_p ≅ ℂ_p ⊕ ℂ_p(k − 1) as G_F-modules.
items.locator: §3.2.1, Definition 3.4, p. 22, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/hodge-tate-weight-convention ('Khare–Wintenberger's weight k means Hodge–Tate weights {k−1, 0}'); recorded in the hypotheses of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/kw-local-conditions.

items.name: Definition 3.4(2): ordinary representations over CNL_𝒪-algebras
items.statement: Let F/ℚ_p be finite and V a continuous representation of G_F on a free rank 2 module over a CNL_𝒪-algebra R. V is ordinary if there is a free rank one G_F-stable submodule W ⊂ V such that V/W is free of rank one over R with trivial action of the inertia I_F, and an open subgroup of I_F acts on W by χ_p^a for some integer a ≥ 0.
items.locator: §3.2.1, Definition 3.4, p. 22, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Recorded in the hypotheses of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/kw-local-conditions; PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/ordinary-representation is the field-coefficient (Perrin-Riou) notion, not KW's CNL_𝒪 version.

items.name: Lemma 3.5(i), first part: low crystalline weight and ordinarity
items.statement: Let F be an unramified extension of ℚ_p, V a 2-dimensional vector space over a p-adic field E and ρ : G_F → Aut(V) a continuous representation lifting ρ̄. If V is crystalline of weight k with 2 ≤ k ≤ p, then V is ordinary if residually it is ordinary.
items.locator: §3.2.1, Lemma 3.5(i), p. 22, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Owner: PadicHodgeTheory R06.4, whose text asks to 'State separately p=2 and modular weights p and p+1 … Include the ordinary and crystalline criteria actually invoked in those branches'. R06.4/two-dimensional-ordinarity-criterion proves the criteria for F = ℚ_p only, and no node states them for unramified F ≠ ℚ_p. Lemma 3.5(i), first part, (ii) and (iii) (/83, /85, /86) take one status and one route (route 3) (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/7). Consumers: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/kw-local-conditions (acceptance: 'A lift that is crystalline of weight k but not ordinary with ρ̄_v ordinary does not occur for 2 ≤ k ≤ p (KW II Lemma 3.5)') and the hypotheses of R08.6/export-ordinary. The printed proof (via Fontaine–Laffaille, strongly divisible lattices and the unit-root summand [46]) has a duplicated sentence (sourceIssues E7).

items.name: Lemma 3.5(i), second part (Berger–Li–Zhu [3]): weight up to p + 1 over ℚ_p
items.statement: With F = ℚ_p: if V is crystalline of weight k with 2 ≤ k ≤ p + 1, then V is ordinary if residually it is ordinary.
items.locator: §3.2.1, Lemma 3.5(i), p. 22 (cites [3]); used in §3.2.7, p. 31, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.5/crystalline-reducible-reduction-is-ordinary (2 ≤ k ≤ p + 1, reducible semisimplified reduction ⇒ ordinary, via R21.5/blz-reduction-theorem); PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/weight-p-plus-one-branch.

items.name: Lemma 3.5(ii): semistable non-crystalline weight 2 is ordinary
items.statement: Let F be an unramified extension of ℚ_p and ρ : G_F → Aut(V) lifting ρ̄ as in Lemma 3.5. If V is semistable non-crystalline of weight 2, then V is ordinary.
items.locator: §3.2.1, Lemma 3.5(ii), p. 22, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Owner: PadicHodgeTheory R06.4, whose text asks to 'State separately p=2 and modular weights p and p+1 … Include the ordinary and crystalline criteria actually invoked in those branches'. R06.4/two-dimensional-ordinarity-criterion proves the criteria for F = ℚ_p only, and no node states them for unramified F ≠ ℚ_p. Lemma 3.5(i), first part, (ii) and (iii) (/83, /85, /86) take one status and one route (route 3) (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/7). R06.4/two-dimensional-ordinarity-criterion (c) is the case F = ℚ_p. KW need unramified F ≠ ℚ_p in §3.2.2(i) (k(ρ̄_v) = p + 1) and §3.2.6, and call it 'an easy exercise on filtered Dieudonné modules'. Consumer: LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.6.

items.name: Lemma 3.5(iii) (Conrad–Diamond–Taylor [13], Lemma 2.1.2): weight 2 crystalline over ℚ_p^{nr}(µ_p)
items.statement: Let F be an unramified extension of ℚ_p and ρ : G_F → Aut(V) lifting ρ̄ as in Lemma 3.5. If V is of weight 2 and crystalline over ℚ_p^{nr}(µ_p), then V is ordinary if residually it is ordinary.
items.locator: §3.2.1, Lemma 3.5(iii), p. 22 (cites [13]), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Owner: PadicHodgeTheory R06.4, whose text asks to 'State separately p=2 and modular weights p and p+1 … Include the ordinary and crystalline criteria actually invoked in those branches'. R06.4/two-dimensional-ordinarity-criterion proves the criteria for F = ℚ_p only, and no node states them for unramified F ≠ ℚ_p. Lemma 3.5(i), first part, (ii) and (iii) (/83, /85, /86) take one status and one route (route 3) (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/7). Consumers: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-ordinary, which states the resulting shape (χ₁η₁ ∗; 0 η₂) of every weight-two lift and names [13] Lemma 2.1.2 as input, and ClassicalSerreModularity:R26.4/local-reducibility-ordinary, which covers F = ℚ_p only.

items.name: External (Fontaine–Laffaille [26]): filtered Dieudonné modules and strongly divisible lattices
items.statement: For F/ℚ_p unramified and crystalline representations with Hodge–Tate weights in [0, p − 1], there is a filtered Dieudonné module D(V) with strongly divisible lattices M, and a functor M ↦ V(M) (exact, fully faithful in the appropriate range) between Fontaine–Laffaille modules and lattices/torsion Galois representations; in particular (0.9 of [26]) the structure of Fil^{p−1}.
items.locator: §3.2.1 proof of Lemma 3.5, p. 22; §3.2.2(ii)(a), p. 23; §3.2.3, p. 24, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3/fl-filtered-modules, fl-functor-torsion, strongly-divisible-lattices; PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/weight-p-endpoint-branch (endpoint k = p).

items.name: §3.2.2(i): weight 2 deformations at v | p
items.statement: Setting: ρ̄_v : D_v → GL₂(𝔽) with F_v/ℚ_p finite unramified if ρ̄_v is reducible and F_v = ℚ_p if ρ̄_v is irreducible (and F_v = ℚ_p if k(ρ̄_v) = p + 1 for crystalline deformations); if p ≠ 2, 2 ≤ k(ρ̄_v) ≤ p + 1 (for reducible ρ̄_v and F_v ≠ ℚ_p this means (ρ̄_v)|_{I_v} is ordinary with det a power of the cyclotomic character). For p ≠ 2 the weight 2 lifts ρ_v are potentially semistable of weight 2 with fixed determinant φ = ψχ_p and inertial Weil–Deligne parameter (ω_p^{k(ρ̄)−2} ⊕ 1, 0) if k(ρ̄_v) ≠ p + 1, and (id, N) with N a nonzero nilpotent matrix if k(ρ̄_v) = p + 1. For p = 2 they are crystalline of weight 2 (equivalently Barsotti–Tate with det(ρ_v)|_{I_v} = χ_p) if k(ρ̄_v) = 2, and semistable of weight 2 if k(ρ̄_v) = 4, with fixed determinant of the form ψχ₂. ψ is required to satisfy (χ_pψ)|_{I_v} = det(ρ_v|_{I_v}).
items.locator: §3.2.2(i), pp. 22–23, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/kw-local-conditions (p). The general potentially semistable rings of fixed type are R08.3/pst-deformation-ring, but KW only need the flat reduced quotient of Definition 2.4.

items.name: §3.2.2(ii): low weight crystalline deformations at v | p
items.statement: Assume k(ρ̄_v) = 2 if p = 2 (if k(ρ̄_v) = p + 1 then ρ̄_v|_{I_v} ≅ (χ_p ∗; 0 1)). The lifts ρ_v have determinant φ = ψχ_p and are (a) crystalline of weight k(ρ̄_v) if k(ρ̄_v) ≤ p (Fontaine–Laffaille lifts), (b) with ρ_v|_{I_v} ≅ (χ_p^p ∗; 0 1) if k(ρ̄_v) = p + 1. If ρ̄_v is unramified (so k(ρ̄) = p) and ρ̄_v = η̄₁ ⊕ η̄₂ with η̄₁ ≠ η̄₂ unramified, one of the characters is chosen and only lifts whose unramified quotient reduces to it are considered.
items.locator: §3.2.2(ii), p. 23, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/kw-local-conditions (including the acceptance item on the choice of character).

items.name: §3.2.2: shape of the weight 2 lifts; reducible ρ̄_v gives ordinary lifts
items.statement: By Lemma 3.5, if ρ̄_v|_{I_v} ≅ (χ_p^{k−1} ∗; 0 1) with 2 ≤ k ≤ p + 1, a weight 2 lift ρ_v is of the form (ω_p^{k−2}χ_p ∗; 0 1) (on inertia), with the further condition that ρ_v is crystalline of weight 2 when ρ̄_v is finite flat (k = 2); whenever ρ̄_v is reducible the lifts considered are ordinary.
items.locator: §3.2.2, pp. 23–24, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-ordinary ('Every lift of this type is (χ₁η₁ ∗; 0 η₂) ... χ₁ = χ_p^{k−1} or χ_pω^{k−2}'). The printed parenthesis 'which can occur only when k = 2' is false for unramified ρ̄_v (sourceIssues E8).

items.name: §3.2.3: irreducible ρ̄_p, low weight crystalline lifts
items.statement: Let ρ̄_p : G_{ℚ_p} → GL₂(𝔽) be irreducible of weight k ≤ p and consider lifts crystalline of weight k with fixed determinant. The (fixed-determinant) deformation ring is smooth over 𝒪 of dimension 1 (including k = p and p = 2): the filtered Dieudonné module has a basis v₁, v₂ with v₂ generating Fil^{k−1} and φ-matrix (λ p^{k−1}; α 0), α a unit determined by the determinant and λ any element of the maximal ideal. The framed deformation ring is smooth over 𝒪 of dimension 4 (a PGL₂-torsor completion over the deformation ring, End(ρ̄_p) = 𝔽).
items.locator: §3.2.3, p. 24, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-fontaine-laffaille-irreducible states the item as written, including k = p and p = 2. But its only inputs are L7 and R08.1/local-forget-framing, and they cover less. L7/fontaine-laffaille-deformation-condition has Fil^{l−1}M = 0, i.e. Hodge–Tate weights in [0, p − 2]; general smoothness is L7/fontaine-laffaille-tangent-space-and-smoothness (Ramakrishna [49], Diamond–Flach–Guo [20], CHT). So L7 covers k ≤ p − 1 for odd p only. For k = p the weights {0, p − 1} lie in the range of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3/fl-full-faithfulness, which is fully faithful on MF′, and irreducibility of ρ̄_p keeps every deformation in MF′. For p = 2 (k = 2) R07.3's safe interval is [0, 0]; the weight-one objects go to FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.4 and to the 2-adic Barsotti–Tate rings of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.5. The paper gives no argument for these two cases (p. 24: 'There the case k(ρ̄p) = p and the case p = 2 is excluded, but as ρ̄p is irreducible the argument extends'). The item stays planned at R08.6, whose node states it; the node's missing inputs are a note for the maintainer (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/6). For odd p and k(ρ̄_p) = 2 this is also the weight-two ring (/92, sourceIssues E33).

items.name: External (Savitt [54], Thm 6.22(3) and Thm 6.24): weight-two rings for irreducible ρ̄_p
items.statement: For p ≠ 2 and ρ̄_p irreducible with 3 ≤ k(ρ̄_p) ≤ p (hypothesis added, sourceIssues E33), provided 𝒪 is sufficiently big, the quotient R̄_v^ψ of the fixed-determinant universal deformation ring by the intersection of the kernels of 𝒪′-points of the required weight-two type (inertial parameter (ω_p^{k−2} ⊕ 1, 0)) is isomorphic to 𝒪[[T₁, T₂]]/(T₁T₂ − p), and every 𝒪′-point of R̄_v^ψ is of the required type.
items.locator: §3.2.4, p. 24 (cites [54]), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.4/savitt-weight-two-rings (𝒪_E⟦X₁, X₂⟧/(X₁X₂ − pw), w a unit, in the irreducible case). Savitt's irreducible case needs a principal-series type ω̃^i ⊕ ω̃^j with i ≢ j mod p − 1. KW's type (ω_p^{k(ρ̄)−2} ⊕ 1, 0) has i = k(ρ̄_p) − 2 and j = 0, so the paper's statement holds exactly when 3 ≤ k(ρ̄_p) ≤ p (for irreducible ρ̄_p and odd p, k(ρ̄_p) ≤ p). When k(ρ̄_p) = 2 (e.g. ρ̄_p|I_p ≅ ω₂ ⊕ ω₂^p) the type is trivial and the lifts are crystalline of weight 2. The ring is then the formally smooth ring 𝒪[[T]] of §3.2.3 (/91), not 𝒪[[T₁, T₂]]/(T₁T₂ − p) (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/5).

items.name: §3.2.4: framed weight-two ring for irreducible ρ̄_p
items.statement: For p ≠ 2 and ρ̄_v irreducible (F_v = ℚ_p) with 3 ≤ k(ρ̄_v) ≤ p (hypothesis added, sourceIssues E33), the framed weight-2 deformation ring R̄_v^{□,ψ} is isomorphic to 𝒪[[T₁, T₂, T₃, T₄, T₅]]/(T₁T₂ − p) (by the obvious case of Proposition 2.1).
items.locator: §3.2.4, p. 24, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-weight-two-irreducible, which states the unrestricted form. For k(ρ̄_v) = 2 the framed weight-two ring is the formally smooth ring 𝒪[[T₁, …, T₄]] of §3.2.3 (/91); see /92 and sourceIssues E33 (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/5).

items.name: Proposition 3.6(a): ordinary rings of low weight or weight 2
items.statement: Let F_v/ℚ_p be unramified and ρ̄_v ordinary with k(ρ̄_v) ≤ p. There are flat and reduced CNL_𝒪-algebras R_v^{□,ψ} classifying the weight 2 and the low-weight crystalline framed deformations of §3.2.2; R_v^{□,ψ} is a domain of relative dimension 3 + [F_v : ℚ_p] with regular generic fibre.
items.locator: §3.2.5, Proposition 3.6, pp. 24–25, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-ordinary. When ρ̄_v is unramified with D_v acting by homotheties on the semisimplification the proof builds a smooth resolution (§2.8), whose algebraization uses Lemma 3.8.

items.name: Proposition 3.6(b): formally smooth cases
items.statement: In the setting of Proposition 3.6, if ρ̄_v is ramified, or ρ̄_v ≅ η₁ ⊕ η₂ with η₁ ≠ η₂ unramified characters, then R_v^{□,ψ} is formally smooth over 𝒪 (of relative dimension 3 + [F_v : ℚ_p]).
items.locator: §3.2.5, Proposition 3.6, p. 25; proof pp. 28–29, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-ordinary (proof step: 'the stable line is unique and the resolution is an isomorphism').

items.name: §3.2.5: the character space A = 𝒪[[T]] and Ξ
items.statement: Write φ = χ₁η with χ₁ a character of the cyclotomic Galois group (χ₁ = χ_p^{k(ρ̄)−1} in the crystalline case, χ_pω_p^{k(ρ̄)−2} in the weight 2 case) and η unramified; ρ̄_v ≅ (χ̄₁η̄₁ ∗; 0 η̄₂), and lifts considered are (χ₁η₁ ∗; 0 η₂) with η₁, η₂ unramified lifting η̄₁, η̄₂, η₁η₂ = η. A = 𝒪[[T]], η_T : D_v → (1 + T𝒪[[T]])^× the unramified character through the ℤ_p-unramified extension with Frobenius ↦ 1 + T, η₁ = [η̄₁]η_T (universal character η₁χ₁ with fixed inertial restriction χ₁), η₂ = η/η₁, and Ξ := χ₁η₁η₂^{−1}.
items.locator: §3.2.5, proof of Proposition 3.6, p. 25, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof step of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-ordinary.

items.name: §3.2.5: finite cocycles Z¹_f
items.statement: For B a CNL_𝒪 A-algebra, N a finitely generated B-module and M = N(Ξ), Z¹(M) is the B-module of continuous 1-cocycles of D_v in M. If k(ρ̄_v) = 2 (so χ₁ = χ_p and Ξ|_{I_v} = χ_p), v_Z : Z¹(M) → H¹(D_v, M) → H¹(I_v, N(χ_p)) ≅ (F^{nr×} ⊗ N)^∧ → N is the composite of restriction, Kummer theory and the completed valuation v ⊗ id (v(p) = 1), and Z¹_f(M) := ker v_Z (finite cocycles); if k(ρ̄_v) > 2, Z¹_f(M) := Z¹(M).
items.locator: §3.2.5, p. 25, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof step of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-ordinary ('Finite cocycles are the kernel of the Kummer valuation map v_Z when k = 2').

items.name: Kummer theory over F^{nr} with 𝒪-module coefficients (§3.2.5, Lemma 3.7)
items.statement: For N a finite 𝒪-module, H¹_cont(I_v, N(χ_p)) ≅ (F^{nr×} ⊗ N)^∧ (m_B-adic completion), F^{nr} the maximal unramified extension of F_v, compatibly with the action of D_v/I_v; as a Galois module F^{nr×} ≅ ℤ × U (U the units, p a Galois-fixed uniformiser), so ((F^{nr×} ⊗ N)(η̃))^{D_v} → (N(η̃))^{D_v} is surjective.
items.locator: §3.2.5, definition of Z¹_f and proof of Lemma 3.7, pp. 25–26, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Missing. Its μ_{p^n} core, the Kummer isomorphism for the field F^{nr} with G_{F^{nr}} = I_v, is /343, planned at Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9. What remains is specific to KW: the passage to the coefficients N(χ_p), N a finitely generated B-module, with the m_B-adic completion; the D_v/I_v-equivariance; and the structure F^{nr×} ≅ ℤ × U used for the surjectivity. It belongs with Lemma 3.7 in LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.6, which owns the deformation-specific calculations (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.5's text: 'the deformation-specific calculations are owned by R08'). So it is routed there (route 2), not to R02.5 (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/10). Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 plans the Kummer isomorphism kummerEquiv_mixed only for finite extensions F/ℚ_p.

items.name: §3.2.5, formula (∗): size of the cocycle group
items.statement: For M = N(Ξ) finite: |Z¹(D_v, M)| = |H¹(D_v, M)|·|M|·|H⁰(D_v, M)|^{−1} = |M|^{1+[F:ℚ_p]}·|H⁰(D_v, M^*)|, with M^* = N^∨(χ_pΞ^{−1}), N^∨ = Hom_𝒪(N, E/𝒪), χ_pΞ^{−1} = χ_pχ₁^{−1}η₁^{−1}η₂.
items.locator: §3.2.5, proof of Lemma 3.7, p. 26, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Used in the proof steps of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-semistable-weight-two-at-p (|Z¹(D_v, N(χ_p))| = |N|^{2+[F_v:ℚ_p]}) and export-ordinary; the dimension form is R08.1/local-tangent-obstruction.

items.name: Lemma 3.7: finite cocycles form a free module
items.statement: The B-module Z¹_f(B(Ξ)) is free of rank 1 + [F_v : ℚ_p]; moreover Z¹_f(N(Ξ)) = Z¹_f(B(Ξ)) ⊗_B N for every finitely generated B-module N.
items.locator: §3.2.5, Lemma 3.7, p. 25, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof step of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-ordinary (and used in R08.6/local-nonemptiness).

items.name: §3.2.5: the affine bundle E_f and the Borel action
items.statement: Z¹_f is the vector bundle over Spec A with sections Z¹_f(A(Ξ)); BA_A is the scheme of bases (u₁, u₂) of A ⊗_𝒪 V, a torsor over ℙ¹_A (via u₁ ↦ line) under the Borel B_A of upper triangular matrices (g·(u₁, u₂) = (α′u₁, β′u₁ + δ′u₂) for g^{−1} = (α′ β′; 0 δ′)). For z and a basis ℬ, ρ_{z,ℬ} has matrix (χ₁η₁ η₂a_z; 0 η₂). B_A acts on Z¹_f by affine automorphisms with ρ_{bz,bℬ} = ρ_{z,ℬ}: for g = (α β; 0 δ), a_{gz} = βδ^{−1}(1 − Ξ) + αδ^{−1}a_z. E_f := (Z¹_f ×_{Spec A} BA_A)/B_A is an affine bundle over ℙ¹_A with representations ρ_e; its vector bundle of translations Z̃¹_f descends from Z¹_f(D_v, Hom(V/L, L)(Ξ)). ℛ₀ ⊂ E_f ×_{Spec 𝒪} Spec(R_v^{□,ψ}) is cut out by ρ_e = ρ_v^{univ}, and ℛ₀ → ℙ¹_A ×_{Spec 𝒪} Spec(R_v^{□,ψ}) is a closed immersion.
items.locator: §3.2.5, proof of Proposition 3.6, pp. 26–28, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof step of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-ordinary ('lines ... form a ℙ¹-type space, over which the lifts form a torsor under Z¹_f'). The formula a_{gz} was checked by direct computation.

items.name: Lemma 3.8: normalising a vector over O[T] ⊂ O[[T]]
items.statement: Let A₀ = 𝒪[T], A = 𝒪[[T]], M₀ a free A₀-module of finite type, M = A ⊗_{A₀} M₀ and m ∈ M. Then there exist m₀ ∈ M₀ and an isomorphism A ⊗_{A₀} M₀ ≃ M sending m₀ to m.
items.locator: §3.2.5, Lemma 3.8, p. 30, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Used only for the smooth algebraization in the proof of Proposition 3.6; not stated in any node (R08.6/export-ordinary asserts the smooth resolution without its algebraization). Its inputs, Weierstrass preparation and division, are in Mathlib (see the next item).

items.name: External: Weierstrass preparation and division over 𝒪[[T]]
items.statement: For A complete local and g ∈ A[[X]] with nonzero image in the residue field, every f ∈ A[[X]] is f = gq + r with r a polynomial of degree < ord(ḡ), and g = u·P with u a unit and P a distinguished polynomial.
items.locator: §3.2.5, proof of Lemma 3.8, p. 30, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/WeierstrassPreparation.lean ([IsLocalRing A] [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal A) A], hypothesis g.map residue ≠ 0). Read and matches.

items.name: §3.2.6: semistable weight 2 deformations at v | p
items.statement: Suppose ρ̄_v ≅ (γ̄_vχ̄_p ∗; 0 γ̄_v) with γ̄_v unramified. The lifts considered are (γ_vχ_p ∗; 0 γ_v), where γ_v is a fixed unramified character of D_v lifting γ̄_v with γ_v²χ_p = φ.
items.locator: §3.2.6, p. 30, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/kw-local-conditions and export-semistable-weight-two-at-p.

items.name: §3.2.6: semistable weight 2 rings, generic case
items.statement: For finite 𝒪-algebras B and finite B-modules N, |Z¹(D_v, N(χ_p))| = |N|^{2+[F:ℚ_p]} (by (∗)). Unless p = 2 and D_v acts by homotheties, the resolution ℛ → Spec(R_v^{□,ψ}) is an isomorphism, ℛ being a torsor over the completion of ℙ¹_𝒪 at the point of the special fibre given by the unique stable line of ρ̄, under the completion of a free module of rank 2 + [F : ℚ_p]; R_v^{□,ψ} is formally smooth over 𝒪 of relative dimension 3 + [F : ℚ_p].
items.locator: §3.2.6, p. 30, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-semistable-weight-two-at-p. The printed text says ℙ¹ over 𝔽 (sourceIssues E12).

items.name: §3.2.6: semistable weight 2 rings, p = 2 with D_v acting by homotheties
items.statement: If p = 2 and D_v acts by homotheties, ℛ is a torsor over the completion of ℙ¹_𝒪 along its special fibre under the completion of a free module of rank 2 + [F : ℚ_p], and by Proposition 2.12 R_v^{□,ψ} is a domain, faithfully flat over 𝒪 of relative dimension 3 + [F : ℚ_p], with regular generic fibre.
items.locator: §3.2.6, p. 30, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-semistable-weight-two-at-p (hypothesis: the dyadic exception belongs to R08.5).

items.name: §3.2.7: crystalline lifts of weight p + 1
items.statement: Let p ≠ 2, k(ρ̄_v) = p + 1 and F_v/ℚ_p unramified; consider ordinary lifts of weight p + 1, i.e. extensions of an unramified free rank one representation by a free rank one representation on which I_v acts by χ_p^p (for F_v = ℚ_p these are all crystalline lifts of weight p + 1, by [3]). The corresponding framed deformation ring R_v^{□,ψ} is formally smooth over 𝒪 of relative dimension 3 + [F_v : ℚ_p], i.e. isomorphic to 𝒪[[T₁, …, T_{3+[F_v:ℚ_p]}]].
items.locator: §3.2.7, pp. 31–32, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-endpoint-weight (proof steps: tangent space via the très ramifiée cocycle forcing η₁ = η₂; obstruction killed by an unramified γ using the nonvanishing cup product with a très ramifiée class, 'by local class field theory').

items.name: §3.2.7 Remark: the stable-line character map is not formally smooth
items.statement: The map Spf(R_v^{□,ψ}) → X = Spf(A) sending ρ to the character of D_v on its stable line is not formally smooth.
items.locator: §3.2.7, Remark, p. 32, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-endpoint-weight (statement and acceptance).

items.name: §3.3: inertia-rigid lifts at v ∤ p
items.statement: Let v ∤ p with residue characteristic q, fix the determinant φ and (after enlarging 𝒪) a lift ρ₀ : D_v → GL₂(𝒪) of ρ̄_v with ρ₀(I_v) finite and determinant φ. Inertia-rigid lifts are the lifts whose restriction to inertia is conjugate to ρ₀|_{I_v} and whose determinant is φ; the corresponding CNL_𝒪-algebra is R^□_{φ,0,fl} of §2.7, which has the properties of Theorem 3.1 by Propositions 2.10 and 2.11.
items.locator: §3.3, p. 32, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-away-from-p (b); GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/inertia-rigid-deformations (applied to D_v/ker(ρ₀|_{I_v})).

items.name: §3.3.1: minimal lifts
items.statement: (Excluding the case where ρ̄_v(I_v) is projectively cyclic of order p, treated in §3.3.4.) Minimal lifts ρ of ρ̄_v are inertia-rigid lifts for the lift ρ₀ constructed in §3.3.1: for p ≠ 2, or p = 2 with non-dihedral projective image of I_v, ρ(I_v) ≅ ρ̄_v(I_v); in all cases det ρ|_{I_v} is the Teichmüller lift of det ρ̄_v|_{I_v} and the conductor of ρ equals the conductor of ρ̄_v (cf. [18] for p ≠ 2).
items.locator: §3.3.1, p. 32, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/kw-local-conditions and export-away-from-p (acceptance: conductor and Teichmüller determinant). Distinct from the CHT notion LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.2/minimally-ramified-condition.

items.name: §3.3.1: the lift ρ₀ when the projective image of inertia has order prime to p
items.statement: If the projective image of I_v has order prime to p, then ρ̄_v(I_v) has order prime to p and there is a lift ρ_I of ρ̄_v|_{I_v} to GL₂(𝒪) with ρ_I(I_v) ≅ ρ̄_v(I_v), unique up to conjugation; choosing g with ρ_I ∘ int(F) = int(g) ∘ ρ_I reducing to ρ̄_v(F) (possible as the centraliser of ρ_I surjects onto that of ρ̄_v|_{I_v}), extending by F ↦ g and twisting by an unramified character gives ρ₀ with determinant φ.
items.locator: §3.3.1, p. 32, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof step of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-away-from-p ('lift ρ̄_v(I_v) isomorphically when its projective image has order prime to p'); lifting of prime-to-p group representations is AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.1/lifting-representations-of-groups-of-order-prime-to-l.

items.name: §3.3.1: classification when the projective image of inertia is non-cyclic of order divisible by p
items.statement: Let G be the projective image of I_v, of order divisible by p and non-cyclic; then the image of wild inertia in G is nontrivial, with nontrivial centre C. If C is cyclic, then p = 2, G is dihedral of order 2d with d odd and q | d, and ρ̄_v ≅ Ind_{G_L}^{D_v}(γ) for a character γ of G_L with values in 𝔽̄₂^×, L/F_v ramified quadratic. If C is non-cyclic, then C has order 4 (projectively {(±1 0; 0 ±1), (0 ±1; ±1 0)}), q = 2, the normaliser of C in PGL₂(𝔽̄_p) is S₄, p = 3 and G ≅ A₄, and the projective image of ρ̄_v lies in S₄.
items.locator: §3.3.1, pp. 32–33, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Referred to in the proof step of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-away-from-p ('use the dihedral or S₄ constructions otherwise (§3.3.1)'); the classification itself is not stated as a node.

items.name: §3.3.1: the lift ρ₀ in the dihedral case (p = 2)
items.statement: With ρ̄_v ≅ Ind_{G_L}^{D_v}(γ) as above, δ a ramified order-2 character of G_L with values in ℚ̄₂^×, ε the character of D_v defined by L and γ̂ the Teichmüller lift, ρ₀′ := Ind(γ̂δ) has det ρ₀′ = ε·(γ̂ ∘ t)·(δ ∘ t) (t the transfer D_v^{ab} → G_L^{ab}), so det(ρ₀′)|_{I_v} = (γ̂ ∘ t)|_{I_v}, the Teichmüller lift of det(ρ̄_v)|_{I_v}; ρ₀ is an unramified twist of ρ₀′ with determinant φ, its restriction to inertia does not depend on δ, and its conductor equals that of ρ̄_v.
items.locator: §3.3.1, p. 33, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof step of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-away-from-p.

items.name: §3.3.1: the lift ρ₀ in the A₄ case (p = 3, q = 2)
items.statement: The normaliser of the projective image of the matrices (±1 0; 0 ±1), (0 ±1; ±1 0) in PGL₂(ℤ₃) is an isomorphic lift of S₄; letting (ρ₀)_proj be the induced lift of the projective representation, since p ≠ 2 there is a unique lift ρ₀ of ρ̄_v with projectivisation (ρ₀)_proj and determinant φ.
items.locator: §3.3.1, p. 33, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof step of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-away-from-p ('S₄ constructions').

items.name: §3.3.2: abelian lifts with fixed inertial character
items.statement: Enlarge 𝔽 to contain the (q − 1)-st roots of unity. Suppose ρ̄_v is upper triangular in the basis e₁, e₂ with ρ̄|_{I_v} ≅ (χ̄ ∗; 0 1), χ̄ from a mod p character of Gal(F_v(µ_q)/F_v), χ its Teichmüller lift (a power of ω_q). Let χ′ = χω_q^{a(q−1)/p^r} (p^r ∥ q − 1) be a nontrivial power of ω_q lifting χ̄ with χ′|_{I_v} = φ|_{I_v}. The lifts considered are those with (ρ ⊗ E)|_{I_v} ≅ 1 ⊕ χ′; in the particular case (χ unramified and ρ̄_v a sum of two distinct unramified characters) one requires in addition ρ|_{I_v} ≅ (χ′ ∗; 0 1) in a basis lifting e₁, e₂.
