These are inertia-rigid lifts (in the particular case, an irreducible component of them); D_v acts through the abelian group Gal(L/F_v), L the compositum of F_v^{nr} and F_v(µ_q).
items.locator: §3.3.2, pp. 33–34, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/kw-local-conditions and export-away-from-p (b).

items.name: §3.3.2: existence of an abelian lift
items.statement: There is a lift of the type of §3.3.2 with values in the ring of integers of a finite extension of E: with σ a generator of inertia of Gal(L/F_v), F the Frobenius of L/F_v(µ_q) and ε = χ′(σ), there are commuting lifts of ρ̄(F), ρ̄(σ) with the lift of ρ̄(σ) of characteristic polynomial (X − 1)(X − ε), and det(F) = φ(F) is achieved by an unramified twist.
items.locator: §3.3.2, p. 34, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof step of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-away-from-p ('In the abelian case with χ′ ≡ χ, use Lemma 3.9 to lift commuting unipotents').

items.name: Lemma 3.9: commuting lifts of two unipotent matrices
items.statement: Let (1 a; 0 1) and (1 a′; 0 1) be matrices with coefficients in 𝔽, and ε ∈ 𝒪^× with ε ≡ 1 mod π, ε ≠ 1. Then, possibly after enlarging 𝒪, there exist lifts of these matrices that commute, the first one having characteristic polynomial (X − 1)(X − ε).
items.locator: §3.3.2, Lemma 3.9, p. 34, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Named in the proof step of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-away-from-p. The proof uses the elementary fact: for lines L₁ ≠ L₂ ⊂ V with v(L₁, L₂) the least v with distinct images in V/π^{v+1}V and g ∈ GL₂(E) with eigenlines L₁, L₂, eigenvalues 1, α (v(α − 1) > 0), g(V) = V iff v(L₁, L₂) ≤ v(α − 1), with reduction id if <, unipotent ≠ id if =; not stated in any node.

items.name: §3.3.3: non-abelian liftings with fixed level-2 inertial character
items.statement: Assume F_v = ℚ_q, p^r | q + 1 for some r > 0, and ρ̄|_{D_q} up to unramified twist ≅ (χ̄_p ∗; 0 1) in the basis e₁, e₂. Enlarge 𝔽 (and 𝒪) to contain the (q² − 1)-st roots of unity. Let χ′ be a character of level 2 of I_q (factoring through 𝔽_{q²}^× but not through 𝔽_q^×) of p-power order. The lifts considered have determinant φ = ψχ_p with φ|_{I_q} = (χ′)^{1+q} and ρ|_{I_q} ≅ (χ′ ∗; 0 χ′^q) in a basis lifting e₁, e₂; since χ′ ≠ χ′^q, (ρ ⊗ E)|_{I_q} ≅ χ′ ⊕ χ′^q and these lifts are inertia-rigid.
items.locator: §3.3.3, p. 35, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/kw-local-conditions and export-away-from-p (b).

items.name: §3.3.3: existence of a level-2 lift, p odd
items.statement: For p ≠ 2 (so χ̄_p(F) = −1 and ε := χ′(σ) satisfies ε^q = ε^{−1}): in a basis with ρ̄_v(F) = (−1 0; 0 1) and ρ̄(σ) = (1 a; 0 1), take ρ(F) = (−1 0; 0 1) and ρ(σ) with eigenlines 𝒪(e₁ + λe₂), 𝒪(e₁ − λe₂) and eigenvalues ε, ε^{−1}, i.e. ρ(σ) = ((ε+ε^{−1})/2, (ε−ε^{−1})/2λ; λ(ε−ε^{−1})/2, (ε+ε^{−1})/2), with 0 < v(λ) < v(ε − ε^{−1}) if a = 0, and v(λ) = v(ε − ε^{−1}), (ε − ε^{−1})/2λ ≡ a mod π if a ≠ 0. Then int(ρ(F))(ρ(σ)) = ρ(σ)^q and ρ lifts ρ̄; an unramified twist gives determinant φ.
items.locator: §3.3.3, pp. 35–36, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof step of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-away-from-p ('explicit ρ(F), ρ(σ) with int(ρ(F))ρ(σ) = ρ(σ)^q'). Matrix entries checked by direct computation.

items.name: §3.3.3: existence of a level-2 lift, p = 2
items.statement: For p = 2 (ε ≠ −1 as χ′ has level 2): take ρ(F) = (−1 z; 0 1) with v(z) > 0 if ρ̄(F) = id, v(z) = 0 if ρ̄(F) is unipotent ≠ id, and v(z) < v(ε² − 1); take ρ(σ) with eigenlines e₁ + λe₂ and ρ(F)(e₁ + λe₂) and eigenvalues ε and ε^{−1} (explicit matrix with entries involving (ε − ε^{−1})/(2 − λz)); choose v(λ) > 0 with 2v(λ) + v(z) < v(ε² − 1) if ρ̄(σ) = id, and 2v(λ) + v(z) = v(ε² − 1) with suitable residue if ρ̄(σ) ≠ id, so that ρ(σ) reduces to ρ̄(σ).
items.locator: §3.3.3, p. 36, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof step of LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-away-from-p. As printed, the eigenvalue ε^{−1} gives int(ρ(F))ρ(σ) = ρ(σ)^{−1}, which equals ρ(σ)^q only if χ′^{q+1} = 1; this fails for every level-2 character of 2-power order when q ≡ 1 mod 4 (sourceIssues E11).

items.name: §3.3.4: twists of semistable deformations at v ∤ p
items.statement: Suppose ρ̄|_{D_v} ≅ (γ̄_vχ̄_p ∗; 0 γ̄_v). The lifts considered are (γ_vχ_p ∗; 0 γ_v) with γ_v a fixed character of D_v lifting γ̄_v whose restriction to I_v is the Teichmüller lift and γ_v²χ_p = φ.
items.locator: §3.3.4, p. 36, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/kw-local-conditions and export-away-from-p (a).

items.name: §3.3.4: rings of twisted semistable lifts
items.statement: As in §3.2.6 but with cocycles forming an 𝒪-module of rank 2: for a finite CNL_𝒪-algebra A, |Z¹(G_{F_v}, A(χ_p))| = |A|·|H⁰(G_{F_v}, A)| = |A|²; hence (formalism of §2.8) R̄_v^{□,ψ} is a domain, flat over 𝒪 of relative dimension 3 with regular generic fibre. If ρ̄_v is ramified, the conductor of such a lift equals the conductor of ρ̄_v.
items.locator: §3.3.4, pp. 36–37, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-away-from-p (a) and its proof step (|Z¹(G, A(χ_p))| = |A|²).

items.name: §4 notation: the restricted-ramification Galois groups G_{F,S}
items.statement: For number fields ℚ ⊂ F ⊂ F′ ⊂ ℚ̄ and a finite set S of places of F, G_{F,S} (resp. G_{F′,S}) is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F (resp. F′) in ℚ̄ unramified outside S (resp. outside the places of F′ above S). For W = S ∪ V as in §4.1.1, G_W := G_{F,W}.
items.locator: §4 (opening paragraph), p. 37, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Node ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.3/restricted-ramification-group ("The Galois group G_{K,S} of the maximal extension unramified outside S"). No declaration in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (searched declarations.tsv for unramified-outside / restricted-ramification names).

items.name: §4 standing hypotheses on F, ρ̄, 𝒪 and the determinant φ = ψχ_p
items.statement: F is a totally real number field; ρ̄ = ρ̄_F : G_F → GL₂(𝔽) = GL(V_𝔽) is absolutely irreducible and totally odd; if p = 2, ρ̄ has non-solvable image; if p > 2, ρ̄|G_{F(μ_p)} is absolutely irreducible. F is unramified at the places above p, and split at p if ρ̄|D_v is irreducible for a place v | p. 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p with residue field 𝔽. φ = ψχ_p : G_F → 𝒪^× is a totally odd character lifting det ρ̄_F (ψ arithmetic in every case considered, §1.2). One considers deformations of ρ̄ to CNL_𝒪-algebras with determinant φ, or with determinant φ fixed only locally at the places of a finite set S. Ad = Ad(ρ̄) = M₂(𝔽) and Ad⁰ = Ad⁰(ρ̄) its trace-zero part, with G_F acting by conjugation through ρ̄.
items.locator: §4 (opening paragraphs), p. 37, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/image-hypotheses states the two residual image hypotheses (cyclotomic absolute irreducibility for p > 2, non-solvable image for p = 2); R04.6/kw-deformation-data states the KW II set-up with ψ and the local rings. The same hypotheses are re-imposed in §5.1 and §5.5.

items.name: §4.1.1: local framed rings R^{□,ψ}_v and their completed tensor product R^{□,loc,ψ}_S
items.statement: Let W = S ⊔ V be a finite set of places of F such that ρ̄ and φ are unramified outside W, S contains all infinite places and all places above p; regard ρ̄ as a representation of G_W = G_{F,W}. For v ∈ S, R^{□,ψ}_v is the CNL_𝒪-algebra representing the functor A ↦ {lifts of ρ̄|D_v to GL₂(A) with determinant ψχ_p}, equivalently pairs (V_A, β_{v,A}) with V_A a deformation of the D_v-representation V_𝔽 to A of determinant ψχ_p and β_{v,A} a lift of the chosen basis of V_𝔽. R^{□,loc,ψ}_S := ⊗̂_{v∈S} R^{□,ψ}_v.
items.locator: §4.1.1, p. 37, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Local framed rings with fixed determinant: LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1 (local lifting rings, including archimedean ones: R08.1/archimedean-rings-p-odd, R08.1/archimedean-odd-ring-p2). The completed tensor product over S is GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3/local-to-global-map (R^loc_{S,T} with T = S).

items.name: §4.1.1: global framed rings R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} (determinant fixed) and R^□_{S∪V} (determinant fixed only on S)
items.statement: R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} (resp. R^□_{S∪V}) is the CNL_𝒪-algebra representing A ↦ isomorphism classes of tuples (V_A, {β_{v,A}}_{v∈S}), where V_A is a deformation of the G_W-representation ρ̄ to A with determinant ψχ_p (resp. such that V_A|D_v has determinant ψχ_p for every v ∈ S), and β_{v,A} (v ∈ S) is a lift of the chosen basis of V_𝔽. Restriction to the D_v makes R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} (resp. R^□_{S∪V}) an R^{□,loc,ψ}_S-algebra.
items.locator: §4.1.1, pp. 37–38, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/determinant-fixed-on-S states both rings (and the R^{□,loc,ψ}_S-algebra structure); R04.3/global-deformation-type and R04.3/global-framed-ring give the S-framed global problem in general.

items.name: §4.1.1: the local-condition quotients R̄^{□,ψ}_v, R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S, R̄^{□,ψ}_{S∪V}, R̄^□_{S∪V}, and their factorisation property
items.statement: For v ∈ S let R̄^{□,ψ}_v be one of the quotients of R^{□,ψ}_v defined in §3, classifying lifts satisfying a prescribed condition X_v; R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S := ⊗̂_{v∈S} R̄^{□,ψ}_v; R̄^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} := R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} ⊗̂_{R^{□,loc,ψ}_S} R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S and R̄^□_{S∪V} := R^□_{S∪V} ⊗̂_{R^{□,loc,ψ}_S} R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S. For a CNL_𝒪-algebra A, a morphism R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} → A factors through R̄^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} if and only if, for every v ∈ S, the corresponding local representation factors through the specialisation R^{□,ψ}_v → R̄^{□,ψ}_v.
items.locator: §4.1.1, p. 38, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R04.4/determinant-fixed-on-S ("R̄ denotes base change to the local-condition quotient R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S") and R04.6/kw-deformation-data (R̄^{□,ψ}_S = R^{□,ψ}_S ⊗̂ R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S). The factorisation criterion is the universal property of the completed pushout; no node states it separately.

items.name: Framed tuples (ρ, (ρ_v), (g_v)) and the ring R̃^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} (proof of Proposition 4.1)
items.statement: Write GL₂(A)₁ = ker(GL₂(A) → GL₂(𝔽)). R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} represents A ↦ equivalence classes of tuples (ρ, (ρ_v)_{v∈S}, (g_v)_{v∈S}) with ρ a lift of ρ̄ (resp. ρ_v a lift of ρ̄|D_v) to GL₂(A) of determinant φ and g_v ∈ GL₂(A)₁ with ρ_v = int(g_v)(ρ|D_v); (ρ, (ρ_v), (g_v)) ~ (int(g)(ρ), (ρ_v), (g_v g^{−1})) for g ∈ GL₂(A)₁. R̃^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} classifies the tuples without the equivalence. Spf(R̃^{□,ψ}_{S∪V}) is an Spf(R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V})-torsor under (GL₂)₁; the action of (GL₂)₁ commutes with the action of (h_v) ∈ ∏_{v∈S}(GL₂)₁ given by (ρ, (ρ_v), (g_v)) ↦ (ρ, int(h_v)(ρ_v), h_v g_v); homotheties embedded diagonally in (GL₂)₁ × ∏_{v∈S}(GL₂)₁ act trivially, and Spf(R̃^{□,ψ}_{S∪V}) is a torsor over Spf(R^ψ_{S∪V}) under ((GL₂)₁ × ∏_{v∈S}(GL₂)₁)/G_m.
items.locator: §4.1.2, proof of Proposition 4.1, p. 38, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R04.3/global-deformation-type (T-framed deformations (ρ, {α_v}) modulo (βρβ^{−1}, {βα_v})) and R04.6/trace-subring-universal-representation (proof step: the tuples form a torsor over the unframed ring under (∏(GL₂)₁)/Ĝ_m). The same tuples are used for the twisting action (§5.1) and in the proof of Lemma 4.6.

items.name: Proposition 4.1: framed rings are power series over the trace subrings
items.statement: Let R̄^ψ_{S∪V} (resp. R̄_{S∪V}) be the subring of R̄^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} (resp. R̄^□_{S∪V}) generated by the traces of the universal deformation; it equals the image of the unframed universal deformation ring R^ψ_{S∪V} (resp. R_{S∪V}) in R̄^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} (resp. R̄^□_{S∪V}). Then Spf(R̄^{□,ψ}_{S∪V}) (resp. Spf(R̄^□_{S∪V})) is a Spf(R̄^ψ_{S∪V})-torsor (resp. Spf(R̄_{S∪V})-torsor) under (∏_{v∈S}(GL₂)₁)/G_m, and R̄^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} (resp. R̄^□_{S∪V}) is a power series ring over R̄^ψ_{S∪V} (resp. R̄_{S∪V}) in 4|S| − 1 variables.
items.locator: §4.1.2, Proposition 4.1, p. 38, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R04.6/trace-subring-universal-representation states exactly this (torsor under (∏_{v∈S}(GL₂)₁)/Ĝ_m, j = 4|S| − 1 variables); the general framed/unframed comparison is R04.2/framed-unframed-comparison and the determinant-only-on-S variant is recorded in R04.4/determinant-fixed-on-S. "Image of R^ψ = subring generated by traces" is Carayol (R04.2/carayol-trace-theorem). The paper proves only the fixed-determinant case ("the other case is similar").

items.name: §4.1.3: flatness, dimension and regularity of R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S
items.statement: Recall (Theorem 3.1) that for v ∈ S the ring R̄^{□,ψ}_v is flat over 𝒪, each of its components has relative dimension over 𝒪 equal to 3 if v ∤ p∞, 3 + [F_v : ℚ_p] if v | p, and 2 if v is infinite, and R̄^{□,ψ}_v[1/p] is regular. Hence (Propositions 2.2 and 3.2) the completed tensor product R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S is flat over 𝒪, each of its components has relative dimension 3|S|, and R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S[1/p] is regular.
items.locator: §4.1.3, p. 39, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-completed-tensor-product and R08.6/local-nonemptiness (KW II Proposition 3.2, Theorem 3.1); GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/kw-deformation-data restates the flat-domain, relative-dimension-3|S| conclusion. The count 3|S| uses that F is totally real (|S_∞| = [F:ℚ]). The middle bullet is misprinted without the bar (see sourceIssues).

items.name: §4.1.4: Galois cohomology with local conditions, dual conditions and dimension notation
items.statement: For a discrete G_F-module M unramified outside the finite set W, H^*(W, M) := H^*(G_{F,W}, M). Given subspaces L_v ⊆ H^*(D_v, M) for v ∈ W, H^*_{{L_v}}(W, M) is the preimage of ∏_{v∈W} L_v under the restriction map H^*(W, M) → ∏_{v∈W} H^*(D_v, M). L_v^⊥ is the annihilator of L_v under the local Tate duality pairing H¹(D_v, Ad⁰) × H¹(D_v, (Ad⁰)^*(1)) → 𝔽 (resp. H¹(D_v, Ad) × H¹(D_v, Ad(1)) → 𝔽). The 𝔽-dimension of a cohomology group is written with h in place of H.
items.locator: §4.1.4, pp. 39–40, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.5/greenberg-wiles-formula defines the Selmer groups H¹_L(F, M), H¹_{L*}(F, M^*) with dual conditions L_v^⊥ (unramified conditions outside a finite set, which is KW's H¹_{{L_v}}(W, M)).

items.name: §4.1.4: the local conditions of Case 1 and Case 2, η-images, and H¹_{S−split}(V, M)
items.statement: Case 1: * = 1, M = Ad⁰; for v ∈ S, L_v is the image of H⁰(D_v, Ad/Ad⁰) in H¹(D_v, Ad⁰) (of 𝔽-dimension 0 or 1, and 1 only possibly when p = 2); for v ∈ V, L_v = H¹(D_v, Ad⁰). Case 2: * = 1, M = Ad; L_v = 0 for v ∈ S and L_v = H¹(D_v, Ad) for v ∈ V. A superscript η denotes the image of Ad⁰-cohomology in Ad-cohomology: H¹(W, Ad⁰)^η := im(H¹(W, Ad⁰) → H¹(W, Ad)) and (H¹_{{L_v}}(W, Ad⁰))^η := im(H¹_{{L_v}}(W, Ad⁰) → H¹(W, Ad)). For M unramified outside W = S ∪ V, H¹_{S−split}(V, M) := H¹_{{L_v}}(G_{F,W}, M) with L_v = 0 (v ∈ S) and L_v = H¹(D_v, M) (v ∈ V); in Case 2 this is H¹_{S−split}(V, Ad).
items.locator: §4.1.4, pp. 39–40, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3/relative-tangent-space works with the framed cone complex (Gee) and records in its acceptance that for p = 2 "the δ₂ corrections of KW II Lemma 4.2 [= final Lemma 4.3] appear"; ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.6 stage text asks for the exact trace-zero module, its dual and determinant-fixed tangent spaces with p = 2 visible. No node states KW's Case 1 condition L_v = im(H⁰(D_v, Ad/Ad⁰) → H¹(D_v, Ad⁰)) verbatim.

items.name: §4.1.4: the dual of Ad⁰ and the adjoint pairings
items.statement: (Ad⁰)^* = Hom_𝔽(Ad⁰, 𝔽) is isomorphic to Ad/Z as a G_F-module, where Z ⊂ M₂(𝔽) is the space of scalar matrices. For p ≠ 2, Ad = Ad⁰ ⊕ Z and Ad/Z ≅ Ad⁰; for p = 2 these need not hold. There are G_F-equivariant perfect pairings Ad⁰ × (Ad⁰)^*(1) → 𝔽(1) and Ad × Ad(1) → 𝔽(1).
items.locator: §4.1.4, p. 39, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.6 stage text: "Record the exact adjoint module: trace-zero endomorphisms, its dual, and determinant-fixed tangent spaces cannot be identified by dividing by 2". No node yet.

items.name: Definition 4.2: δ_p
items.statement: For a prime p, δ_p := 0 if p > 2 and δ_2 := 1.
items.locator: §4.1.4, Definition 4.2, p. 40, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Appears through GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3/relative-tangent-space (acceptance: "the δ₂ corrections of KW II Lemma 4.2 appear"; ESI numbering).

items.name: Lemma 4.3(1): the kernel of Ad⁰-cohomology in Ad-cohomology has dimension δ_p
items.statement: Under the §4 hypotheses (ρ̄ absolutely irreducible), consider the exact sequence 0 → H⁰(W, Ad⁰) → H⁰(W, Ad) → H⁰(W, Ad/Ad⁰) (= 𝔽) → H¹(W, Ad⁰) → H¹(W, Ad). The kernels of the surjections H¹(W, Ad⁰) → H¹(W, Ad⁰)^η and H¹_{{L_v}}(W, Ad⁰) → (H¹_{{L_v}}(W, Ad⁰))^η (Case 1 conditions) have 𝔽-dimension δ_p.
items.locator: §4.1.4, Lemma 4.3(1) and proof, p. 40, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof: H⁰(G_F, Ad) = 𝔽·id = Z, with id ∉ Ad⁰ for p ≠ 2 and id ∈ Ad⁰ for p = 2. For the Selmer version one also needs that the image of 𝔽 = H⁰(W, Ad/Ad⁰) restricts into L_v at v ∈ S, which holds by the definition of the Case 1 condition (not said explicitly). Planned through the δ₂ bookkeeping of R04.3/relative-tangent-space and the R02.6 stage text; no node states the kernel dimension.

items.name: Lemma 4.3(2)(i): vanishing of global invariants for p > 2
items.statement: If p > 2 (so ρ̄|G_{F(μ_p)} is absolutely irreducible), H⁰(G_F, Ad⁰) = H⁰(G_F, (Ad⁰)^*(1)) = 0.
items.locator: §4.1.4, Lemma 4.3(2)(i) and proof, p. 40, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof cites the proof of DDT [14] Corollary 2.43. Only the R02.6 stage text ("global numerical inequalities used in KW II §4") covers it; the term h⁰(G_{F,S}, ad⁰(1)) appears in GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3/relative-tangent-space and global-dimension-lower-bound but its vanishing is not stated in a node.

items.name: Lemma 4.3(2)(ii), first part: the projective image for p = 2
items.statement: If p = 2 (ρ̄ absolutely irreducible with non-solvable image), the projective image proj.im.(ρ̄) is G := SL₂(𝔽_{2^r}) for some r > 1 (by Dickson: PGL₂(𝔽₀) ≅ SL₂(𝔽₀) for a subfield 𝔽₀ ⊂ 𝔽 with |𝔽₀| = 2^r, r > 1).
items.locator: §4.1.4, Lemma 4.3(2)(ii) and proof, pp. 40–41, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement (data/decompositions) states Dickson with its p = 2 refinement; GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/image-hypotheses states "Dickson then makes the projective image SL₂(𝔽_{2^r}) with r > 1".

items.name: Lemma 4.3(2)(ii), second part: invariants of Ad, Ad⁰ and Ad/Z for p = 2
items.statement: If p = 2 and G = proj.im.(ρ̄) ≅ SL₂(𝔽_{2^r}), r > 1, then H⁰(G, Ad) = H⁰(G, Ad⁰) = Z is 1-dimensional over 𝔽, and H⁰(G, Ad/Z) = H⁰(G, (Ad⁰)^*) = 0.
items.locator: §4.1.4, Lemma 4.3(2)(ii) and proof, pp. 40–41, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof: an invariant line in Ad/Z would make the plane P = ⟨id, l⟩ equal to the diagonal matrices for a non-trivial semisimple ρ̄(g), so ρ̄(G_F) would normalise a split torus and be solvable. Only the R02.6 stage text ("p = 2 contributions visible", "trace-zero endomorphisms, its dual") covers it; no node states it. GlobalGaloisDeformations requests the related SL₂(𝔽_{2^r}) facts from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4 (open request).

items.name: Lemma 4.3(3): the global Euler-characteristic ratio |𝔽|^{δ_p}
items.locator: §4.1.4, Lemma 4.3(3), p. 40 (proof p. 41), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Follows from (2). Used in the proof of Proposition 4.5 with Wiles' formula (2). Planned via R02.6 (numerical inequalities of KW II §4) and the δ₂ corrections recorded in R04.3/relative-tangent-space.

items.name: Lemma 4.3(4): H¹(G_F, Z) injects into H¹(G_F, Ad)
items.statement: The map H¹(G_F, Z) → H¹(G_F, Ad) induced by Z ⊂ Ad is injective.
items.locator: §4.1.4, Lemma 4.3(4), p. 40 (proof p. 41), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Clear for p > 2 (Z is a direct summand); for p = 2 it follows from H⁰(G_F, Ad/Z) = 0. Used in Lemma 5.10(g) (t = h¹_{S−split}(Q_n, 𝔽)). Nearest layers: ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.6 (stage text about §4/§5 numerics with p = 2 visible) and GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/dyadic-taylor-wiles-primes, whose proof steps for (f)–(g) use it implicitly; neither states the injection.

items.name: Lemma 4.3(5)(i): H¹(SL₂(𝔽_{2^r}), M₂(𝔽)) = 0 for r > 1 (Dickinson, Lemma 42)
items.statement: For p = 2 and G = proj.im.(ρ̄) ≅ SL₂(𝔽_{2^r}) with r > 1: H¹(G, Ad) = 0. More precisely (Dickinson [21], Lemma 42): for finite fields 𝔽₀ ⊂ 𝔽 with 𝔽₀ = 𝔽_{2^r}, r > 1, H¹(SL₂(𝔽₀), M₂(𝔽)) = 0.
items.locator: §4.1.4, Lemma 4.3(5)(i), p. 40 (proof p. 41), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: External black box (Dickinson, Duke 2001, Lemma 42). GlobalGaloisDeformations requests it from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4 (requests list, status open), but neither the R01.4 stage text nor its Dickson node states it. ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.6/sl2-adjoint-h1-vanishing covers only odd characteristic with #𝔽 ≠ 5 (and End⁰, not M₂).

items.name: Lemma 4.3(5)(ii): the SL₂(𝔽_{2^r})-submodules of Ad
items.statement: For p = 2 and G = proj.im.(ρ̄) ≅ SL₂(𝔽_{2^r}), r > 1, the only G-submodules of Ad are 0, Z, Ad⁰ and Ad (in particular the only non-zero irreducible G-submodule of Ad is Z).
items.locator: §4.1.4, Lemma 4.3(5)(ii), p. 40 (proof p. 41), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof uses that G is perfect, H⁰(G, Ad⁰) = Z and H⁰(G, (Ad⁰)^*) = H⁰(G, Ad/Z) = 0. Requested by GlobalGaloisDeformations from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4 (open request, "the submodule list 0, Z, Ad⁰, Ad"); not stated by any R01.4 node or stage text. Used in Lemma 5.3's Remark and in the proof of Lemma 5.10.

items.name: Lemma 4.4(1): number of generators of R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} over R^{□,loc,ψ}_S
items.statement: The minimal number of generators of R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} (resp. R̄^{□,ψ}_{S∪V}) over R^{□,loc,ψ}_S (resp. R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S) is dim_𝔽 H¹_{{L_v}}(S ∪ V, Ad⁰) − δ_p + Σ_{v∈S} dim_𝔽 H⁰(D_v, Ad) − dim_𝔽 H⁰(G_F, Ad), with the Case 1 conditions L_v.
items.locator: §4.1.5, Lemma 4.4(1) and proof, pp. 41–42, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proved "by arguments as in the proof of Lemma 3.2.2 of [36]" (Kisin): the relative tangent space is computed and the count follows. Planned in GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3/relative-tangent-space (with KW II conventions in its acceptance) and used in R04.5/taylor-wiles-generator-count ("the number of generators as the dimension of the relative tangent space (KW II Lemma 4.4)"). For p = 2 these R04.3 nodes do not apply as written: they are stated for p > 2 in Gee's conventions, with ad⁰ρ̄ and dual module ad⁰ρ̄(1), and frame only finite places. KW II §4 covers p = 2, with the correction δ₂ = 1, the dual (Ad⁰)*(1), where (Ad⁰)* ≅ Ad/Z (p. 39), and framed infinite places. That all-p form is stated by DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.2/presentation-relations-and-dual-selmer-bound ("KW II treats all p"). R04.3's text plans the bounds 'in the form of KW II §4, particularly Proposition 4.5 and Corollary 4.7', so the item stays planned there (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/3).

items.name: Lemma 4.4(2): number of generators of R^□_{S∪V} over R^{□,loc,ψ}_S
items.statement: The minimal number of generators of R^□_{S∪V} (resp. R̄^□_{S∪V}) over R^{□,loc,ψ}_S (resp. R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S) is dim_𝔽 H¹_{S−split}(V, Ad) + Σ_{v∈S} dim_𝔽 H⁰(D_v, Ad) − dim_𝔽 H⁰(G_F, Ad).
items.locator: §4.1.5, Lemma 4.4(2), p. 41, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Stated without proof ("2. is similar"). Planned at its owner, GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.3, whose text plans the tangent and obstruction descriptions and the bound on relations 'in the form of KW II §4'. No node states this count, with the determinant fixed only on S and coefficients Ad. Its consumers are R04.4/determinant-fixed-on-S, which defines the ring R^□_{S∪V}, and R04.5/dyadic-taylor-wiles-primes, whose proof step "(e) follows by Lemma 4.4" uses it for Lemma 5.10(e) at p = 2. They were formerly listed as planning it (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/3).

items.name: Relative tangent space exact sequence (Diamond), proof of Lemma 4.4
items.statement: Let T be the tangent space of R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} relative to R^{□,loc,ψ}_S: deformations V_{𝔽[ε]} of V_𝔽 over 𝔽[ε] with determinant φ, with bases {β_v}_{v∈S} lifting the chosen basis, such that (V_{𝔽[ε]}|D_v, β_v) ≅ V_𝔽 ⊗_𝔽 𝔽[ε] with its induced action and basis for each v ∈ S. The space of such deformations is (H¹_{{L_v}}(W, Ad⁰))^η, of dimension dim_𝔽 H¹_{{L_v}}(S ∪ V, Ad⁰) − δ_p (Lemma 4.3), and there is an exact sequence 0 → H⁰(G_F, Ad) → ∏_{v∈S} H⁰(D_v, Ad) → T → H¹_{{L_v}}(W, Ad⁰)^η → 0.
items.locator: §4.1.5, proof of Lemma 4.4, pp. 41–42, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3/relative-tangent-space (long exact sequence 0 → H⁰_{S,T} → H⁰(G, ad) → ⊕_T H⁰(G_v, ad) → H¹_{S,T} → …). Attributed by KW to F. Diamond.

items.name: Wiles' formula (1) (Greenberg–Wiles; DDT [14] Theorem 2.19)
items.statement: Let M be a finite discrete G_F-module unramified outside W = S ∪ V, with nM = 0 for some n ∈ ℕ, and M^*(1) := Hom(M, μ_n). For subspaces L_v ⊆ H¹(D_v, M) (v ∈ W): |H¹_{{L_v}}(S ∪ V, M)| / |H¹_{{L_v^⊥}}(S ∪ V, M^*(1))| = (|H⁰(G_F, M)| / |H⁰(G_F, M^*(1))|) · ∏_{v∈S} |L_v|/|H⁰(D_v, M)| · ∏_{v∈V} |L_v|/|H⁰(D_v, M)|. (S contains all infinite places; H⁰ at infinite places is ordinary cohomology.)
items.locator: §4.1.6, formula (1), p. 42, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: External black box (DDT Theorem 2.19). ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.5/greenberg-wiles-formula states it in the equivalent all-places form with unramified conditions outside a finite set. Not in Mathlib/Tau Ceti.

items.name: Wiles' formula (2): the Case 1 specialisation
items.locator: §4.1.6, formula (2), p. 42, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Special case of (1). Used in Proposition 4.5 and Proposition 5.5 (GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/taylor-wiles-generator-count cites "Wiles' formula (KW II §4.1.6, (2))").

items.name: Wiles' formula (3): the Case 2 specialisation
items.statement: |H¹_{S−split}(V, Ad)| / |H¹_{V−split}(S, Ad(1))| = (|H⁰(G_F, Ad)| / |H⁰(G_F, Ad(1))|) · ∏_{v∈S} 1/|H⁰(D_v, Ad)| · ∏_{v∈V} |H¹(D_v, Ad)|/|H⁰(D_v, Ad)|.
items.locator: §4.1.6, formula (3), p. 42, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Special case of (1) with Ad^* ≅ Ad via the trace pairing. Used in Lemma 5.10(d); GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/dyadic-taylor-wiles-primes proof step "(d) is Wiles' formula (3)".

items.name: Proposition 4.5: the unframed global ring R̄^ψ_S has absolute dimension ≥ 1
items.statement: Under the §4 hypotheses, with V = ∅ and Ad⁰ coefficients, and the local quotients R̄^{□,ψ}_v (v ∈ S) as in Theorem 3.1: the absolute (Krull) dimension of R̄^ψ_S is ≥ 1.
items.locator: §4.2, Proposition 4.5 and proof, pp. 42–45, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3/global-dimension-lower-bound ("In the setting of KW II … the absolute dimension of R̄^ψ_S is ≥ 1"; stage text names Proposition 4.5 explicitly); DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.2/presentation-relations-and-dual-selmer-bound (data/decompositions). Proof: presentation with g = h¹_{{L_v^⊥}}(S,(Ad⁰)^*(1)) + |S| − 1 variables and at most h¹_{{L_v^⊥}}(S,(Ad⁰)^*(1)) relations (Lemma 4.6) over R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S of dimension 1 + 3|S|, then Proposition 4.1.

items.name: Proof of Proposition 4.5: the variable count g and the presentation of R^{□,ψ}_S
items.statement: With V = ∅, g := dim_𝔽 H¹_{{L_v}}(S, Ad⁰) − δ_p + Σ_{v∈S} dim_𝔽 H⁰(D_v, Ad) − dim_𝔽 H⁰(G_F, Ad) = dim_𝔽 H¹_{{L_v^⊥}}(S, (Ad⁰)^*(1)) − dim_𝔽 H⁰(G_F, Ad) + Σ_{v∈S}(dim_𝔽 H⁰(D_v, Ad) + dim_𝔽 L_v − dim_𝔽 H⁰(D_v, Ad⁰)) (by Wiles' formula (2) and Lemma 4.3(3)). Since 0 → H⁰(D_v, Ad⁰) → H⁰(D_v, Ad) → 𝔽 → L_v → 0 is exact, each summand is 1, so g = dim_𝔽 H¹_{{L_v^⊥}}(S, (Ad⁰)^*(1)) + |S| − 1. By Lemma 4.4 there is a presentation R^{□,ψ}_S ≅ R^{□,loc,ψ}_S[[X_1, …, X_g]]/J inducing an isomorphism of tangent spaces relative to R^{□,loc,ψ}_S; r(J) := dim_𝔽 J/𝔪J, 𝔪 the maximal ideal of R^{□,loc,ψ}_S[[X_1, …, X_g]].
items.locator: §4.2, proof of Proposition 4.5, pp. 42–43, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3/relative-tangent-space (acceptance: "g = h¹_{L^⊥}(S, (ad⁰)^*(1)) + |S| − 1" in KW II conventions) and R04.3/local-to-global-presentation (presentation with g variables). For p = 2 these R04.3 nodes do not apply as written: they are stated for p > 2 in Gee's conventions, with ad⁰ρ̄ and dual module ad⁰ρ̄(1), and frame only finite places. KW II §4 covers p = 2, with the correction δ₂ = 1, the dual (Ad⁰)*(1), where (Ad⁰)* ≅ Ad/Z (p. 39), and framed infinite places. That all-p form is stated by DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.2/presentation-relations-and-dual-selmer-bound ("KW II treats all p"). R04.3's text plans the bounds 'in the form of KW II §4, particularly Proposition 4.5 and Corollary 4.7', so the item stays planned there (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/3).

items.name: The obstruction pairing and the map f : Hom_𝔽(J/𝔪J, 𝔽) → H¹_{{L_v^⊥}}(S, (Ad⁰)^*(1))^* (proof of Lemma 4.6)
items.statement: For u ∈ Hom_𝔽(J/𝔪J, 𝔽), push the extension 0 → J/𝔪J → R^{□,loc,ψ}_S[[X]]/𝔪J → R^{□,ψ}_S → 0 out along u to 0 → I_u → R_u → R^{□,ψ}_S → 0 (I_u² = 0, I_u ≅ 𝔽). With (ρ, (ρ_v), (g_v)) the tautological tuple, the R^{□,loc,ψ}_S-algebra structure of R_u gives lifts ρ̃_v of ρ_v; choose lifts g̃_v of g_v and put ρ̃′_v = int(g̃_v^{−1})(ρ̃_v); choose a set-theoretic lift ρ̃ : G_S → GL(V_{R_u}) of the universal representation with determinant φ. Define the 2-cocycle c(g₁, g₂) = ρ̃(g₁)ρ̃(g₂)ρ̃(g₁g₂)^{−1} − 1 ∈ Ad⁰ and 1-cochains a_v : D_v → Ad⁰ by ρ̃(g) = (1 + a_v(g))ρ̃′_v(g), so c|D_v = δ(a_v). For [x] ∈ H¹_{{L_v^⊥}}(S, (Ad⁰)^*(1)) with representative x, choose a 2-cochain z of G_S with values in 𝒪_S^× with δ(z) = x ∪ c, and set (x, u) := Σ_{v∈S} inv((x_v ∪ a_v) + z_v) ∈ 𝔽_p, where ∪ is cup product followed by (Ad⁰)^*(1) × Ad⁰ → 𝔽(1) → 𝔽_p(1) (trace 𝔽 → 𝔽_p). The pairing is well defined, 𝔽_p-bilinear with (λx, u) = (x, λu) for λ ∈ 𝔽, and defines an 𝔽-linear map f.
items.locator: §4.2, proof of Lemma 4.6, pp. 43–44, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3/local-to-global-presentation proof steps reproduce this pairing ("Pair with x ∈ H¹_{L^⊥}(S, ad⁰(1)) by Σ_v inv(x_v ∪ a_v + z_v), where ∂z = x ∪ c"). The independence-of-g̃_v step is incomplete as written for p = 2 (see sourceIssues). For p = 2 these R04.3 nodes do not apply as written: they are stated for p > 2 in Gee's conventions, with ad⁰ρ̄ and dual module ad⁰ρ̄(1), and frame only finite places. KW II §4 covers p = 2, with the correction δ₂ = 1, the dual (Ad⁰)*(1), where (Ad⁰)* ≅ Ad/Z (p. 39), and framed infinite places. That all-p form is stated by DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.2/presentation-relations-and-dual-selmer-bound ("KW II treats all p"). R04.3's text plans the bounds 'in the form of KW II §4, particularly Proposition 4.5 and Corollary 4.7', so the item stays planned there (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/3).

items.name: Lemma 4.6: bound on the number of relations
items.statement: In the presentation R^{□,ψ}_S ≅ R^{□,loc,ψ}_S[[X_1, …, X_g]]/J (V = ∅, Ad⁰ coefficients, inducing an isomorphism on relative tangent spaces), r(J) = dim_𝔽 J/𝔪J ≤ dim_𝔽 H¹_{{L_v^⊥}}(S, (Ad⁰)^*(1)). The map f is injective.
items.locator: §4.2, Lemma 4.6 and proof, pp. 43–45, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3/local-to-global-presentation (r(J) ≤ h²_{S,T}(ad⁰) = h¹ of the dual Selmer group with conditions L(D_v)^⊥; sources cite KW II Lemma 4.6) and DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.2/presentation-relations-and-dual-selmer-bound. The node writes the dual module as ad⁰ρ̄(1) (Gee's p > 2 convention); for p = 2 KW's (Ad⁰)^*(1) ≅ Ad/Z is only covered by citation. Injectivity uses the Poitou–Tate sequence and non-degeneracy of the Ш pairing. KW remark the argument follows Kisin [37] Lemma 4.1.1 / Böckle [4] Theorem 5.2 and answers a question of [37] §4.

items.name: Proof of Proposition 4.5: presentation of R̄^{□,ψ}_S and the lower bound 4|S|
items.statement: Base change along R^{□,loc,ψ}_S → R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S gives R̄^{□,ψ}_S ≅ R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S[[X_1, …, X_g]]/J′ with J′ generated by dim H¹_{{L_v^⊥}}(S, (Ad⁰)^*(1)) elements. Hence abs.dim R̄^{□,ψ}_S ≥ |S| − 1 + abs.dim R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S = |S| − 1 + 1 + 3|S| = 4|S| (R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S being 𝒪-flat with components of relative dimension 3|S|); comparing with abs.dim R̄^{□,ψ}_S = abs.dim R̄^ψ_S + 4|S| − 1 (Proposition 4.1) gives abs.dim R̄^ψ_S ≥ 1.
items.locator: §4.2, proof of Proposition 4.5, p. 45, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3/global-dimension-lower-bound proof steps (dim R^□ ≥ dim R^loc + g − r(J); forgetting framing removes n²#T − 1 dimensions). For p = 2 these R04.3 nodes do not apply as written: they are stated for p > 2 in Gee's conventions, with ad⁰ρ̄ and dual module ad⁰ρ̄(1), and frame only finite places. KW II §4 covers p = 2, with the correction δ₂ = 1, the dual (Ad⁰)*(1), where (Ad⁰)* ≅ Ad/Z (p. 39), and framed infinite places. That all-p form is stated by DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.2/presentation-relations-and-dual-selmer-bound ("KW II treats all p"). R04.3's text plans the bounds 'in the form of KW II §4, particularly Proposition 4.5 and Corollary 4.7', so the item stays planned there (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/3).

items.name: Dimension of a presentation (Krull's height theorem), used in Proposition 4.5
items.statement: For a Noetherian complete local ring A and elements f_1, …, f_r in the maximal ideal of A[[X_1, …, X_g]], dim A[[X_1, …, X_g]]/(f_1, …, f_r) ≥ dim A + g − r.
items.locator: §4.2, proof of Proposition 4.5, p. 45 (used implicitly), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Used without comment. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.2/presentation-relations-and-dual-selmer-bound (decomposition) states the consequence ("the absolute dimension of the global ring is bounded below by that of the local ring plus the excess of variables over relations"). Mathlib has the two ingredients but not the combined statement: mathlib:ringKrullDim_le_ringKrullDim_quotient_add_spanFinrank (Noetherian R, I ≤ Jacobson: dim R ≤ dim R/I + spanFinrank I) and mathlib:ringKrullDim_succ_le_ringKrullDim_powerseries (dim R + 1 ≤ dim R[[X]]).

items.name: Remarks after Lemma 4.6: systems of parameters, flatness and Cohen–Macaulay / Gorenstein / complete-intersection transfer
items.statement: Let r_1, …, r_{r(J)} ∈ J reduce to a basis of J/𝔪J. Granting that R̄^ψ_S is a finite 𝒪-module (Theorem 10.1), y_1, …, y_{4|S|−1}, r_1, …, r_{r(J)}, p is a system of parameters of R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S[[X_1, …, X_g]], where the images of the y_i generate R̄^{□,ψ}_S over R̄^ψ_S. If the 𝒪-algebras R̄^{□,ψ}_v are Cohen–Macaulay, it is a regular sequence; hence R̄^ψ_S is flat over 𝒪, and is Cohen–Macaulay (resp. Gorenstein, resp. a complete intersection) if all R̄^{□,ψ}_v are.
items.locator: §4.2, Remarks after Lemma 4.6, p. 45, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.4/integral-r-equals-t-when-smooth ("if each R̄^{□,ψ}_v is Cohen–Macaulay (resp. Gorenstein, resp. a complete intersection), so is R̄^ψ_S, once it is finite over 𝒪"; source: remarks after Lemma 4.6, p. 45). Being a system of parameters forces r(J) = h¹_{{L_v^⊥}}(S,(Ad⁰)^*(1)), which the remark leaves implicit.

items.name: Corollary 4.7: characteristic-zero points of R̄^ψ_S
items.statement: If R̄^ψ_S is a finitely generated ℤ_p-module, then there is a map of CNL_𝒪-algebras π : R̄^ψ_S → 𝒪′ with 𝒪′ the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p. As R̄^{□,ψ}_S is smooth (a power series ring) over R̄^ψ_S, there is also a morphism R̄^{□,ψ}_S → 𝒪″ with 𝒪″ of the same kind.
items.locator: §4.2, Corollary 4.7 and proof, pp. 45–46, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.4/characteristic-zero-points-from-finiteness-and-dimension (packet P7 and decomposition) with sub-lemmas nilpotent-uniformizer-artinian, generic-prime-coefficient-injection, algebraic-point-of-generic-prime; application PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.2/characteristic-zero-points-of-R-bar-S-psi-give-lifts-of-required-type. Not yet in Tau Ceti (no CharacteristicZeroPoints module at the pinned commit). Proof: p is not nilpotent (Proposition 4.5), so some prime I ∌ p, and R/I ↪ 𝒪′. Strictly, 𝒪′ may have a larger residue field than 𝔽, so "map of CNL_𝒪-algebras" means a local 𝒪-algebra map.

items.name: §5.1: the twisting group G_V and its diagonalizable group G*_V
items.statement: With S, V, ψ as in §4 (S ⊇ all places above p and ∞), F^S_V/F is the maximal abelian extension of F of p-power degree unramified outside V and split at the places of S, and G_V := Gal(F^S_V/F). G*_V is the diagonalizable group of characters of G_V in the category of functors on CNL_𝒪-algebras (§2.5): G*_V(A) = Hom(G_V, A^×), the continuous characters reducing to the trivial character modulo 𝔪_A. If p = 2, G_{V,2} := G_V/2G_V (maximal quotient killed by 2) and G*_{V,2} its character group.
items.locator: §5.1, p. 46, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/twisting-action (G_V, G*_V, G*_{V,2}) and R04.4/diagonalizable-groups ((a)* on complete local algebras).

items.name: §5.1: G_V is a finite abelian p-group (class field theory)
items.statement: Since S contains all places above p, G_V = Gal(F^S_V/F) is a finite abelian p-group.
items.locator: §5.1, p. 46, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Stated in GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/twisting-action ("it is a finite abelian p-group"); its hypothesis requests the class-field-theory proof from Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 12 (open request). KW II give no proof.

items.name: §5.1: the twisting action of G*_V and the automorphisms a_χ
items.statement: G*_V acts on Sp R^□_{S∪V}: for A ∈ CNL_𝒪, a lift ρ_A of ρ̄ and χ ∈ Hom(G_V, A^×), χ ⊗ ρ_A is unramified outside W and, χ being split at v ∈ S, det(χ ⊗ ρ_A)|D_v = ψχ_p; on framed tuples χ · (ρ, (ρ_v), (g_v)) = (χ ⊗ ρ, (ρ_v), (g_v)) (the action is trivial on the frame). This defines automorphisms a_χ of R^□_{S∪V} with a_χ ∘ ρ^{□,univ}_{S∪V} = χ ⊗ ρ^{□,univ}_{S∪V}, commuting with the action of ∏_{v∈S}(GL₂)₁ (Proposition 4.1). If p = 2 and χ ∈ G*_{V,2}(A), then χ² = 1 and det(χ ⊗ ρ_A) = det ρ_A, so G*_{V,2} acts on Sp R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V}. These actions restrict to Sp R̄^□_{S∪V} (resp. Sp R̄^{□,ψ}_{S∪V}) and factor through actions on Sp R̄_{S∪V} (resp. Sp R̄^ψ_{S∪V}).
items.locator: §5.1, p. 46, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/twisting-action states all of this (including descent to local-condition quotients and trace subrings).

items.name: Lemma 5.1: freeness of the dyadic twisting action
items.statement: Let p = 2 (ρ̄ with non-solvable image). If A is a CNL_𝒪-algebra, a lift ρ_A : G_F → GL(V_A) of ρ̄ is not equivalent to any of its twists χ ⊗ ρ_A by a non-trivial χ ∈ Hom(G_V, A^×). Consequently the actions of G*_V on R^□_{S∪V} and of G*_{V,2} on R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} are free (in the sense of §2.4).
items.locator: §5.2, Lemma 5.1 and proof, pp. 46–47, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/twist-action-free. Proof: choose g with χ(g) ≠ 1 and tr ρ̄(g) ≠ 0 (possible because the projective image SL₂(𝔽₀), |𝔽₀| > 2, is perfect; KW state the existence without argument); then χ(g) tr ρ_A(g) ≠ tr ρ_A(g) as tr ρ_A(g) is a unit.

items.name: Lemma 5.2(1): H¹(Gal(KF_m/F), Ad⁰(ρ̄)^*(1)) = 0 for p > 2
items.statement: Let F be totally real and unramified above p, ρ̄ : G_F → GL₂(𝔽) totally odd with ρ̄|G_{F(μ_p)} absolutely irreducible, p > 2 (hence ρ̄|G_{F(ζ_{p^m})} irreducible for all m ≥ 0). Let K/F be the extension cut out by Ad⁰(ρ̄) and F_m = F(ζ_{p^m}). Then H¹(Gal(KF_m/F), Ad⁰(ρ̄)^*(1)) = 0.
items.locator: §5.3, Lemma 5.2(1) and proof, p. 47, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof: the argument of DDT [14] Theorem 2.49 (stated there for F = ℚ; KW say it extends because F is unramified at p); for p ≥ 5 also Taylor [59] Lemma 2.5. ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.6/sigma-criterion states the F = ℚ case; GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/odd-taylor-wiles-primes names this exact statement (KW II Lemma 5.2(1)) as its R02.6 input.

items.name: Lemma 5.2(2): H¹(Gal(KF_m/F), Ad(ρ̄)) for p = 2
items.statement: Let F be totally real, unramified above 2, ρ̄ : G_F → GL₂(𝔽) totally odd with non-solvable image, p = 2; K/F the extension cut out by Ad(ρ̄), F_m = F(ζ_{2^m}). Then H¹(Gal(KF_m/F), Ad(ρ̄)) = H¹(F_m/F, Z) (Z = 𝔽·id ⊂ Ad), and H¹(F_m/F, Z) has 𝔽-dimension 2 for m > n₀, where n₀ is the largest m with F_m^+ ⊂ F (F_m^+ the maximal totally real subfield of F_m).
items.locator: §5.3, Lemma 5.2(2) and proof, p. 47, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof: Gal(KF_m/F_m) ≅ SL₂(𝔽₀) (simple), inflation–restriction with H⁰(SL₂(𝔽₀), M₂(𝔽)) = Z and H¹(SL₂(𝔽₀), Ad) = 0 (Lemma 4.3(5)); for m > n₀ the maximal elementary abelian 2-quotient of Gal(F_m/F) is (ℤ/2)². GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/dyadic-taylor-wiles-primes names it as an input "from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.6"; the R02.6 stage text covers the §5 p = 2 cohomology, but no R02.6 node states it.

items.name: Lemma 5.3: Taylor–Wiles primes for odd p
items.statement: Let p be odd and F totally real, unramified at p (with the §5.1 hypotheses on ρ̄). For each n ≥ 1 there is a finite set Q_n of places of F such that: |Q_n| = dim_𝔽 H¹_{{L_v^⊥}}(S, (Ad⁰)^*(1)); for v ∈ Q_n, v is unramified in ρ̄ and ψ, ρ̄(Frob_v) has distinct eigenvalues α_v, β_v, and N(v) ≡ 1 mod p^n; and H¹_{{L_v^⊥}}(S ∪ Q_n, (Ad⁰)^*(1)) = 0, where L_v^⊥ = 0 for v ∈ Q_n (L_v for v ∈ S as in Case 1).
items.locator: §5.4, Lemma 5.3 and proof, pp. 47–48, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/odd-taylor-wiles-primes (KW II form r = h¹_{{L_v^⊥}}(S, (Ad⁰)^*(1))). Proof: condition (1) of Taylor [59] Lemma 2.5 from Lemma 5.2(1), then Chebotarev. The Remark after the lemma (Diamond) explains why the argument fails for p = 2: (Ad⁰)^*(1) ≅ Ad/Z has Ad⁰/Z as its only irreducible submodule, on which no element with distinct eigenvalues has eigenvalue 1.

items.name: Lemma 5.4: local cohomology at the primes of Q_n (p odd)
items.statement: For v ∈ Q_n (Lemma 5.3), dim_𝔽 H¹(D_v, Ad⁰) = 2 = 1 + dim_𝔽 H⁰(D_v, Ad⁰).
items.locator: §5.4, Lemma 5.4 and proof, p. 48, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/taylor-wiles-local-cohomology states it; ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.6/taylor-wiles-local-count gives the F = ℚ version. Proof: local Euler characteristic and Tate duality reduce to dim H⁰(D_v, (Ad⁰)^*(1)) = 1, which holds as N(v) ≡ 1 mod p and ρ̄(Frob_v) has distinct eigenvalues.

items.name: Proposition 5.5: generator count at Taylor–Wiles level (p odd)
items.statement: For p odd and Q_n as in Lemma 5.3, R^{□,ψ}_{S∪Q_n} is generated over R^{□,loc,ψ}_S by |Q_n| + |S| − 1 = h¹_{{L_v^⊥}}(S, (Ad⁰)^*(1)) + |S| − 1 elements.
items.locator: §5.4, Proposition 5.5 and proof, p. 48, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/taylor-wiles-generator-count. Proof: Lemma 5.4, Lemma 4.4 and Wiles' formula (2).

items.name: §5.5.1: the dyadic Kummer data (M_n, x_n, y_n, n₀, κ_n, K, L, F_n, K_n, L_n, F̃_n)
items.statement: p = 2; F totally real, ρ̄ : G_F → GL₂(𝔽) with non-solvable image; S a finite set of places containing the archimedean places, the places above 2 and the places where ρ̄ ramifies. M_n := ℚ(μ_{2^n}) (n ≥ 1), M_n^+ its maximal totally real subfield; ε_1 = −1, ε_{n+1}² = ε_n; x_n := (ε_n + ε_n^{−1})/2, so M_n = ℚ(ε_n), M_n^+ = ℚ(x_n), x_2 = 0, x_3 = 1/√2, 2x_{n+1}² = x_n + 1; y_n := (x_n + 1)/2 = x_{n+1}², M_{n+1}^+ = M_n^+(√y_n). n₀ is the largest n ≥ 2 with M_n^+ ⊂ F. For n > n₀: ȳ_n is the image of y_{n₀} in F^×/(F^×)^{2^n} and κ_n ∈ H¹(G_F, μ_{2^n}) its Kummer class; K is the splitting field of Ad(ρ̄); L is the splitting field over K of the image of H¹(G_{F,S}, Ad(ρ̄)) in Hom(G_K, Ad(ρ̄)); F_n = F(μ_{2^n}), K_n = K(μ_{2^n}), L_n = L(μ_{2^n}); F̃_n is the extension of F_n cut out by the kernel of the image of κ_n in Hom(G_{F_n}, μ_{2^n}).
items.locator: §5.5 and §5.5.1, p. 48, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/dyadic-linear-disjointness states the same data.

items.name: Proposition 5.6: linear disjointness of L_n and F̃_n
items.statement: For n > n₀, L_n and F̃_n are linearly disjoint extensions of F_n.
items.locator: §5.5.1, Proposition 5.6 and proof, pp. 49–50, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/dyadic-linear-disjointness. Proof: K/F (group SL₂(𝔽₀), simple non-cyclic) is disjoint from the solvable Galois F̃_n/F; reduce to K_n(y_{n₀}^{1/4}) ⊄ L_n (L_n/K_n abelian of exponent 2), which would make Gal(F_n(y_{n₀}^{1/4})/F) abelian, contradicting Lemma 5.8.

items.name: Lemma 5.7: degrees of Kummer extensions of 2-power (p-power) order
items.statement: Let p be a prime and Ω a field of characteristic ≠ p containing a primitive p^n-th root of unity (n ≥ 1). Let y ∈ Ω^× and 1 ≤ m ≤ n. If Ω(y^{1/p^m})/Ω has degree p^a with a ≥ 1, then Ω(y^{1/p^n})/Ω has degree p^{a+n−m}.
items.locator: §5.5.1, Lemma 5.7, p. 49, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof left to the reader (standard Kummer theory; it holds because μ_{p^{n−m}} ⊂ (Ω^×)^{p^m}). Stated in GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/dyadic-linear-disjointness. Not in Mathlib: Mathlib/FieldTheory/KummerExtension.lean has irreducibility criteria for X^n − a and finrank_of_isSplittingField_X_pow_sub_C (degree n under irreducibility) but no degree formula of this shape; Tau Ceti has the Kummer map (TauCeti.kummerMap, TauCeti.kummerClassMap_injective) but not this lemma.

items.name: Lemma 5.8: F_{n₀}(y_{n₀}^{1/4})/F is dihedral of degree 8
items.statement: F_{n₀}(y_{n₀}^{1/4}) is a dihedral extension of F of degree 8.
items.locator: §5.5.1, Lemma 5.8 and proof, p. 49, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/dyadic-linear-disjointness (its proof step writes F(√y_{n₀}) = F·M_{n₀+1}^+, silently correcting the printed F M_{n₀+1}; see sourceIssues). Proof: F(i) = F_{n₀} is CM quadratic, F(√y_{n₀}) is totally real quadratic and disjoint from it, Lemma 5.7 gives degree 8, and Gal(F(i)/F) inverts μ₄.

items.name: Lemma 5.9(1): the Kummer extension F̃_n/F_n
items.statement: For n > n₀, F̃_n/F_n is cyclic of degree 2^{n−1} and its cyclic subextension of degree 2 is F_n(y_{n₀}^{1/4}).
items.locator: §5.5.1, Lemma 5.9(1), p. 50, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: From Lemma 5.7 with √y_{n₀} ∈ F_n and y_{n₀}^{1/4} ∉ F_n (Lemma 5.8). GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/dyadic-linear-disjointness.

items.name: Lemma 5.9(2): κ_n is unramified outside S and has order divisible by 2^{n−1}
items.statement: For n > n₀, κ_n is unramified outside S, i.e. κ_n ∈ H¹(G_{F,S}, μ_{2^n}), and the order of κ_n is divisible by 2^{n−1}.
items.locator: §5.5.1, Lemma 5.9(2) and proof, pp. 50–51, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof: the minimal polynomials R_n of x_n satisfy R_2 = X, R_3 = 2X² − 1, R_n(X) = R_{n−1}(2X² − 1), R_n = 2^{2^{n−2}−1}X^{2^{n−2}} + …, R_3(0) = −1 and R_n(0) = 1 (n ≥ 4); so x_n^{−1} is integral of norm 2^{2^{n−2}−1} (n ≥ 4) or −2 (n = 3), x_n is a unit away from 2, and y_{n₀} = x_{n₀+1}² too. Checked: R_4 = 8X⁴ − 8X² + 1. GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/dyadic-linear-disjointness.

items.name: Lemma 5.10(f): the ray-class 2-group G_n = Gal(F^S_{Q_n}/F)
items.statement: For a finite set Q_n of places, F^S_{Q_n} is the maximal abelian extension of F of 2-power degree unramified outside Q_n and split at the places of S, and G_n := Gal(F^S_{Q_n}/F). G_{n,2} is the maximal quotient of G_n killed by 2.
items.locator: §5.5.2, Lemma 5.10(f), p. 51; §5.6, p. 53, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/dyadic-taylor-wiles-primes (f) and R04.6/dyadic-patching-data (G_n, G′_n = G_n/2^{n−2}G_n). It is G_V of §5.1 with V = Q_n, p = 2.

items.name: Lemma 5.10(a)–(c): existence of dyadic auxiliary sets Q_n
items.statement: Let p = 2 (F totally real, ρ̄ with non-solvable image, S as in §5.5). For each n > n₀ there is a finite set Q_n of places of F such that: (a) |Q_n| = h¹(S, Ad) − 2 (independent of n); (b) for v ∈ Q_n, N(v) ≡ 1 mod 2^n, ρ̄ is unramified at v and ρ̄(Frob_v) has distinct eigenvalues α_v, β_v; (c) every v ∈ Q_n splits in the Kummer extension F̃_n/F, h⁰(D_v, Ad) = 2, and h¹_{Q_n−split}(S, Ad) = 2.
items.locator: §5.5.2, Lemma 5.10(a)–(c) and proof, pp. 50–52, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/dyadic-taylor-wiles-primes (a)–(c). Proof: claims (1) and (2) below applied to a complement of ker(H¹(G_{F,S}, Ad) → H¹(G_{F̃_n}, Ad)); H¹_{Q_n−split}(S, Ad) = H¹(F_n/F, Z). The proof calls the lemma "the Proposition".

items.name: Lemma 5.10(d): dimension of H¹_{S−split}(Q_n, Ad)
items.statement: h¹_{S−split}(Q_n, Ad) = 2 − Σ_{v∈S} h⁰(D_v, Ad) + Σ_{v∈Q_n} h⁰(D_v, Ad) = 2 − Σ_{v∈S} h⁰(D_v, Ad) + 2|Q_n|.
items.locator: §5.5.2, Lemma 5.10(d) and proof, pp. 50 and 52, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Wiles' formula (3) with h¹(D_v, Ad) − h⁰(D_v, Ad) = h²(D_v, Ad) = h⁰(D_v, Ad) for v ∈ Q_n (local Euler–Poincaré characteristic and Tate duality; Ad(1) = Ad for p = 2). GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/dyadic-taylor-wiles-primes (d).

items.name: Lemma 5.10(e): generators of R^□_{S∪Q_n} over R^{□,loc,ψ}_S
items.statement: The minimal number of generators of R^□_{S∪Q_n} (determinant fixed only on S) over R^{□,loc,ψ}_S is 2 + 2|Q_n| − 1.
items.locator: §5.5.2, Lemma 5.10(e) and proof, pp. 50 and 52, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: From (d) and Lemma 4.4(2). GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/dyadic-taylor-wiles-primes (e).

items.name: Lemma 5.10(f): structure of G_n/2^{n−2}G_n
items.statement: G_n/2^{n−2}G_n ≅ (ℤ/2^{n−2}ℤ)^t, where t = h¹_{S−split}(Q_n, 𝔽).
items.locator: §5.5.2, Lemma 5.10(f) and proof, pp. 51–53, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/dyadic-taylor-wiles-primes (f). Proof: Wiles' formula (4) for ℤ/2^n gives |H¹_{S−split}(Q_n, ℤ/2^n)| = |H¹_{Q_n−split}(S, μ_{2^n})|·2^{n−1}·2^{n(|Q_n|−|S|)} (checked: 2^n/2 from the global H⁰ terms, 2^{−n|S|}, 2^{n|Q_n|}); κ_n ∈ H¹_{Q_n−split}(S, μ_{2^n}) of order ≥ 2^{n−1} gives 2^{n(2+|Q_n|−|S|)−2} | |H¹_{S−split}(Q_n, ℤ/2^n)|, a ℤ/2^n-module generated by t elements.

items.name: Lemma 5.10(g): t = 2 − |S| + |Q_n|
items.statement: t = h¹_{S−split}(Q_n, 𝔽) (= h¹_{S−split}(Q_n, ℤ/2ℤ)) = 2 − |S| + |Q_n|.
items.locator: §5.5.2, Lemma 5.10(g) and proof, pp. 51–52, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof: H¹(G_F, 𝔽) ↪ H¹(G_F, Ad) (Lemma 4.3(4)), so H¹_{Q_n−split}(S, 𝔽) is the inflation of H¹(F_n/F, 𝔽) (dimension 2), then Wiles' formula for M = 𝔽 (h¹(D_v, 𝔽) − h⁰(D_v, 𝔽) = 1 at v ∈ Q_n). GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/dyadic-taylor-wiles-primes (g).

items.name: Lemma 5.10(h): the numerical coincidence for 2-adic patching
items.statement: [h¹_{S−split}(Q_n, Ad) − h¹_{S−split}(Q_n, 𝔽)] + [Σ_{v∈S} h⁰(D_v, Ad) − h⁰(G_F, Ad)] = |Q_n| + |S| − 1.
items.locator: §5.5.2, Lemma 5.10(h), p. 51, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Immediate from (d), (g) and h⁰(G_F, Ad) = 1. GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/dyadic-taylor-wiles-primes (h) and R04.6/patching-numerology (2h + 1 = h + j + t − d).

items.name: Proof of Lemma 5.10, claim (1): a single auxiliary place detecting a class
items.statement: Given ψ ∈ H¹(G_F, Ad) (for n > n₀) whose restriction to H¹(G_{F̃_n}, Ad) is non-trivial (hence also its restriction to H¹(G_{KF̃_n}, Ad), as H¹(G, Ad) = 0), there is a place v ∉ S of F such that v splits in F̃_n/F, ρ̄ is unramified at v with ρ̄(Frob_v) having distinct eigenvalues α_v, β_v, and ψ maps non-trivially to H¹(G_{𝔽_v}, Ad) ⊂ H¹(G_{F_v}, Ad). (By Chebotarev it suffices to find σ′ ∈ G_{F̃_n} with ρ̄(σ′) of distinct eigenvalues and ψ(σ′) ∉ (σ′ − 1)Ad; this uses that Z is the only non-zero irreducible G-submodule of Ad.)
items.locator: §5.5.2, proof of Lemma 5.10, (1), p. 51, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/dyadic-taylor-wiles-primes, first proof step. Odd analogue: ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.6/sigma-criterion. Chebotarev is Tau Ceti Chebotarev Layer 10 (planned).

items.name: Proof of Lemma 5.10, claim (2): the kernel of restriction to G_{F̃_n}
items.statement: For n > n₀: ker(H¹(G_{F,S}, Ad) → H¹(G_{F̃_n}, Ad)) = ker(H¹(G_{F,S}, Ad) → H¹(G_{F_n}, Ad)) = H¹(F_n/F, Ad^{im(ρ̄)}) = H¹(F_n/F, 𝔽), which has 𝔽-dimension 2 (Lemma 5.2); it is also the kernel of H¹(G_{F,S}, Ad) → H¹(G_{KF_n, S̃}, Ad).
items.locator: §5.5.2, proof of Lemma 5.10, (2), pp. 51–52, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Uses Proposition 5.6 and Lemma 4.3(5). GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/dyadic-taylor-wiles-primes, second proof step.

items.name: §5.6: Δ′_v, Δ′_{Q_n} and the class-field map Δ′_{Q_n} → G_n
items.statement: For v ∈ Q_n, Δ′_v is the maximal p-quotient of k_v^×, and 𝒪[Δ′_{Q_n}] := ⊗_{v∈Q_n} 𝒪[Δ′_v]. For p = 2, class field theory gives a natural map Δ′_{Q_n} → G_n mapping Δ′_v onto the inertia subgroup of G_n at v; this gives a meaning to χ(δ) for δ ∈ Δ′_{Q_n} and χ ∈ G*_{n,2}.
items.locator: §5.6, p. 53, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Δ_v, Δ_Q: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/taylor-wiles-datum (KW's Δ′). The map to G_n onto inertia (local–global class field theory) is used without proof and is not stated by any node; R04.5/taylor-wiles-inertia-action uses χ(δ) in its statement of Lemma 5.12.

items.name: Proposition 5.11(i): the universal deformation at an auxiliary place is a sum of two characters
items.statement: Let v ∈ Q_n (Lemma 5.3 for p odd, Lemma 5.10 for p = 2). The universal deformation ρ^{univ,ψ}_{S∪Q_n} over R̄^ψ_{S∪Q_n} restricted to D_v is of the form diag(γ_{α_v}, γ_{β_v}), where γ_{α_v}, γ_{β_v} are characters of D_v which modulo the maximal ideal are unramified and send Frob_v to α_v and β_v respectively. Moreover γ_v := γ_{α_v}|I_v = γ_{β_v}^{−1}|I_v is a character I_v → Δ′_v → (R̄^ψ_{S∪Q_n})^×.
items.locator: §5.6, Proposition 5.11, p. 53, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Called standard, citing Taylor [59] Lemma 2.1 ("p may be odd or even"). GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/taylor-wiles-inertia-action; local input LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.2/taylor-wiles-local-ring (Gee Lemma 3.33).

items.name: Proposition 5.11(ii): the 𝒪[Δ′_{Q_n}]-structure and its augmentation quotient
items.statement: The character γ_v endows R̄^ψ_{S∪Q_n} (and hence R̄^{□,ψ}_{S∪Q_n}) with a structure of 𝒪[Δ′_{Q_n}] = ⊗_{v∈Q_n} 𝒪[Δ′_v]-module, and its quotient by the augmentation ideal of 𝒪[Δ′_{Q_n}] is isomorphic to R̄^ψ_S (resp. R̄^{□,ψ}_S).
items.locator: §5.6, Proposition 5.11, p. 53, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/taylor-wiles-inertia-action; the quotient statement is R04.4/enlarging-ramification (whose sources cite Proposition 5.11).

items.name: Lemma 5.12: compatibility of twisting with the Δ′_{Q_n}-action (p = 2)
items.statement: Let p = 2, G_{n,2} the maximal quotient of G_n killed by 2, acting on R̄^ψ_{S∪Q_n} through G*_{n,2}(R̄^ψ_{S∪Q_n}) by twisting. For δ ∈ Δ′_{Q_n} and χ ∈ (G_{n,2})^*(R̄^ψ_{S∪Q_n}): a_χ ∘ δ = χ(δ) · (δ ∘ a_χ).
items.locator: §5.6, Lemma 5.12 and proof, p. 53, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/taylor-wiles-inertia-action (last sentence) and R04.4/twisting-action (acceptance). Proof: δ acts by multiplication by γ_v(δ), and a_χ(γ_v(δ)) = χ(δ)γ_v(δ).

items.name: Theorem 6.1(i): potential modularity of ρ̄ in weight k(ρ̄), unramified at p
items.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝔽) (𝔽 finite of characteristic p) be of S-type (odd and absolutely irreducible), with 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1 if p > 2; assume ρ̄ has non-solvable image when p = 2 and ρ̄|ℚ(μ_p) is absolutely irreducible when p > 2. Then there is a totally real field F, Galois over ℚ of even degree, unramified at p, and split above p if ρ̄|D_p is irreducible, with im(ρ̄) = im(ρ̄|G_F) and ρ̄|F(μ_p) absolutely irreducible, such that (i), assuming k(ρ̄) = 2 if p = 2: ρ̄|G_F arises from a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL₂(𝔸_F) that is discrete series of weight k(ρ̄) at the infinite places and unramified at all places above p.
items.locator: §6, Theorem 6.1(i), pp. 53–54; proof pp. 54–57, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.3/kw-ii-theorem-6-1-potential-modularity-of-rho-bar-over-a-controlled-F (states (i)–(ii) verbatim). Inputs: Taylor [58], [59]; Khare [33] Theorem 2.1; Moret-Bailly; Langlands–Tunnell; Theorem 8.2 for solvable image. Its p = 2 cases also depend on the local points of Taylor's moduli problem at 2 and at the auxiliary primes (/341). No node states those in residual characteristic 2 (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/4).

items.name: Theorem 6.1(ii): potential modularity of ρ̄ in parallel weight 2 with conductor dividing v above p
items.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝔽) (𝔽 finite of characteristic p) be of S-type (odd and absolutely irreducible), with 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1 if p > 2; assume ρ̄ has non-solvable image when p = 2 and ρ̄|ℚ(μ_p) is absolutely irreducible when p > 2. Then there is a totally real field F, Galois over ℚ of even degree, unramified at p, and split above p if ρ̄|D_p is irreducible, with im(ρ̄) = im(ρ̄|G_F) and ρ̄|F(μ_p) absolutely irreducible, such that (ii): ρ̄|G_F arises from a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL₂(𝔸_F) such that, at every place v above p, π_v has conductor dividing v (and is unramified if ρ̄ is finite flat at v), and π is of weight 2 at the infinite places.
items.locator: §6, Theorem 6.1(ii), p. 54; proof pp. 54–57, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.3/kw-ii-theorem-6-1-potential-modularity-of-rho-bar-over-a-controlled-F. Same F as in (i). Its p = 2 cases also depend on the local points of Taylor's moduli problem at 2 and at the auxiliary primes (/341). No node states those in residual characteristic 2 (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/4).

items.name: Theorem 6.1(iii)(a): making ρ̄ trivial at places above p when k(ρ̄) = p and ρ̄|I_p is trivial
items.statement: In Theorem 6.1, if k(ρ̄) = p and ρ̄|I_p is trivial, F may be chosen so that ρ̄|D_℘ is trivial for every place ℘ of F above p.
items.locator: §6, Theorem 6.1(iii)(a), p. 54; proof p. 57, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.5/control-of-the-extension (a). Proof: enlarge F by an extension unramified (but not split) at p.

items.name: Theorem 6.1(iii)(b): prescribed local extensions at finitely many primes ℓ_i ≠ p
items.statement: In Theorem 6.1, given finitely many primes ℓ_i ≠ p and finite extensions F_{ℓ_i}/ℚ_{ℓ_i}, F may be chosen so that for every embedding F ↪ ℚ̄_{ℓ_i} the closure of F contains F_{ℓ_i}.
items.locator: §6, Theorem 6.1(iii)(b), p. 54; proof p. 57, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.5/control-of-the-extension (b) (mechanism: successive Grunwald–Wang). The printed proof treats only ℓ_i ≠ 2, p (see sourceIssues); Theorem 10.1 invokes (b) for every ℓ_i ≠ p at which τ ramifies. Grunwald–Wang itself is not planned (see its item).

items.name: Theorem 6.1(iii)(c): F split at p in weight p + 1
items.statement: In Theorem 6.1, if p > 2 and k(ρ̄) = p + 1, F may be chosen split at p.
items.locator: §6, Theorem 6.1(iii)(c), p. 54; proof p. 57, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.5/control-of-the-extension (c). Proof (for any even k(ρ̄), p > 2): if ρ̄|D_p irreducible apply [59]; otherwise twist by γ₂^{−1} where det(ρ̄)χ_p^{−1} = η₁γ₂² with η₁ even and split at p, take F ⊇ F₀ = fixed field of ker η₁ and apply [58] Theorem 1.6.

items.name: Theorem 6.1(iii)(d): linear disjointness from a given finite extension
items.statement: In Theorem 6.1, given a finite extension L of ℚ, F may moreover be chosen linearly disjoint from L.
items.locator: §6, Theorem 6.1(iii)(d), p. 54; proof p. 57, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.5/control-of-the-extension (d) and R23.1/forcing-linear-disjointness-by-extra-split-places (require F split at primes unramified in L whose Frobenii generate the Galois group of the Galois closure of L/ℚ).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 6.1: the solvable-image case
items.statement: If ρ̄ (of S-type, p > 2 here) has solvable image, then ρ̄ arises from S_k(Γ₁(N)) for some N and k ≥ 2 (Langlands–Tunnell), hence from S_{k(ρ̄)}(Γ₁(N)) with p ∤ N and from S₂(Γ₁(Np)) (Gross [27] Theorem 13.10, Propositions 8.13, 8.18; Coleman–Voloch [12]; Edixhoven [23]); so hypotheses (α), (β) of §8.2 hold and (i), (ii) follow from Theorem 8.2.
items.locator: §6, proof of Theorem 6.1, p. 54, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.3/kw-ii-theorem-6-1-potential-modularity-of-rho-bar-over-a-controlled-F (source "proof of Theorem 6.1, solvable case, p. 54"); Langlands–Tunnell is GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R17.5, weight optimisation SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.3. Theorem 8.2 is outside this range.

items.name: Proof of Theorem 6.1: keeping ρ̄|G_{F(μ_p)} irreducible when the projective image is dihedral
items.statement: If the projective image of ρ̄ is dihedral, choosing every auxiliary field linearly disjoint from the field cut out by ρ̄ and split at a prime that splits in the field cut out by the projectivisation of ρ̄ but is inert in the quadratic subfield of ℚ(μ_p) ensures that ρ̄|G_{F(μ_p)} is irreducible for all the fields F considered.
items.locator: §6, proof of Theorem 6.1, p. 54, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Asserted without further argument (it holds: the quadratic subfield K′ of K(√p^*) other than K and ℚ(√p^*) would have to lie in F, but the chosen prime is inert in K′). No node states it; nearest: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.3/R23.5 stage texts (verify hypotheses; control of the extension) and GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R17.6 ("conditions preserving residual irreducibility" for base change).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 6.1: real points of Taylor's moduli problem X for p = 2
items.statement: For p = 2, X(ℝ) ≠ ∅. If ρ̄|D₂ is reducible (Taylor [58], polarisation (𝒪_M^+) ≅ P(A, i) as in the erratum [59] p. 776): A(ℂ) = ℂ^{Hom(M,ℝ)}/L with L = δ_M^{−1}·1 + 𝒪_M z (z ∈ (iℝ_{>0})^{Hom(M,ℝ)}), Riemann forms E(x + yz, u + vz) = tr_{M/ℚ}(a(yu − xv)); complex conjugation acts trivially on A[2], giving a real point when ρ̄(c) = 1; when ρ̄(c) ≠ 1 one uses the sublattice L′ = {u + zv ∈ L : v ≡ βu mod 2𝒪_M} (β ∈ δ_M generating δ_{M,2}) with polarisation from ½E, on which c has matrix (1 0; −1 −1) in the basis (γ + z, 2z) (γβ ≡ 1 mod 2). If ρ̄|D₂ is irreducible (Taylor [59], polarisation ((δ_M^{−1})^+) ≅ P(A, i)): take A = E ⊗ 𝒪_M with E/ℝ an elliptic curve with 4 or 2 real points of order 2 according as ρ̄(c) is trivial or not.
items.locator: §6, proof of Theorem 6.1, pp. 54–55, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.2/taylor-lemmas-1-3-1-4-local-points-at-p-and-at-infinity records in its hypotheses that residual characteristic 2 needs KW's lattice L′; R23.2 stage text ("suitable real points") and HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H6 ("prove nonempty real … local open loci by explicit abelian varieties") plan it; no node states the p = 2 construction. Checked: c(γ + z) = (γ + z) − 2z, c(2z) = −2z.

items.name: Proof of Theorem 6.1: the case p = 2, k(ρ̄) = 4 (parallel weight 2, Steinberg above 2)
items.statement: For p = 2 and k(ρ̄) = 4, ρ̄|G_F is associated to a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(𝔸_F) of parallel weight 2 which is Steinberg at the places above 2 (so of weight 2 and level v for v | 2), by Taylor's argument [58] in the case χ_v² = 1, choosing A with completely toric reduction above 2 (first case of [58] Lemma 1.2).
items.locator: §6, proof of Theorem 6.1, pp. 55–56, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Covered by PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.3/kw-ii-theorem-6-1-potential-modularity-of-rho-bar-over-a-controlled-F (source "p = 2 and k(rho-bar) = 4, pp. 55-56").

items.name: Proof of Theorem 6.1: k(ρ̄) = 2 — unramified above p, ordinary when ρ̄ is ordinary
items.statement: If k(ρ̄) = 2, π can be taken of weight 2, unramified above p (including p = 2), and ordinary at the places above p if ρ̄ is ordinary. If ρ̄|D_p is irreducible, impose χ unramified at p in [59] Lemma 4.3. If ρ̄ is ordinary: after an unramified twist, ρ̄|D_p ≅ (χ_pχ_v^{−1} ∗; 0 χ_v) with χ_v unramified; the obstruction in H²(D_v, 𝒪_{M,λ}(χ_pχ̃_v^{−2})) to lifting the extension class x vanishes (automatic if χ_v² ≠ 1; if χ_v² = 1 it equals η ∪ x with η unramified and x finite), so there is a local abelian variety A_v with good ordinary reduction; Moret-Bailly (part II, Théorème 1.3) with Ω_v the points of X(ℚ_p) reducing to x_v then gives A over F with good ordinary reduction above p.
items.locator: §6, proof of Theorem 6.1, p. 56, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.3/kw-ii-theorem-6-1-potential-modularity-of-rho-bar-over-a-controlled-F (source "ordinary k(rho-bar) = 2 branch, p. 56"); R23.1/taylor-theorem-g-split-completely-points-are-dense records the use of Moret-Bailly with prescribed Ω_v; local points are R23.2. The obstruction comparison "o is the cup product η with x" is only sketched.

items.name: Proof of Theorem 6.1: weight adjustment for p ≠ 2, ρ̄|D_p reducible, k(ρ̄) > 2 (Hida theory)
items.statement: For p ≠ 2, ρ̄|D_p reducible and k(ρ̄) > 2, the abelian variety A of [58] Lemma 1.5 is ordinary at v | p with inertial Weil–Deligne parameter (ω^{k(ρ̄)−2} ⊕ 1, 0) if k(ρ̄) ≠ p + 1 and (1 ⊕ 1, N) (N ≠ 0 nilpotent) if k(ρ̄) = p + 1; so ρ̄ arises from a parallel weight 2 cuspidal π, ordinary above p with the same inertial parameter (as in [58], using [13] Appendix B), and then by Hida theory ([30] §8, with [33] Lemma 2.2 to avoid neatness) from a cuspidal π unramified above p of parallel weight k(ρ̄).
items.locator: §6, proof of Theorem 6.1, pp. 56–57, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.3/kw-ii-theorem-6-1-potential-modularity-of-rho-bar-over-a-controlled-F (source "weight adjustment, p. 57"); Hida control over totally real fields is PadicFamilies:L5. KW note that for k(ρ̄) = p with ρ̄|D_p semisimple, [58] does not say to which line the cyclotomic line reduces.

items.name: Proof of Theorem 6.1: the case p = 3 with ρ̄|D_p irreducible
items.statement: For p = 3 and ρ̄|D_p irreducible, the weight adjustment of [59] §5 (stated there for p > 3) remains available: Lemma 2.2 of Khare [33] (see [33] §2) lifts the restriction p ≠ 3.
items.locator: §6, proof of Theorem 6.1, p. 56, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.3/kw-ii-theorem-6-1-potential-modularity-of-rho-bar-over-a-controlled-F (source "p = 3 branch, p. 56"); R23.3/taylor-2006-theorem-5-7-serre-weight-at-level-one records Khare's Lemma 2.2 as an unread gap. Khare [33] Lemma 2.2 itself is not planned (see its item).

items.name: External: local Tate duality (DDT [14] Theorem 2.17)
items.statement: For a finite place v and a finite G_{F_v}-module M with nM = 0, cup product and the local invariant give a perfect pairing H¹(D_v, M) × H¹(D_v, M^*(1)) → ℚ/ℤ (here 𝔽-valued for M = Ad⁰, Ad), and more generally H^i × H^{2−i}; in particular H²(D_v, M) is dual to H⁰(D_v, M^*(1)).
items.locator: §4.1.4, p. 39 (definition of L_v^⊥); proofs of Lemma 5.4, p. 48, and Lemma 5.10(d), p. 52; also §3.2.5 proof of Lemma 3.7, p. 26; §3.2.6, p. 30; §3.2.7, p. 32; §3.3.4, p. 37, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 plans local Tate duality (tateDualityPairing_perfect_mixed for the evaluation pairing Hom(A, μ_n) × A → μ_n); ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7/derived-local-duality for the derived form. Not in the pinned libraries.

items.name: External: the local Euler–Poincaré characteristic formula
items.statement: For a finite place v of F and a finite G_{F_v}-module M that is an 𝔽-vector space (p = char 𝔽): h⁰(D_v, M) − h¹(D_v, M) + h²(D_v, M) = 0 if v ∤ p, and = −[F_v : ℚ_p]·dim_𝔽 M if v | p.
items.locator: proofs of Lemma 5.4, p. 48, and Lemma 5.10(d), p. 52; also §3.2.5 proof of Lemma 3.7, p. 26; §3.2.6, p. 30; §3.2.7, p. 32; §3.3.4, p. 37, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Used at auxiliary primes v ∤ p (§5) and, at v | p, in the dimension counts of §3.2. Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 plans the cardinality Euler characteristic and eulerCharacteristic_finrank_fp.

items.name: External: Poitou–Tate duality ([48] 8.6.7–8.6.8) in the form used for Lemma 4.6
items.statement: For the finite G_{F,S}-module Ad⁰ (and its dual (Ad⁰)^*(1)) there is an exact sequence H¹(S, Ad⁰) → ⊕_{v∈S} H¹(D_v, Ad⁰)/L_v → H¹_{{L_v^⊥}}(S, (Ad⁰)^*(1))^* → Ш²(S, Ad⁰); the Poitou–Tate pairing Ш¹(S, (Ad⁰)^*(1)) × Ш²(S, Ad⁰) → ℚ/ℤ is non-degenerate, and for [x] ∈ Ш¹ it is computed by the cochain formula Σ_v inv((x_v ∪ a_v) + z_v) with δz = x ∪ c, c|D_v = δa_v (so that (x, u) is the Poitou–Tate product of [x] with [c]); the 2-cochain z with values in 𝒪_S^× and δz = x ∪ c exists as in the proof of [48] 8.6.7.
items.locator: §4.2, proof of Lemma 4.6, pp. 43–44, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.4/poitou-tate (nine-term sequence, non-degenerate Ш pairing, cochain description Σ_v inv_v(c_v)); the Selmer-condition form of the sequence is derived from it (R02.5). Numbering 8.6.7/8.6.8 refers to NSW 1st ed. (2000) and was not checked.

items.name: External: Dickson's classification of finite subgroups of PGL₂(𝔽̄_p)
items.statement: A finite irreducible subgroup of GL₂(𝔽̄_p) has projective image dihedral, A₄, S₄, A₅, PSL₂(𝔽₀) or PGL₂(𝔽₀) for a finite field 𝔽₀; for p = 2, a non-solvable projective image is PGL₂(𝔽₀) ≅ SL₂(𝔽₀) with |𝔽₀| = 2^r, r > 1 (a simple group).
items.locator: proofs of Lemma 4.3(2)(ii), p. 40, Lemma 5.1, pp. 46–47, and Lemma 5.2(2), p. 47, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement (data/decompositions). Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

items.name: External: the Chebotarev density theorem
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension of number fields E/F and a conjugacy class C ⊂ Gal(E/F), the set of places v of F unramified in E with Frob_v ∈ C has Dirichlet density |C|/[E : F] (in particular it is infinite, and one may avoid any finite set of places).
items.locator: proofs of Lemma 5.3, p. 48, and Lemma 5.10, (1), p. 51, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Tau Ceti Chebotarev Layer 10 (hasDirichletDensity_frobeniusPrimeSet). At the pinned commit Tau Ceti has only infrastructure (NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet, NumberField.exists_auxiliaryPrime), not the density theorem; GlobalGaloisDeformations requests it (open).

items.name: External: the inflation–restriction exact sequence in degree 1
items.statement: For a group G, a normal subgroup N and a G-module A, 0 → H¹(G/N, A^N) → H¹(G, A) → H¹(N, A) is exact.
items.locator: proofs of Lemma 5.2(2), p. 47 (G = Gal(KF_m/F), N = Gal(KF_m/F_m)), and Lemma 5.10, (1)–(2), pp. 51–52, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Read in Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/GroupCohomology/Functoriality.lean: H1InfRes is the short complex H¹(G ⧸ S, A^S) ⟶ H¹(G, A) ⟶ H¹(S, A), H1InfRes_exact its exactness, and an instance there proves the inflation map is a monomorphism. This is for abstract (discrete) groups, which covers the finite Galois group of Lemma 5.2(2); the profinite continuous version used in Lemma 5.10 is planned in ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.2 (compact-five-term, five-term-transgression).

items.name: External: Taylor's potential modularity theorems ([58] Theorem 1.6; [59] Proposition 4.1, Corollary 4.6, Theorem 5.7; [33] Theorem 2.1)
items.statement: For ρ̄ odd and irreducible (with the local hypotheses of each statement) there is a finite Galois totally real extension, split or controlled at the places above p, over which ρ̄ becomes modular: Taylor [58] Theorem 1.6 (p odd, ρ̄ ordinary-shaped at p, with ordinary lift refinement), Taylor [59] Proposition 4.1 and Corollary 4.6 (ρ̄|G_ℓ irreducible, ℓ split completely, weight 2) and Theorem 5.7 (p > 3, Serre weight, unramified everywhere), and Khare [33] Theorem 2.1; their proofs use Taylor's Hilbert–Blumenthal moduli problem X with level structures, a point x ∈ X(F) from Moret-Bailly, and modularity of an auxiliary residual representation with solvable image.
items.locator: §6, Theorem 6.1 and its proof, pp. 53–57, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.3/taylor-theorem-1-6-potential-residual-modularity-ordinary-at-l, R23.3/taylor-2006-potential-modularity-when-residually-irreducible-at-l, R23.3/taylor-2006-theorem-5-7-serre-weight-at-level-one; Khare [33] Theorem 2.1 has no node of its own (it is subsumed by R23.3/kw-ii-theorem-6-1-potential-modularity-of-rho-bar-over-a-controlled-F). These Taylor results are stated for odd residual characteristic. KW's p = 2 cases also depend on the local points of Taylor's moduli problem at 2 and at the auxiliary primes (/341), which no node states in residual characteristic 2 (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/4).

items.name: External: Moret-Bailly's theorem ([47] part II, Théorème 1.3)
items.statement: Every incomplete Skolem datum (X → Spec R, Σ, {L_v}, {Ω_v}) with X geometrically irreducible and Ω_v non-empty Galois-stable open sets of smooth local points has an integral point: a finite extension K′/K, split as L_v at each v ∈ Σ, and x ∈ X(R′) with all local images in Ω_v. Used to find F and x ∈ X(F) with prescribed local behaviour at ∞, p and the auxiliary primes (and with prescribed reduction x_v in the ordinary case, and extra split primes for (iii)(d)).
items.locator: §6, proof of Theorem 6.1, pp. 54–57, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.1/moret-bailly-theorem-incomplete-skolem-data-have-integral-points (and R23.1/theorem-g-from-moret-bailly, R23.1/forcing-linear-disjointness-by-extra-split-places).

items.name: External: Langlands–Tunnell
items.statement: A continuous odd irreducible ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝔽̄_p) with solvable image arises from a cusp form in S_k(Γ₁(N)) for some N and k ≥ 2 (via Langlands [40] base change and Tunnell [65] octahedral case; hint in Serre [56] p. 220).
items.locator: §6, proof of Theorem 6.1 (solvable case), p. 54, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R17.5 ("Automorphic induction and Langlands–Tunnell", with "the full soluble-image input required by the Serre proof").

items.name: External: Serre-weight optimisation (Gross [27] Theorem 13.10, Propositions 8.13, 8.18; Coleman–Voloch [12]; Edixhoven [23])
items.statement: If ρ̄ (p odd, irreducible, modular) arises from S_k(Γ₁(N)) for some k ≥ 2, then it arises from S_{k(ρ̄)}(Γ₁(N′)) for some N′ prime to p, and also from S₂(Γ₁(N′p)).
items.locator: §6, proof of Theorem 6.1 (solvable case), p. 54, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.3 ("Prove the Edixhoven/Serre weight theorem … including the reducible and irreducible local cases").

items.name: External: Hida theory over totally real fields ([30] §8) with [13] Appendix B
items.statement: For π cuspidal of parallel weight 2, ordinary at the places above p with prescribed inertial Weil–Deligne parameters (ω^{k−2} ⊕ 1, 0) or (1 ⊕ 1, N), ρ̄_π also arises from a cuspidal π′ of parallel weight k unramified above p (Hida families; CDT Appendix B for the local shape of ordinary Hilbert modular forms).
items.locator: §6, proof of Theorem 6.1 (weight adjustment), p. 57, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PadicFamilies:L5 ("Establish Hida control on the actual ordinary loci … over totally real fields"); CDT [13] Appendix B has no identified node. Neatness is avoided with Khare [33] Lemma 2.2 (not planned).

items.name: External: Khare [33] Lemma 2.2 (removing p = 3 and neatness restrictions)
items.statement: Lemma 2.2 of Khare, "Serre's modularity conjecture: the level one case" (Duke 2006), as used by KW: it allows one to lift the restriction p ≠ 3 in [59] §5 and to avoid the neatness hypothesis in Hida [30] §8.
items.locator: §6, proof of Theorem 6.1, pp. 56–57; §8.2, proof of Theorem 8.2 (via Lemma 8.3), p. 73, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas. It is used twice. (1) In the proof of Theorem 6.1 (pp. 56–57): PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.3/kw-ii-theorem-6-1-potential-modularity-of-rho-bar-over-a-controlled-F lists "Lemma 2.2 of [33]" among its imports, and R23.3/taylor-2006-theorem-5-7-serre-weight-at-level-one records it as unread (a gap). (2) In the proof of Theorem 8.2 (p. 73), to take the level U of Lemma 8.3 neat in the sense of Taylor [59] Lemma 1.1. The item is routed with Taylor's neatness lemma (/272) to HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.3 (route 8).
