There it closes no cycle with its consumers SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.6 and R23.3; at R23.3 it closed one, through the R23.3 node's import of Theorem 8.2 (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/1). Also: ClassicalSerreModularity:R26.x nodes cite Khare's level-one paper but not this lemma. The statement was not read here (only KW's description of its use).

items.name: External: the Grunwald–Wang theorem
items.statement: For a number field K, a finite set of places Σ and cyclic local extensions L_v/K_v (v ∈ Σ) of degrees dividing n, there is a cyclic global extension L/K of degree n realising them, outside the special case (8 | n and places above 2).
items.locator: §6, proof of Theorem 6.1(iii)(b), p. 57; §7.6.3, proof of Lemma 7.10, p. 69, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2/R02.4 (route 4). Three accepted extractions route the same theorem there: PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/84 (the same Artin–Tate, Chapter X, Theorem 5), PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21/189 and PAPER-ALLEN-ETAL-23/328. KW use it twice: for the local conditions of Theorem 6.1(iii)(b) (p. 57), and for p = 2 in the proof of Lemma 7.10 (p. 69, /252). Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 12 says explicitly that "The Grunwald–Wang theorem is not used and is outside this roadmap". The former route to InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.4 followed GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/change-of-determinant, which says it "is planned under InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.4", but the IG.4 stage text (embedding problems, Shafarevich) does not state it. The InverseGalois packet's coverage and PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23/130 also place it at IG.4, so the choice of a single owner is left to the maintainer (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/2).

items.name: External: presentations over local deformation rings (Kisin [36] Lemma 3.2.2; Kisin [37] Lemma 4.1.1; Böckle [4] Theorem 5.2)
items.statement: The global framed deformation ring is a quotient of a power series ring over the completed tensor product of the local framed rings, in as many variables as the relative tangent dimension, by an ideal with at most h¹ of the dual Selmer group generators; KW's Lemma 4.4 is proved "by arguments as in the proof of Lemma 3.2.2 of [36]", and Lemma 4.6 is "along the lines of Lemma 4.1.1 of [37], or Theorem 5.2 of [4]".
items.locator: §4.1.5, p. 41; §4.2, Remarks after Lemma 4.6, p. 45, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: KW re-prove the statements they need (Lemmas 4.4, 4.6), so these are cited as models rather than used as black boxes. GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3/local-to-global-presentation and relative-tangent-space plan the result (from Gee Proposition 3.24 and KW II). PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.3/bockle-presentation is a different result (Böckle's 2003 appendix to Khare).

items.name: §7 set-up: the definite quaternion algebra D and the coefficient rings
items.statement: Let p be any prime and F a totally real number field of even degree in which p is unramified. D is a quaternion algebra over F ramified at all infinite places and at a finite set Σ of finite places of F. Fix a maximal order 𝒪_D of D and isomorphisms (𝒪_D)_v ≃ M₂(𝒪_{F_v}) for all places v at which D is split. A is a topological ℤ_p-algebra which is either an algebraic extension of ℚ_p, the ring of integers of such an extension, or a quotient of such a ring of integers. E ⊂ ℚ̄_p is a sufficiently large finite extension of ℚ_p, with ring of integers 𝒪 = 𝒪_E and residue field 𝔽, containing the images of all embeddings F ↪ ℚ̄_p, and such that D_v ⊗_{F,ι} E is split for all places v above p and all embeddings ι : F ↪ E.
items.locator: §7, opening, pp. 57–58, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R18.3 ('Define algebraic automorphic forms on the finite double-coset set with their weight module and integral coefficients'). GL2ModularityLifting:R22.1/minimal-level-data and AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.6/hecke-algebra-representation-quaternionic restate this set-up (with |Σ| even). Mathlib has QuaternionAlgebra ℍ[R,a,b] and TauCeti has splitting lemmas (TauCeti.QuaternionAlgebra.oneEquivMatrix etc.), but neither has a quaternion algebra over a number field with prescribed ramification, maximal orders or its adelic points.

items.name: §7: the local level groups U₀(v) and U₁(v)
items.statement: For a place v at which D is split, U₀(v) = {g ∈ GL₂(𝒪_{F_v}) : g ≡ (a b; 0 d) mod π_v} and U₁(v) = {g ∈ GL₂(𝒪_{F_v}) : g ≡ (a b; 0 1) mod π_v}.
items.locator: §7, p. 58, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.2/auxiliary-level-groups builds (U_Q)_v inside U₀(v); GL2ModularityLifting:R22.1/minimal-level-data and AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.5/hilbert-local-behaviour-at-p use U₁(v). TauCeti's Γ₀/Γ₁ (TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing/GL2/Gamma0, Gamma1; ModularForms/CongruenceSubgroups) are congruence subgroups over ℤ, not over 𝒪_{F_v}.

items.name: §7: admissible levels U, the set Σ₀ and the maximal compact subgroup U⁰ (p = 2)
items.statement: U = ∏_v U_v is an open subgroup of (D ⊗_F 𝔸_F^∞)^× of the following shape, for a subset Σ₀ ⊂ Σ: at places v ∉ Σ₀, U_v ⊂ (𝒪_D)_v^× and U_v = (𝒪_D)_v^× for almost all v; for v ∈ Σ₀, U_v = D_v^×, and then [U_v : (𝒪_D)_v^× F_v^×] = 2. Non-empty Σ₀ is considered only when p = 2. When U is not compact, U⁰ = ∏_v U⁰_v denotes its maximal compact subgroup (U⁰_v maximal compact for v ∈ Σ₀, U⁰_v = U_v for the other finite v).
items.locator: §7, pp. 58–59, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.1/minimal-level-data takes U_v = D_v^× at v ∈ Σ when p = 2; the GL2ModularityLifting--R22.1 packet requests the non-compact level from R18.6 (open). The index-2 claim is the surjectivity of the normalised valuation of the reduced norm on D_v^×; not in the library.

items.name: §7: the space S_{τ,ψ}(U) = S_{τ,ψ}(U, A) of forms on D
items.statement: Let ψ : (𝔸_F^∞)^×/F^× → A^× be a continuous character and τ : U → Aut(W_τ) a continuous representation of U on a finitely generated A-module W_τ with τ|_{U∩(𝔸_F^∞)^×} = ψ^{-1}|_{U∩(𝔸_F^∞)^×}; ψ and τ are always such that, on an open subgroup of 𝒪_{F_p}^×, ψ is an integral power of the norm character N : ∏_{v|p} F_v^× → ℚ_p^× (product of the local norms). W_τ is regarded as a U(𝔸_F^∞)^×-module, U acting via τ and (𝔸_F^∞)^× via ψ^{-1}. S_{τ,ψ}(U) (also written S_{τ,ψ}(U, A)) is the space of functions f : D^×∖(D ⊗_F 𝔸_F^∞)^× → W_τ with f(gu) = u^{-1}f(g) and f(gz) = ψ(z)f(g) for all g ∈ (D ⊗_F 𝔸_F^∞)^×, u ∈ U, z ∈ (𝔸_F^∞)^×.
items.locator: §7, p. 58, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R18.3 plans algebraic automorphic forms on the finite double-coset set with weight module and integral coefficients; the GL2ModularityLifting--R22.1 packet requests 'definite quaternionic forms S_{τ,ψ}(U, A)' from R18.6 (open). No library counterpart.

items.name: §7: the weight modules W_k, W̄_k and the spaces S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪), S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝔽)
items.statement: For an integer k ≥ 2, with k = 2 if p = 2, W_k = ⊗_{F↪E} Sym^{k−2} 𝒪_E² and W̄_k = ⊗_{F↪E} Sym^{k−2} 𝔽², regarded as ∏_{v|p}(𝒪_D)_v^×-modules via an identification 𝒪_D ⊗_{𝒪_F} 𝒪_E ≅ M₂(𝒪_E); ψ : (𝔸_F^∞)^×/F^× → A^× acts on them through A^×, and ψ restricted to an open subgroup of (𝔸_F^∞)^× is N^{2−k} (N the product of the local norms at the places above p). For p > 2, W_k and W̄_k are U_p = ∏_{v|p}U_v-modules, hence U-modules. The modules W_τ used are W_k ⊗_𝒪 V with V finite free over 𝒪 on which U acts through a finite quotient, or W̄_k ⊗_𝒪 V with V a finite-dimensional 𝔽-vector space with a U-action (k = 2 if p = 2). For W_τ = W_k, W̄_k one writes S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪), S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝔽).
items.locator: §7, pp. 58–59, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R18.3 ('with their weight module and integral coefficients'); GL2ModularityLifting:R22.1/minimal-level-data uses W_k. Mathlib has SymmetricPower, but not these modules with their ∏_{v|p}(𝒪_D)_v^× action.

items.name: §7: extension of W₂ and W̄₂ to U(𝔸_F^∞)^× for non-compact U (p = 2)
items.statement: Let p = 2 and U non-compact (Σ₀ ≠ ∅), with maximal compact subgroup U⁰. U⁰ acts trivially on W₂ and W̄₂; U(𝔸_F^∞)^×/U⁰ is abelian and U(𝔸_F^∞)^×/U⁰(𝔸_F^∞)^× ≅ (ℤ/2ℤ)^{Σ₀}. Hence the U⁰(𝔸_F^∞)^×-module W₂ extends to a U(𝔸_F^∞)^×-module in one of 2^{|Σ₀|} ways (a fixed extension is again denoted W₂), and W̄₂ has a unique extension to U(𝔸_F^∞)^× (again denoted W̄₂). For p > 2, W_k and W̄_k are U-modules via U_p. So in all cases W_k and W̄_k are U(𝔸_F^∞)^×-modules.
items.locator: §7, p. 59, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.1/minimal-level-data: 'W_2 extended to U(𝔸_F^∞)^× when U is not compact'; the R22.1 packet requests 'the p = 2 extension of W_2 to non-compact U with U_v = D_v^× at Σ' from R18.6 (open). The count 2^{|Σ₀|} assumes 𝒪 contains the needed square roots.

items.name: §7, (5): forms as invariants on the finite double-coset set
items.statement: If (D ⊗_F 𝔸_F^∞)^× = ∐_{i∈I} D^× t_i U(𝔸_F^∞)^× for a finite set I and t_i ∈ (D ⊗_F 𝔸_F^∞)^×, then f ↦ (f(t_i))_i identifies S_{τ,ψ}(U) with ⊕_{i∈I} W_τ^{(U(𝔸_F^∞)^× ∩ t_i^{-1}D^× t_i)/F^×}.
items.locator: §7, display (5), p. 59, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R18.3 ('the finite double-coset set', 'Prove finiteness'). Mathlib has double cosets (Doset) and TauCeti an abstract double-coset Hecke API (HeckeCoset), but not the finiteness of D^×∖(D ⊗ 𝔸^∞)^×/U(𝔸^∞)^× or this identification.

items.name: §7: the set S, the Hecke operators T_v, S_v and the Hecke algebra 𝕋_ψ(U)
items.statement: S is a finite set of places of F containing the infinite places, Σ, the places above p, and the places v at which U_v ⊂ D_v^× is not maximal compact or U_v acts non-trivially on W_τ. Fix a uniformiser π_v of F_v for each finite v. Right translation g.f makes the double cosets U(π_v 0; 0 π_v)U and U(π_v 0; 0 1)U act on S_{k,ψ}(U) for v ∉ S; these are S_v (multiplication by ψ(π_v)) and T_v, independent of the choice of π_v. 𝕋_ψ(U) is the 𝒪-algebra generated by the endomorphisms T_v and S_v, v ∉ S, of S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪) (the weight k is suppressed from the notation).
items.locator: §7, p. 59, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R18.3 ('the Hecke action'); used by AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.6/hecke-algebra-representation-quaternionic and GL2ModularityLifting:R22.1/minimal-level-data. The abstract double-coset Hecke ring (Mathlib.NumberTheory.HeckeRing.Defs, TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing) exists, but not these adelic quaternionic operators.

items.name: §7: Eisenstein and non-Eisenstein maximal ideals
items.statement: A maximal ideal 𝔪 of 𝕋_ψ(U) is Eisenstein if T_v − 2 ∈ 𝔪 and S_v − 1 ∈ 𝔪 for all but finitely many places v that split in a fixed finite abelian extension of F. For non-Eisenstein 𝔪, S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪)_𝔪 denotes the localisation of S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪) at 𝔪.
items.locator: §7, p. 59, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.6/hecke-algebra-representation-quaternionic and R19.4/quaternionic-sigma-place-local-form take 'non-Eisenstein in the sense of KW II §7' as a hypothesis, by reference only; no node restates the definition. OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.2/permissible-maximal-ideal is Skinner–Wiles' analogue.

items.name: §7: the Galois representation ρ_f of a quaternionic eigenform (Jacquet–Langlands, [10], [61], [59] Lemma 1.3)
items.statement: Let 𝔪 be non-Eisenstein. For k = 2 the functions in S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪) that factor through the norm die in S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪)_𝔪. S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪)_𝔪 is identified with a space of cusp forms via the Jacquet–Langlands correspondence, as in Lemma 1.3 of [59]. Hence a Hecke eigenform f ∈ S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪)_𝔪 gives rise, as in [10] and [61], to ρ_f : G_F → GL₂(𝒪), which is residually irreducible because 𝔪 is non-Eisenstein. ρ_f is characterised by: for almost all places v of F, ρ_f is unramified at v and ρ_f(Frob_v) has characteristic polynomial X² − a_vX + N(v)ψ(Frob_v), where Frob_v is the arithmetic Frobenius and a_v is the T_v-eigenvalue of f.
items.locator: §7, pp. 59–60, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.6/hecke-algebra-representation-quaternionic states ρ_𝔪 over 𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪 with the Eichler–Shimura relation and its specialisations ρ_f; R19.2/hilbert-modular-compatible-system-carayol-theorem-A is [10]; PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.3/taylor-2006-lemma-1-3-quaternionic-forms-and-galois-representations is [59] Lemma 1.3, but only for D ramified exactly at the infinite places (Σ = ∅); R18.3 plans 'the comparison to the corresponding GL₂ representations'.

items.name: Lemma 7.1: Ihara-type lemma (Eisenstein kernel of the degeneracy map)
items.statement: Let U = ∏_v U_v be an open compact subgroup of (D ⊗_F 𝔸_F^∞)^× and W̄_τ a U(𝔸_F^∞)^×-module as before which is a finite-dimensional 𝔽-vector space on which (𝔸_F^∞)^× acts by ψ̄^{-1}. Let w ∉ Σ be a finite place of F such that U_w = GL₂(𝒪_w) is maximal compact and acts trivially on W̄_τ. Let U′ = ∏_v U′_v ⊂ U with U′_v = U_v for v ≠ w and U′_w = U₀(w), and let α_w : S_{W̄_τ,ψ̄}(U, 𝔽)² → S_{W̄_τ,ψ̄}(U′, 𝔽), (f₁, f₂) ↦ f₁ + (1 0; 0 π_w)f₂. Then the maximal ideals of the Hecke algebra 𝕋_ψ(U) (with S assumed to contain w), acting diagonally on S_{W̄_τ,ψ̄}(U, 𝔽)², that are in the support of ker(α_w) are Eisenstein.
items.locator: §7, Lemma 7.1, p. 60, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R18.4: 'Prove the finite-level and degeneracy-map properties used in R19/R22'; the GL2ModularityLifting--R22.1 README assigns KW II Lemma 7.1 to R18.3 (RS-23) and requests it through R18.6 (open). OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.2/ihara-lemma-quaternionic (Skinner–Wiles Lemma 3.26) is the same statement for D ramified only at infinity with trivial coefficients. The proof uses strong approximation for D¹ (AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.4). Stated for compact U but applied through Corollary 7.5 to non-compact U at p = 2 (source issue).

items.name: Lemma 7.2: the local form at the places of Σ, with a fixed unramified γ_v (and Remark)
items.statement: Keep the conventions of §7 and let U = ∏_v U_v be as before with, in addition: (i) U_v = (𝒪_D)_v^× for all v ∈ Σ when p > 2; (ii) U_v = D_v^× for all v ∈ Σ when p = 2 (i.e. Σ₀ = Σ). Consider S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪)_𝔪 for a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal 𝔪 (k = 2 when p = 2), and assume that Σ is disjoint from {v | p} if k > 2. Then for each v ∈ Σ there is a fixed unramified character γ_v : G_{F_v} → 𝒪^× such that for every Hecke eigenform f ∈ S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪)_𝔪, ρ_f|_{D_v} ≅ (χ_pγ_v ∗; 0 γ_v). (The proof gives γ_v² = ψ_v. Remark: γ_v(Frob_v) is the inverse of the eigenvalue of a uniformiser of D_v^× acting on such f.)
items.locator: §7.1, Lemma 7.2 and Remark, pp. 60–61, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.4/quaternionic-sigma-place-local-form states it, including γ_v² = ψ_v and the Remark; used by GL2ModularityLifting:R22.1/hecke-points-local-conditions. For p > 2 the independence of γ_v from f is not proved when N(v) ≡ −1 mod p and ρ̄_𝔪 is unramified at v (source issue); the node inherits this.

items.name: §7.2, (6): the isotropy group modulo its norm-one part
items.statement: Let U be compact and V = ∏_{v<∞} 𝒪_{F_v}^×; D^{det=1} denotes the elements of reduced norm 1. For every t = ∏_v t_v ∈ (D ⊗_F 𝔸_F^∞)^× there is an exact sequence 0 → (UV ∩ t^{-1}D^{det=1}t)/{±1} → (U(𝔸_F^∞)^× ∩ t^{-1}D^×t)/F^× → (((𝔸_F^∞)^×)²V ∩ F^×)/(F^×)², the second map induced by the reduced norm.
items.locator: §7.2, display (6), p. 61, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R18.3 ('Compute stabilisers'); R18.6 exports 'stabiliser hypotheses used by KW II §§7–9'; the GL2ModularityLifting--R22.1 packet requests 'the isotropy groups and their Sylow exponents (KW II §7.2)' from R18.6 (open). No node states (6).

items.name: §7.2, (7): the norm quotient is an extension of H[2] by units mod squares
items.statement: 0 → 𝒪_F^×/(𝒪_F^×)² → (((𝔸_F^∞)^×)²V ∩ F^×)/(F^×)² → H[2] → 0 is exact, where H is the class group of 𝒪_F. In particular (((𝔸_F^∞)^×)²V ∩ F^×)/(F^×)² is finite of exponent 2.
items.locator: §7.2, display (7), p. 61, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Part of the §7.2 stabiliser computation requested from R18.6 (planned there as 'stabiliser hypotheses'); no node states it. Mathlib has finiteness of the class group and finite generation of 𝒪_F^×, but not this sequence.

items.name: §7.2: finiteness of UV ∩ t^{-1}D^{det=1}t and the Sylow exponent bound 2N_w (U compact)
items.statement: Let U be compact and w a finite place of F not above p (e.g. one at which D splits), N_w = #GL₂(k_w). Then UV ∩ t^{-1}D^{det=1}t is a finite group, and the p-part of its order is bounded independently of t and U: tUVt^{-1} ∩ D^{det=1} is a discrete subgroup of the compact group tUVD_∞^{det=1}t^{-1} and maps injectively to t_wU_wV_wt_w^{-1}, which has a pro-q subgroup (q ≠ p a prime) of index bounded independently of t_w and U_w. Consequently the exponent of a Sylow p-subgroup of the finite groups (U(𝔸_F^∞)^× ∩ t^{-1}D^×t)/F^× divides 2N_w.
items.locator: §7.2, pp. 61–62, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: As for (6): stabiliser computations of R18.3, exported by R18.6 for KW II §§7–9. GL2ModularityLifting:R22.2/auxiliary-level-groups uses the resulting integer N.

items.name: §7.2: relative index of intersected subgroups (group-theoretic fact)
items.statement: If G, H, K are subgroups of a group G₀ and H is normal and of finite index in G, then H ∩ K is normal in G ∩ K and [G ∩ K : H ∩ K] divides [G : H].
items.locator: §7.2, p. 62, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Work in the group G with K replaced by K ⊓ G: Subgroup.relIndex_dvd_index_of_normal ([H.Normal] → H.relIndex K ∣ H.index, Mathlib/GroupTheory/Index.lean:154) is [G ∩ K : H ∩ K] ∣ [G : H], and Subgroup.Normal.subgroupOf (Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Basic.lean:981) gives normality of H ∩ K in G ∩ K.

items.name: §7.2: the Sylow exponent bound 4N_w for non-compact U (p = 2)
items.statement: In the non-compact cases considered (p = 2), with U⁰ = ∏_v U⁰_v the maximal compact subgroup of U: U⁰(𝔸_F^∞)^× is normal of finite index in U(𝔸_F^∞)^× with quotient of type (2, …, 2); hence (U⁰(𝔸_F^∞)^× ∩ t^{-1}D^×t)/F^× is normal of finite index in (U(𝔸_F^∞)^× ∩ t^{-1}D^×t)/F^×, with quotient of type (2, …, 2), and the exponent of a Sylow p-subgroup of (U(𝔸_F^∞)^× ∩ t^{-1}D^×t)/F^× divides 4N_w.
items.locator: §7.2, p. 62, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Requested with the rest of §7.2 from R18.6 ('the p = 2 extension of W_2 to non-compact U' and 'the isotropy groups and their Sylow exponents'); no node states it.

items.name: Lemma 7.3(1): Sylow exponent of isotropy groups after a base change split at w
items.statement: Let w be a place of F of residue characteristic different from p at which D is split, N_w = #GL₂(k_w), and F′/F a totally real finite extension completely split at w. Let D_{F′} = D ⊗_F F′ and let U_{F′} = ∏_r U_{F′,r} be a subgroup of (D_{F′} ⊗_{F′} 𝔸_{F′}^∞)^× as fixed at the beginning of §7 (with F′ in place of F). Then the exponent of the Sylow p-subgroup of the isotropy groups (U_{F′}(𝔸_{F′}^∞)^× ∩ t^{-1}D_{F′}^×t)/F′^× divides 4N_w for every t ∈ (D_{F′} ⊗_{F′} 𝔸_{F′}^∞)^×.
items.locator: §7.3, Lemma 7.3(1), p. 62, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proved in §7.2; covered by the stabiliser computations of R18.3 exported by R18.6. No node states it.

items.name: Lemma 7.3(2): a p-power character of ∏k_{v′}^× killing all isotropy groups
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma 7.3(1), let {v} be a finite set of finite places of F, not above p, at which D is split, and {v′} the places of F′ above them. Assume that for every v′ the order of the p-subgroup of k_{v′}^× is divisible by the p-part of 2p(4N_w), and that U_{F′,v′} = {g ∈ GL₂(𝒪_{F′_{v′}}) : g ≡ (∗ ∗; 0 ∗) mod π_{v′}}. A character χ = ∏_{v′}χ_{v′} of ∏_{v′}k_{v′}^× is regarded as a character of ∏_{v′}U_{F′,v′}, hence of U_{F′}, via the map ∏_{v′}U_{F′,v′} → ∏_{v′}k_{v′}^× with kernel ∏_{v′}{g ≡ (a b; 0 d) mod π_{v′}, ad^{-1} = 1}; it is trivial on U_{F′} ∩ (𝔸_{F′}^∞)^× and extends to U_{F′}(𝔸_{F′}^∞)^× by being trivial on (𝔸_{F′}^∞)^×. Then there is a character χ = ∏_{v′}χ_{v′} of ∏_{v′}k_{v′}^× of p-power order, with each χ_{v′} non-trivial (of order divisible by 4 when p = 2), which, regarded as a character of U_{F′}(𝔸_{F′}^∞)^×, annihilates (U_{F′}(𝔸_{F′}^∞)^× ∩ t^{-1}D_{F′}^×t)/F′^× for every t ∈ (D_{F′} ⊗_{F′} 𝔸_{F′}^∞)^×.
items.locator: §7.3, Lemma 7.3(2), pp. 62–63, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Only at stage level: R18.6 exports 'stabiliser hypotheses used by KW II §§7–9'. No node states it, and its consumer (Theorem 8.2) is not planned.

items.name: §7.4: the integer N, the groups Δ_v, Δ_Q and the levels U_Q ⊂ U′_Q
items.statement: N (a power of p) is the least common multiple of the exponents of the Sylow p-subgroups of the finite groups (U(𝔸_F^∞)^× ∩ t^{-1}D^×t)/F^×, t ∈ (D ⊗_F 𝔸_F^∞)^× (it exists by §7.2). Let n ≥ 1 and Q = {v} a finite set of places of F disjoint from S with N(v) ≡ 1 mod p^n for v ∈ Q. Δ′_v is the pro-p quotient of the cyclic group k_v^× = (𝒪_{F_v}/π_v)^×, and Δ_v is the quotient of Δ′_v by its N-torsion; so every character Δ_v → 𝒪^×, viewed as a character of Δ′_v, is an N-th power. U_Q = ∏_v(U_Q)_v and U′_Q = ∏_v(U′_Q)_v are subgroups of U with the same local components as U outside Q, and for v ∈ Q: (U_Q)_v = {g ∈ GL₂(𝒪_{F_v}) : g ≡ (a b; 0 d) mod π_v, ad^{-1} ↦ 1 ∈ Δ_v} and (U′_Q)_v = {g ∈ GL₂(𝒪_{F_v}) : g ≡ (∗ ∗; 0 ∗) mod π_v}. There is a natural isomorphism U′_Q/U_Q ≅ ∏_v Δ_v =: Δ_Q, through which characters of Δ_Q are regarded as characters of U′_Q.
items.locator: §7.4, p. 63, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.2/auxiliary-level-groups states this (writing U⁰_Q for U′_Q).

items.name: §7.4: the operators ⟨g⟩, U_v, S_v at Q and the Hecke algebra 𝕋_{ψ,Q}(U_Q)
items.statement: S_{k,ψ}(U_Q, 𝒪) carries an action of Δ_Q and of the operators U_{π_v}, S_{π_v} for v ∈ Q: g ∈ Δ_v acts by ⟨g⟩, the double coset U_Q(g̃ 0; 0 1)U_Q with g̃ a lift of g to 𝒪_{F_v}^×; S_v (multiplication by ψ(π_v)) and U_v are the double cosets U_Q(π_v 0; 0 π_v)U_Q and U_Q(π_v 0; 0 1)U_Q (they may depend on π_v). The extended (commutative) Hecke algebra 𝕋_{ψ,Q}(U_Q) is generated over 𝕋_ψ(U_Q) by these operators and Δ_Q.
items.locator: §7.4, p. 63, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.2/auxiliary-hecke-algebra.

items.name: §7.4: the twisted weight module W_k(χ) and the space S_{W_k(χ),ψ}(U′_Q, 𝒪)
items.statement: A character χ : Δ_Q → 𝒪^× induces a character of U′_Q that is trivial on U′_Q ∩ (𝔸_F^∞)^×, and is extended to U′_Q(𝔸_F^∞)^× by being trivial on (𝔸_F^∞)^×. W_k(χ) = W_k ⊗_𝒪 𝒪(χ) as U′_Q(𝔸_F^∞)^×-module, and S_{W_k(χ),ψ}(U′_Q, 𝒪) is the space of continuous functions f : D^×∖(D ⊗_F 𝔸_F^∞)^× → W_k(χ) with f(gu) = u^{-1}f(g) and f(gz) = ψ(z)f(g) for all g ∈ (D ⊗_F 𝔸_F^∞)^×, u ∈ U′_Q, z ∈ (𝔸_F^∞)^×.
items.locator: §7.4, p. 64, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: A special case of S_{τ,ψ} (R18.3 'with their weight module'); no node names W_k(χ).

items.name: §7.4, proof of Lemma 7.4, first claim: characters of Δ_Q kill the isotropy groups
items.statement: Every character χ of Δ_Q (of p-power order), regarded as a character of U′_Q(𝔸_F^∞)^×, kills (U′_Q(𝔸_F^∞)^× ∩ t^{-1}D^×t)/F^× for every t ∈ (D ⊗_F 𝔸_F^∞)^×: on this group χ is an N-th power, and N is divisible by the exponent of its Sylow p-subgroups.
items.locator: §7.4, proof of Lemma 7.4, p. 64, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R18.3 ('Compute stabilisers and prove freeness over Taylor–Wiles group rings under the actual hypotheses'); no node states it.

items.name: §7.4, (8): the isotropy groups at levels U′_Q and U_Q coincide
items.statement: For each t ∈ (D ⊗_F 𝔸_F^∞)^×, (U′_Q(𝔸_F^∞)^× ∩ t^{-1}D^×t)/F^× = (U_Q(𝔸_F^∞)^× ∩ t^{-1}D^×t)/F^×. (Proof: the quotient of the two injects into U′_Q(𝔸_F^∞)^×/U_Q(𝔸_F^∞)^× ≅ Δ_Q, and by the first claim every character of Δ_Q is trivial on it.)
items.locator: §7.4, display (8), p. 64, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Stabiliser input to freeness (R18.3); no node states it.

items.name: Lemma 7.4(1): rank and reduction of S_{W_k(χ),ψ}(U′_Q, 𝒪) are independent of χ
items.statement: The rank of the 𝒪-module S_{W_k(χ),ψ}(U′_Q, 𝒪) is independent of the character χ of Δ_Q, and for characters χ, χ′ of Δ_Q there is a Hecke-equivariant isomorphism S_{W_k(χ),ψ}(U′_Q, 𝒪) ⊗_𝒪 𝔽 ≅ S_{W_k(χ′),ψ}(U′_Q, 𝒪) ⊗_𝒪 𝔽.
items.locator: §7.4, Lemma 7.4(1), p. 64 (proof pp. 64–65), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R18.3 plans freeness over Taylor–Wiles group rings; the GL2ModularityLifting--R22.1 packet requests 'the freeness criterion (KW II Lemma 7.4, Gee Proposition 5.4(2))' from R18.6 (open). No node states Lemma 7.4. Also used in the proof of Theorem 8.2.

items.name: Lemma 7.4(2): S_{k,ψ}(U_Q, 𝒪) is free over 𝒪[Δ_Q]
items.statement: S_{k,ψ}(U_Q, 𝒪) is a free 𝒪[Δ_Q]-module of rank equal to the rank of S_{k,ψ}(U′_Q, 𝒪) as an 𝒪-module.
items.locator: §7.4, Lemma 7.4(2), p. 64 (proof p. 65), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R18.3 ('prove freeness over Taylor–Wiles group rings under the actual hypotheses. A finite set of cosets does not by itself make the module free'). Requested from R18.6 by GL2ModularityLifting--R22.1 (open).

items.name: §7.4: the maximal ideal 𝔪 at auxiliary level (U_v − α̃_v ∈ 𝔪)
items.statement: Let 𝔪 be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal of 𝕋_ψ(U) such that for v ∈ Q the eigenvalues α_v, β_v of ρ̄_𝔪(Frob_v) are distinct, and let Q′ ⊂ Q. By Hensel's lemma X² − T_vX + N(v)ψ(π_v) ∈ 𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪[X] splits as (X − A_v)(X − B_v) with A_v ≡ α_v and B_v ≡ β_v mod 𝔪. 𝔪 is pulled back to a maximal ideal of 𝕋_{ψ,Q′}(U_{Q′}) or 𝕋_{ψ,Q′}(U′_{Q′}), again denoted 𝔪, by declaring U_v − α̃_v ∈ 𝔪 for v ∈ Q′, α̃_v some lift of α_v; this is possible by Lemma 1.6(2) of [59].
items.locator: §7.4, before Corollary 7.5, p. 65, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.2/auxiliary-hecke-algebra states the Hensel factorisation and 𝔪_Q ∋ U_v − α̃_v. Hensel's lemma itself is in Mathlib (separate item); [59] Lemma 1.6(2) is quoted, not stated in a node.

items.name: §7.4: the level-raising maps ξ_v(f) = A_v f − (1 0; 0 π_v)f
items.statement: Let v ∈ Q∖Q′. Since 𝕋′_{ψ,Q′}(U′_{Q′})_{𝔪′} → 𝕋_{ψ,Q′}(U′_{Q′})_𝔪 is an isomorphism (𝕋′ defined without T_v, 𝔪′ the preimage of 𝔪), S_{k,ψ}(U′_{Q′})_{𝔪′} → S_{k,ψ}(U′_{Q′})_𝔪 is an isomorphism. The matrix (1 0; 0 π_v) defines a map S_{k,ψ}(U′_{Q′})_{𝔪′} → S_{k,ψ}(U′_{Q′∪{v}})_{𝔪′} (𝔪′ also denoting the maximal ideal above it in the Hecke algebra of U′_{Q′∪{v}} defined without U_v). Hence ξ_v(f) = A_v f − (1 0; 0 π_v)f, composed with localisation at 𝔪, defines a map S_{k,ψ}(U′_{Q′}, 𝒪)_𝔪 → S_{k,ψ}(U′_{Q′∪{v}}, 𝒪)_𝔪.
items.locator: §7.4, p. 65, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R22.2 stage: 'specialisation back to the original level'; the maps are the proof of GL2ModularityLifting:R22.2/delta-freeness-at-taylor-wiles-level and are not a separate node.

items.name: Corollary 7.5(a): S_{k,ψ}(U_Q, 𝒪)_𝔪 is free over 𝒪[Δ_Q] of the rank of S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪)_𝔪
items.statement: With 𝔪 as above (non-Eisenstein, α_v ≠ β_v for v ∈ Q), S_{k,ψ}(U_Q, 𝒪)_𝔪 is a free 𝒪[Δ_Q]-module, and its rank as an 𝒪[Δ_Q]-module is the rank of S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪)_𝔪 as an 𝒪-module.
items.locator: §7.4, Corollary 7.5, p. 65 (proof pp. 65–66), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.2/delta-freeness-at-taylor-wiles-level states it.

items.name: Corollary 7.5(b): Δ_Q-coinvariants recover level U (control)
items.statement: The Δ_Q-coinvariants of S_{k,ψ}(U_Q, 𝒪)_𝔪 are isomorphic to S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪)_𝔪, compatibly with a map 𝕋_{ψ,Q}(U_Q)_𝔪 → 𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪 sending T_v ↦ T_v for v ∉ S ∪ Q, ⟨g⟩ ↦ 1 for g ∈ Δ_Q and U_v ↦ A_v for v ∈ Q. (The proof shows S_{k,ψ}(U′_Q, 𝒪)_𝔪 ≅ S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪)_𝔪 via the composite of the ξ_v, v ∈ Q: it is an isomorphism after inverting p because no automorphic representation of (D ⊗_F 𝔸_F)^× that is a twist of Steinberg at a place of Q gives rise to ρ̄_𝔪, and it is surjective because, by Lemma 7.1, its reduction modulo the maximal ideal of 𝒪 is injective.)
items.locator: §7.4, Corollary 7.5 and proof, pp. 65–66, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.2/delta-freeness-at-taylor-wiles-level states it; GEE-MLT-2022 Proposition 5.8(2)/5.9 is cited there as the modern form.

items.name: §7.5: twisting quaternionic forms by quadratic characters, f_χ(g) = f(g)χ(Nm g) (p = 2)
items.statement: Let p = 2, Q_n a set of auxiliary primes as in Lemma 5.10 (notation of §5.6), with n such that 2^n > N (N as in §7.4). F^S_{Q_n} is the maximal abelian extension of F of 2-power degree unramified outside Q_n and split at the primes in S, G_n = Gal(F^S_{Q_n}/F) and G_{n,2} = G_n/2G_n. A character χ : G_{n,2} → 𝒪^× of order 2 is split at the infinite places, so is also a character of (𝔸_F^∞)^×. For f ∈ S_{k,ψ}(U_{Q_n}, 𝒪) (so k = 2) put f_χ(g) := f(g)χ(Nm(g)); then f_χ ∈ S_{k,ψ}(U_{Q_n}, 𝒪), since χ(Nm(z)) = 1 for z ∈ (𝔸_F^∞)^× (χ has order 2) and χ(Nm(u)) = 1 for u ∈ U_{Q_n} (for v ∈ Q_n and u_v ∈ (U_{Q_n})_v, det(u_v) = Nm(u_v) is a square in k_v^×). χ is also regarded as a character of Δ_{Q_n} via the map Δ_{Q_n} → G_{n,2} sending a generator of Δ_v (a non-trivial cyclic 2-group, as 2^n > N) to a generator of an inertia group of G_{n,2} above v.
items.locator: §7.5, p. 66, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.2/dyadic-twists-of-forms states it; R18.3 plans 'KW II's dyadic twisting construction'.

items.name: Proposition 7.6(1): the twist f ↦ f_χ and the operators T_v, U_v
items.statement: (p = 2, Q = Q_n.) For T_v ∈ 𝕋_{ψ,Q}(U_Q) with v a place not in S and π_v a uniformiser at v: (i) f_χ|T_v = χ(π_v)(f|T_v)_χ for v ∉ Q; (ii) f_χ|U_v = χ(π_v)(f|U_v)_χ for v ∈ Q (well defined, as for v ∈ Q the operator U_v depends on the choice of π_v).
items.locator: §7.5, Proposition 7.6(1), pp. 66–67, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.2/dyadic-twists-of-forms states both formulas.

items.name: Proposition 7.6(2): the twist f ↦ f_χ and the diamond operators
items.locator: §7.5, Proposition 7.6(2), p. 67, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.2/dyadic-twists-of-forms.

items.name: §7.5: the action of Hom(G_{n,2}, 𝒪^×) on 𝕋_{ψ,Q_n}(U_{Q_n})_𝔪 and S_{k,ψ}(U_{Q_n}, 𝒪)_𝔪
items.statement: χ ∈ Hom(G_{n,2}, 𝒪^×) acts on 𝕋_{ψ,Q_n}(U_{Q_n}) by T_v ↦ χ(π_v)T_v, U_v ↦ χ(π_v)U_v, h ↦ χ(h)h, S_v ↦ S_v, compatibly with its action f ↦ f_χ on S_{k,ψ}(U_{Q_n}, 𝒪). As χ(σ) ≡ 1 mod 𝔪 for σ ∈ G_{n,2}, this action preserves the maximal ideal 𝔪 of §7.4, giving actions on 𝕋_{ψ,Q_n}(U_{Q_n})_𝔪 and S_{k,ψ}(U_{Q_n}, 𝒪)_𝔪 satisfying the compatibilities of Proposition 7.6.
items.locator: §7.5, after Proposition 7.6, p. 67, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.2/dyadic-twists-of-forms (compatibility with the twisting action on R̄^ψ_{S∪Q_n}, GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.4/twisting-action).

items.name: Lemma 7.7: local–global compatibility at p for Hilbert modular forms (Kisin [39], Saito [53])
items.statement: Let F be a totally real number field unramified at p and π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(𝔸_F) that is discrete series of (parallel) weight k ≥ 2 at the infinite places. Let ρ_π : G_F → GL₂(E) be the Galois representation associated to π and assume that it is residually absolutely irreducible. Then the association π ↦ ρ_π is compatible with the Langlands–Fontaine correspondence. (The corollary in the introduction to [39], extending results of [53].)
items.locator: §7.6.1, Lemma 7.7, p. 67, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.5/hilbert-local-behaviour-at-p states Lemma 7.7 and Corollary 7.8 (Kisin's corollary quoted, not read).

items.name: Corollary 7.8(i): unramified π_v gives crystalline ρ_π|_{D_v}
items.statement: Let v be a place of F above p. If π_v is unramified, then ρ_π|_{D_v} is crystalline of weight k; if moreover π_v is ordinary, then ρ_π|_{I_v} ≅ (χ_p^{k−1} ∗; 0 1).
items.locator: §7.6.1, Corollary 7.8(i), p. 67, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.5/hilbert-local-behaviour-at-p, case (i).

items.name: Corollary 7.8(ii): U₁(v)-level π_v gives potentially Barsotti–Tate ρ_π|_{D_v}
items.statement: (k = 2) Let v | p. If π_v^{U₁(v)} ≠ 0 but π_v^{U₀(v)} = 0, and the corresponding character of k_v^× factors through the norm to 𝔽_p^×, then ρ_π|_{D_v} is of weight 2 and crystalline over ℚ_p^{nr}(μ_p). If moreover π_v is ordinary, then ρ_π|_{I_v} is printed as (ω_p^{k−2}χ_p ∗; 0 1); since k = 2 here, the exponent must be read as that of the (non-trivial) character of k_v^× (the nebentypus at v), cf. source issue.
items.locator: §7.6.1, Corollary 7.8(ii), p. 68, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.5/hilbert-local-behaviour-at-p, case (ii), already states the corrected reading ('χ_p times the finite character of inertia given by the nebentypus at v'); its README notes the clash of k.

items.name: Corollary 7.8 (Steinberg case): semistable non-crystalline ρ_π|_{D_v}
items.statement: (In weight 2.) Let v | p. If π_v^{U₀(v)} ≠ 0 but π_v has no invariants under GL₂(𝒪_v) (hence π_v is an unramified twist of Steinberg), then ρ_π|_{D_v} is semistable, non-crystalline of weight 2, i.e. ρ_π|_{D_v} ≅ (χ_pγ_v ∗; 0 γ_v) with γ_v an unramified character of D_v. (Unramified twists of Steinberg representations of GL₂(F_v) are also called Steinberg.)
items.locator: §7.6.1, Corollary 7.8, last case, p. 68, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.5/hilbert-local-behaviour-at-p, case (iii).

items.name: Definition 7.9: allowable base change
items.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝔽) be continuous, absolutely irreducible and totally odd, and F a totally real number field unramified at p and split at p if ρ̄|_{D_p} is irreducible, such that ρ̄|_F has non-solvable image when p = 2 and ρ̄|_{F(μ_p)} is absolutely irreducible when p > 2. A totally real solvable extension F′/F of even degree, unramified at the places above p, split at the places above p if ρ̄|_{D_p} is irreducible, such that im(ρ̄) = im(ρ̄|_{F′}) and ρ̄|_{F′(μ_p)} is absolutely irreducible, is an allowable base change. (The image condition should read im(ρ̄|_F) = im(ρ̄|_{F′}); see source issue.)
items.locator: §7.6.2, Definition 7.9, p. 68, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.4/alpha-beta-from-residual-modularity paraphrases it ('solvable, totally real, unramified or split at p as required') and R24.4/kw-theorem-4-1 and GL2ModularityLifting:R22.1/minimal-level-data use it; GL2ModularityLifting:R22.5/solvable-base-change-reduction states the existence of such extensions. No node states the definition in full.

items.name: §7.6.2: a sufficient condition for preserving the image and cyclotomic irreducibility
items.statement: A totally real extension F′/F has im(ρ̄) = im(ρ̄|_{F′}) and ρ̄|_{F′(μ_p)} absolutely irreducible if (i) it is linearly disjoint from the fixed field of the kernel of ρ̄|_F, and (ii) in case the projective image of ρ̄|_F is dihedral, F′/F is split at a prime of F that is split in the fixed field of the kernel of the projective image of ρ̄|_F but inert in F(μ_p). (Here too im(ρ̄) should read im(ρ̄|_F).)
items.locator: §7.6.2, p. 68, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.5/solvable-base-change-reduction asserts that linear disjointness keeps non-solvable image and absolute irreducibility over F′(ζ_p); the dihedral criterion (ii) is not stated. See also PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.1/forcing-linear-disjointness-by-extra-split-places.

items.name: Lemma 7.10: matching determinants after twisting and solvable base change
items.statement: Suppose ψ, ψ′ : F^×∖(𝔸_F^∞)^× → 𝒪^× are characters with the same reduction whose restrictions to an open subgroup of 𝒪_{F_p}^× are equal, and let {v} be a finite set of finite places of F at which the restrictions of ψ, ψ′ to (𝒪_F)_v^× are equal. Then, after enlarging 𝒪 if necessary, there are a finite-order character ζ : F^×∖(𝔸_F^∞)^× → 𝒪^× of p-power order, unramified at {v}, and a totally real solvable extension F′/F, which can be made disjoint from any given finite extension of F and is split at all places of {v}, such that the characters ζ|²_{F′}ψ_{F′} and ψ′_{F′} of F′^×∖(𝔸_{F′}^∞)^× are equal. (For p > 2 one may take F′ = F.)
items.locator: §7.6.3, Lemma 7.10, p. 69, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2/R02.4 (route 4), beside the square-root-after-base-change arguments of PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21/189, PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/84 and PAPER-ALLEN-ETAL-23/328. Their local conditions differ from KW's, but the Grunwald–Wang input (/210) is the same (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/2). GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/change-of-determinant states the p > 2 content (a residually trivial character is the square of a residually trivial one). Its hypothesis says that Lemma 7.10 'stays with its consumer (GL2ModularityLifting)', but the consumer is Theorem 8.2 (p. 73, /257) at SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.6. R02.2 precedes R20.6, and R02.4 → R20.6 closes no cycle. The former route to GL2ModularityLifting R22.1, downstream of R20.6, closed one (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/1). The p = 2 case needs Grunwald–Wang (/210; excluded from the Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory roadmap) and a Chebotarev choice of places w (TauCeti's Chebotarev roadmap, in progress).

items.name: Lemma 8.1: a solvable totally real field over which ρ̄ is unramified outside p
items.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝔽) be the fixed representation of S-type, with 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1 if p > 2, non-solvable image if p = 2, and ρ̄|_{ℚ(μ_p)} irreducible if p > 2. There is a totally real field F such that: F/ℚ is solvable; [F : ℚ] is even, F is unramified at p, and F is split at p if ρ̄|_{D_p} is irreducible or if k(ρ̄) = p + 1 (hence p > 2); ρ̄_F := ρ̄|_{G_F} has non-solvable image if p = 2 and ρ̄|_{G_{F(μ_p)}} is irreducible if p > 2; ρ̄_F is unramified at the places not above p; and if ρ̄|_{D_p} is unramified, then ρ̄|_{D_℘} is trivial for all places ℘ of F above p. (Proof omitted in the paper as easy.)
items.locator: §8.1, Lemma 8.1, p. 70, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.5/solvable-base-change-reduction (Gee Proposition 4.25/Fact 4.27, after Taylor [60] Lemma 2.2) gives solvable totally real extensions with prescribed completions, linearly disjoint from a given field, with [F′:ℚ] even, ρ̄ unramified away from p and prescribed splitting at p; triviality of ρ̄|_{D_℘} follows by prescribing an unramified completion at p. Requested from GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4.

items.name: §8.1: the arithmetic character ψ and its kinds (i), (ii), (iii) (with Diamond's Remark)
items.statement: Fix F as in Lemma 8.1 (notation of §1.2). ψ : F^×∖(𝔸_F^∞)^× → 𝒪^× is an arithmetic character, unramified outside the places above p, such that the Galois character χ_pρ_ψ : G_F → 𝒪^× (which is totally odd) lifts det ρ̄, and whose restriction to 𝒪_{F_p}^× is of one of the kinds: (i) u ↦ N(u)^{2−k(ρ̄)}; (ii) the character corresponding to ω_p^{k(ρ̄)−2}; (iii) when k(ρ̄) = 2, u ↦ N(u)^{1−p}. Remark (Diamond): these are not mutually exclusive — (i) and (ii) coincide if k(ρ̄) = 2; for p = 2 only (ii) is used. F and ψ are fixed for the rest of §8.
items.locator: §8.1, p. 70, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/kw-deformation-data and PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.1/auxiliary-totally-real-field-for-the-finiteness-argument take 'ψ as in KW II §8(.1)' by reference; no stage or node states the kinds (i)–(iii). Its consumers are Theorems 8.2 and 8.4 (SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.6), the GL2ModularityLifting R22 nodes and R24.1. It is routed to GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.6 (route 6), which supplies the deformation data of KW II §§8–10 and precedes R22.1 and R24.1; R04.6 → R20.6 closes no cycle. The former route to GL2ModularityLifting R22.1 lay downstream of its consumer R20.6 (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/1).

items.name: §8.2: the residual modularity hypotheses (α) and (β)
items.statement: (α) ρ̄|_{G_F} arises from a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL₂(𝔸_F) such that π_v is unramified for all v | p and π is discrete series of weight k(ρ̄) at the infinite places. (β) ρ̄|_{G_F} arises from a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL₂(𝔸_F) such that π_v, at all places v above p, is of conductor dividing v, and π is of weight 2 at the infinite places. Using the Jacquet–Langlands correspondence π is transferred to inner forms of GL₂ (and still called π).
items.locator: §8.2, p. 70, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.5/kw-residual-modularity states (α) and (β).

items.name: §8.2: verifying (α), (β) from modularity (Gross [27], Coleman–Voloch [12], Edixhoven [23]) or from Theorem 6.1
items.statement: For p > 2, and for p = 2 ((α) when k(ρ̄) = 2, (β) for k(ρ̄) = 2 and 4), the hypotheses (α) and (β) are verified, when ρ̄ is modular, by Theorem 13.10 of [27] and [12] (see also [23]) and Propositions 8.13 and 8.18 of [27]; when ρ̄ is not assumed modular but ρ̄_F is made modular by Theorem 6.1, that theorem verifies them.
items.locator: §8.2, p. 70, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.4/alpha-beta-from-residual-modularity states the derivation from modularity (Gross 13.10, Coleman–Voloch, Gross 8.13 and 8.18); its inputs are SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.3/companion-forms and R20.3/edixhoven-weight-theorem. The Theorem 6.1 route is PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.3/kw-ii-theorem-6-1-potential-modularity-of-rho-bar-over-a-controlled-F.

items.name: Theorem 8.2: minimal-at-p modular lifts and level lowering after allowable base change
items.statement: Let ρ̄, F, ψ and π be as above; assume (α) and (β) if p > 2, and if p = 2 that (α) holds if k(ρ̄) = 2 and (β) in general. Suppose π is as in: (p = 2) (α) when k(ρ̄) = 2, or as in (β); (p > 2) (α), or also (β) if k(ρ̄) = 2, in case (a) below, and (β) in cases (b) and (c) below. Let Σ be a subset of the finite places at which π is (an unramified twist of) Steinberg (so Σ contains no place above p when π is as in (α)); when π is as in (β) and k(ρ̄) = 2, assume Σ ⊇ {v | p : π_v Steinberg}. Then there are an allowable base change F″/F, split at p if p > 2, and a cuspidal automorphic representation π″ of GL₂(𝔸_{F″}), discrete series at infinity, such that: ρ_{π″} lifts ρ̄_{F″}; π″ is unramified (spherical) at all finite places not above Σ ∪ {p}, and Steinberg at the places above Σ; (p = 2) π″ has parallel weight 2, if k(ρ̄) = 2 then π″_v is unramified at all v | 2 with v ∉ Σ, if k(ρ̄) = 4 then π″_v is Steinberg at all v | 2, and π″ has central character ψ_{F″} (ψ of kind (ii)); moreover, for each place v of F above 2 and a chosen unramified square root ψ′_v of the unramified character ψ_v, when k(ρ̄) = 4 one may further ensure that the Hecke operator U_{v′} at the places v′ of F″ above v acts on π″ by ψ′_v ∘ N_{F″_{v′}/F_v}(π_{v′}), π_{v′} a chosen uniformiser; (p > 2) π″ can be chosen so that: (a) if ψ is of kind (i), π″ has parallel weight k(ρ̄) and is unramified at the places v | p not in Σ; (b) if ψ is of kind (ii) and k(ρ̄) < p + 1, π″_v has fixed vectors under U₁(v) for all v | p with associated character of k_v^× factoring through the norm to 𝔽_p^×, π″ has parallel weight 2 and central character ψ_{F″}; (c) (only when k(ρ̄) = p + 1) if ψ is of kind (ii), π″_v has fixed vectors under U₀(v) for all v | p, and π″ has parallel weight 2 and central character ψ_{F″}.
items.locator: §8.2, Theorem 8.2, p. 71 (proof pp. 72–73), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Requested from SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.6 by the GL2ModularityLifting--R22.1 packet together with Theorem 8.4 (open request); R20.6's text ('Supply the optimisation inputs used inside KW') does not state it, and the R20 nodes (Mazur, Ribet, Diamond, Buzzard, Edixhoven) are over ℚ and use modular curves, not definite quaternion algebras over totally real fields. PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.4 and R23.6 cite Theorem 8.2 as an input without stating it.

items.name: Theorem 8.2(a), weight p + 1 variant (not used in the paper)
items.statement: (p > 2, case (a).) When k(ρ̄) = 2 and Σ contains no place above p, π″ can also be chosen of weight p + 1, with central character ψ_{F″} for ψ of kind (iii), and unramified at all places above p. (Remark after Theorem 8.2: this statement, and hence Lemma 8.3, is not used in the paper.)
items.locator: §8.2, Theorem 8.2(a) and the Remark following it, p. 71; proof via Lemma 8.3, p. 73, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Not used in KW II; no stage or node states it.

items.name: Lemma 8.3: from weight 2 to weight p + 1 on definite quaternion algebras (mod p)
items.statement: Let U = ∏_v U_v be an open compact subgroup of (D_{F″} ⊗ 𝔸_{F″}^∞)^×, where D_{F″} is the definite quaternion algebra over F″ unramified at all finite places not above Σ, Σ ∩ {v | p} = ∅, and U_v = GL₂(𝒪_{F_v}) for the places v above p. Let ψ : (𝔸_{F″}^∞)^× → 𝔽^× be a continuous character with ψ|_{U∩(𝔸_{F″}^∞)^×} = 1. If ρ̄_{F″} arises from a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra (outside p) acting on S_{2,ψ}(U, 𝔽), then it also arises from a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra (outside p) acting on S_{p+1,ψ}(U, 𝔽).
items.locator: §8.2, Lemma 8.3, p. 73 (proof pp. 73–74), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof: the group-cohomological argument of Edixhoven–Khare [24] §4 Proposition 1, iterated over the places above p, with Lemma 7.1. No stage plans weight raising for quaternionic forms; SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.3 treats Edixhoven's weight theorem over ℚ, and PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R23.3/taylor-2006-lemma-5-3-weight-shift is a different (cyclotomic-twist) weight shift.

items.name: Proof of Lemma 8.3: 𝔽[ℙ¹(k_w)] ≅ 𝟙 ⊕ V and the resulting splitting of S_{τ_i,ψ}(U″, 𝔽)
items.statement: Let w = w_{i+1} be a place of F″ above p with residue field k_w, J_w the embeddings F″ ↪ E corresponding to w, and V = ⊗_{ι∈J_w} Sym^{p−1}(𝔽²) as GL₂(k_w)-module. Then 𝔽[ℙ¹(k_w)], with the natural GL₂(k_w)-action, is isomorphic to 𝟙 ⊕ V (see [24]). Consequently, if U″ ⊂ U has U″_v = U_v for v ≠ w and U″_w = U₀(w), then S_{τ_i,ψ}(U″, 𝔽) ≅ S_{τ_i,ψ}(U, 𝔽) ⊕ S_{τ_i⊗V,ψ}(U, 𝔽), and f ↦ (1 0; 0 π_w)f followed by the projection gives a map S_{τ_i,ψ}(U, 𝔽)_𝔪 → S_{τ_{i+1},ψ}(U, 𝔽)_𝔪 that is injective by Lemma 7.1.
items.locator: §8.2, proof of Lemma 8.3, p. 74, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: The decomposition of the permutation module on ℙ¹(𝔽_q) into the trivial and Steinberg modules (Steinberg tensor product) is not in Mathlib or TauCeti, and no stage plans it for this use.

items.name: §8.3.1–8.3.2: lifting data — determinant and conditions away from p
items.statement: Lifting data for ρ̄|_{G_F} impose the determinant and local conditions at a finite set S of places of F containing the infinite places and the places above p (the lift has to be unramified outside S; oddness at infinity is implied by the determinant). 8.3.1: the determinant of the lifts is ψχ_p, ψ as chosen in §8.1. 8.3.2: at finitely many places v not above p (the ramified places of the lifting data) local lifts ρ̃_v of ρ̄|_{D_v} are given that are ramified and of the form (γ_vχ_p ∗; 0 γ_v) with γ_v a given unramified character and γ_v² = ψ_v; at all other places v not above p the lift is required to be unramified with determinant ψ_vχ_p.
items.locator: §8.3, 8.3.1–8.3.2, p. 74, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/kw-deformation-data (semistable lifts with a fixed unramified γ_v at finite v ∤ p, odd lifts at ∞); the local rings are requested from LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.6 (open).

items.name: §8.3.3: lifting data at p (types (A), (B), (C) and the dyadic cases)
items.statement: For all places v above p a lift ρ̃_v of ρ̄|_{D_v} with det(ρ̃_v) = ψ_vχ_p is given such that: (p = 2) ρ̃_v is crystalline of weight 2 at all primes above 2 when k(ρ̄) = 2, and when k(ρ̄) = 4, ρ̃_v is semistable, non-crystalline of weight 2 and of the form (γ_vχ₂ ∗; 0 γ_v), χ₂ the 2-adic cyclotomic character and γ_v a given unramified character with γ_v² = ψ_v; (p > 2) ρ̃_v is, simultaneously at all v | p, either (A) crystalline of weight k with 2 ≤ k ≤ p + 1, the case k = p + 1 considered only when F is split at p and k(ρ̄) = p + 1; or (B) crystalline of weight 2 over ℚ_p^{nr}(μ_p) with Weil–Deligne parameter (ω_p^{k−2} ⊕ 1, 0) for a fixed k in all embeddings; or (C) semistable, non-crystalline of weight 2 of the form (γ_vχ_p ∗; 0 γ_v), γ_v a given unramified character with γ_v² = ψ_v. For p = 2 only (A) in weight 2 is considered, (B) is not, and (C) only when ρ̄ has weight 4. In (A) ψ has to be of kind (i), in (B) of kind (ii) and in (C) of kind (ii).
items.locator: §8.3.3, pp. 74–75, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.5/kw-odd-prime-lifting and R22.6/kw-dyadic-lifting state (A), (B), (C) and the dyadic variants; GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/kw-deformation-data states the corresponding local rings (requested from LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.6). The kinds of ψ are not stated (see the §8.1 item).

items.name: §8.3.3: a lift fitting the lifting data
items.statement: A lift ρ_F : G_F → GL₂(𝒪) of ρ̄|_{G_F} fits the lifting data if ρ_F|_{D_v} is of type ρ̃_v at all places of S, ρ_F is unramified at the other places, and ψ = det(ρ_F)χ_p^{-1}.
items.locator: §8.3.3, p. 75, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/kw-deformation-data; PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.3/required-lift-types identifies such lifts with the 𝒪′-points of R̄^ψ_S.

items.name: Theorem 8.4: modular lifts with prescribed local properties, after allowable base change
items.statement: Assume (α) and (β) of §8.2 if p > 2, and if p = 2 that (α) is satisfied when k(ρ̄) = 2 and (β) is satisfied. There are an allowable base change F′/F and a cuspidal automorphic representation π′ of GL₂(𝔸_{F′}), discrete series at infinity of parallel weight, such that: ρ_{π′} is a lift of ρ̄_{F′}; (p = 2) ρ_{π′} is crystalline of weight 2 at all primes above 2 when k(ρ̄) = 2, and when k(ρ̄) = 4 it is semistable of weight 2 of the form prescribed in §8.3.3; (p > 2) at all places of F′ above p, ρ_{π′} is, corresponding to the cases (A), (B), (C) of the lifting data, either crystalline of weight k with 2 ≤ k ≤ p + 1 (when k = p + 1 is considered, F′ is split at p and k(ρ̄) = p + 1), or of weight 2 and crystalline over ℚ_p^{nr}(μ_p) with the prescribed inertial Weil–Deligne parameter as in (B), or as in (C) semistable non-crystalline of weight 2 with, for v | p, restriction to D_v of the form (γ_vχ_p ∗; 0 γ_v) (γ_v also denoting the restricted character); ρ_{π′} is unramified at the places where the lifting data is unramified; at all places not above p where the lifting data is ramified, ρ_{π′}|_{D_v} ≅ (γ_vχ_p ∗; 0 γ_v) with γ_v unramified; det ρ_{π′} = ψ_{F′}χ_p. Moreover, for p = 2, π′ is unramified at the places above 2 when k(ρ̄) = 2 and Steinberg there when k(ρ̄) = 4; for p > 2 one may ensure that π′ is unramified at the places above p in (A), that π′_v has fixed vectors under U₁(v) in (B), and under U₀(v) in (C).
items.locator: §8.4, Theorem 8.4, pp. 75–76 (proof pp. 76–78), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: The GL2ModularityLifting--R22.1 packet requests it from SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.6 (open), and GL2ModularityLifting:R22.1/minimal-level-data assumes a π fitting the lifting data; GL2ModularityLifting:R22.5/ordinary-overlap cites it. No stage or node states it. Nearest planned material: SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.2/level-raising-diamond (level raising over ℚ) and OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.2/ihara-lemma-quaternionic.

items.name: External: the Jacquet–Langlands correspondence (global, with local functoriality at Σ)
items.statement: For D a totally definite quaternion algebra over F ramified at a finite set Σ of finite places, there is a correspondence between the automorphic representations of (D ⊗_F 𝔸_F)^× (other than the one-dimensional ones) and the cuspidal automorphic representations of GL₂(𝔸_F) that are discrete series at the infinite places and at the places of Σ, compatible with the local correspondence at every place, including those in Σ (where a one-dimensional χ ∘ Nrd of D_v^× corresponds to χ·St). KW use it to identify S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪)_𝔪 with cusp forms (via [59] Lemma 1.3), in Lemma 7.2, Corollary 7.5, and to move π between GL₂ and its inner forms in §8.
items.locator: §7, p. 60; proof of Lemma 7.2, p. 61; §8.2, p. 70; proofs of Theorems 8.2 and 8.4, pp. 72–78, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.3 ('Prove global transfer and its converse … Supply the definite and indefinite cases needed by R18/R22') and R17.1 (local quaternionic transfer, one-dimensional characters/Steinberg twists). No node (the roadmap has no packet).

items.name: External: Galois representations of Hilbert modular forms and local–global compatibility away from p (Carayol [10], Taylor [61])
items.statement: To a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL₂(𝔸_F), F totally real, discrete series of parallel weight k ≥ 2 at infinity, is attached ρ_π : G_F → GL₂(E) ([10], [61]), compatible with the local Langlands correspondence at the finite places not above p; in particular, for π_v an unramified twist of Steinberg (v ∤ p), ρ_π|_{D_v} ≅ (χ_pγ_v ∗; 0 γ_v) with γ_v unramified, and for π_v unramified, ρ_π is unramified at v with ρ_π(Frob_v) of characteristic polynomial given by the Hecke eigenvalues.
items.locator: §7, p. 60; proofs of Lemma 7.2 (p. 61), Corollary 7.5 (p. 66) and Theorem 8.4 (p. 77), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.2/hilbert-modular-compatible-system-carayol-theorem-A (Carayol's Theorem (A), with his hypothesis of a discrete-series finite place when [F:ℚ] is even) and R19.2/carayol-special-places; R19.2's stage text covers 'the parity and auxiliary-place cases' ([61]), and R19.4 local–global compatibility away from p.

items.name: External: strong approximation for the norm-one group D¹
items.statement: Let w be a finite place at which D splits. The norm-one group D¹ is simply connected with D¹(F_w) ≅ SL₂(F_w) non-compact, so D¹(F)·D¹(F_w) is dense in D¹(𝔸_F^∞). Used in Lemma 7.1: a form invariant under U·SL₂(F_w) is invariant under right translation by D¹(𝔸_F^∞), hence factors through the reduced norm.
items.locator: §7, proof of Lemma 7.1, p. 60, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.4: 'Develop strong approximation for simply connected almost-simple groups outside S with the required noncompact local factor'. TauCeti has only function-field strong approximation (TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Consequences/StrongApproximation.lean).

items.name: External: Hensel's lemma (simple roots lift over complete local rings)
items.statement: If R is a Henselian (e.g. adically complete) local ring and f ∈ R[X] is monic with a root a₀ modulo the maximal ideal at which f′ is a unit, then f has a root a ≡ a₀. KW apply it to X² − T_vX + N(v)ψ(π_v) over 𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪 when the roots α_v, β_v of the reduction are distinct.
items.locator: §7.4, before Corollary 7.5, p. 65, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: HenselianLocalRing.is_henselian (Mathlib/RingTheory/Henselian.lean:108) is exactly this lifting property; the instance IsAdicComplete.henselianRing (same file, line 170, not in the declaration index) makes an I-adically complete ring Henselian at I. That 𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪 is complete (finite over 𝒪) is not a library statement.

items.name: External: Langlands' base change for GL₂ ([40])
items.statement: Cyclic, hence solvable, base change for GL₂ over totally real fields: for a totally real solvable extension F′/F and a cuspidal π of GL₂(𝔸_F) there is a base change π_{F′} with ρ_{π_{F′}} ≅ ρ_π|_{G_{F′}} (cuspidal when the residual representation stays absolutely irreducible), compatible with the local correspondence (Steinberg stays Steinberg, unramified stays unramified, tamely ramified principal series become unramified after suitable ramified base change). This is why the results of §8 may allow allowable base change.
items.locator: §7.6.2, p. 68; proofs of Theorems 8.2 and 8.4, pp. 72–78, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4: 'Prove cyclic base change and descent for GL₂, local compatibility and the exact failure-of-cuspidality criterion. Iterate to solvable extensions'.

items.name: External: global class field theory for characters
items.statement: The reciprocity isomorphism 𝔸_F^×/F^×(F_∞^×)⁰ ≅ G_F^{ab}, compatible with local class field theory normalised so that a uniformiser maps to an arithmetic Frobenius, identifies characters of F^×∖(𝔸_F^∞)^× with totally even Galois characters. Used to view χ : G_{n,2} → 𝒪^× as a character of (𝔸_F^∞)^× (§7.5) and ψψ′^{-1} as a Galois character (Lemma 7.10).
items.locator: §7.5, p. 66; proof of Lemma 7.10, p. 69, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: TauCeti ClassFieldTheory Layer 11 builds globalArtinMap with local compatibility and arithmetic-Frobenius normalisation.

items.name: External: solvable totally real extensions with prescribed local behaviour (Taylor [60], Lemma 2.2)
items.statement: Given a totally real field F, a finite set of places and prescribed local behaviour at them, there is a totally real solvable extension F′/F realising it, which can be chosen linearly disjoint from a given finite extension. In the proof of Theorem 8.2 it produces an allowable base change F′/F of even degree, split at Σ ∪ {v | p} ∪ {w}, such that at the places v′ above S the order of the p-subgroup of k_{v′}^× is divisible by the p-part of 2p(4N_w).
items.locator: §8.2, proof of Theorem 8.2, p. 72, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.5/solvable-base-change-reduction states it (Gee Fact 4.27, after Taylor's Lemma 2.2), requested from GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4 ('Prove the local prescribed splitting/base-change consequences').

items.name: External: neat levels (Taylor [59] Lemma 1.1)
items.statement: For levels U small enough at an auxiliary place (in the proof of Theorem 8.4, (U_i)_{r₀} = U(r₀) at the places above a prime r₀ ∉ Σ not above p), U has the neatness property of Lemma 1.1 of Taylor [59], which makes S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪) → S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝔽) surjective and gives the spaces of forms their perfect pairings.
items.locator: §8.2, proof of Theorem 8.2, p. 73; §8.4, proof of Theorem 8.4, p. 77, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: No stage or node states Taylor's neatness lemma or the surjectivity of reduction; HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:R18.3 plans stabiliser computations in general. Khare's Lemma 2.2, which KW use to assume the level of Lemma 8.3 is neat, is the separate item from §6.

items.name: External: Kisin [36], Corollary 3.1.11 (Ribet's level raising via Ihara's lemma) and Lemma 3.5.3 (quadratic towers and Jacquet–Langlands)
items.statement: KW prove Theorem 8.4 by the method of proof of Corollary 3.1.11 of [36] (Ribet's method of raising levels using Ihara's lemma) and of Lemma 3.5.3 of [36] (use of base change and Jacquet–Langlands). (1) Kisin [36], Corollary 3.1.11. Hypotheses: 𝔪 ⊂ 𝕋^univ_{S_p,𝒪} is a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal; S_{σ,ψ}(U, 𝒪)_𝔪 ≠ 0; and the level-raising congruence (T_λ² − (N(λ) + 1)²ψ(λ))S_{σ,ψ}(U, 𝒪) ⊂ 𝔪S_{σ,ψ}(U, 𝒪) holds at the new place λ. The set-up is that of Kisin §3.1: forms on a definite quaternion algebra, U′ ⊂ U with U′_λ = U₀(λ), and levels small enough for the spaces of forms to have their perfect pairings (KW secure this with the level U(r₀) at an auxiliary place r₀, p. 77). Conclusion: S_{σ,ψ}(U′, 𝒪)_𝔪 / i(S_{σ,ψ}(U, 𝒪)²_𝔪) is a non-zero free 𝒪-module, i being the degeneracy map. So ρ̄ arises from a π with U′-invariants that is Steinberg at λ. The Ihara input is separate: it is Kisin's (3.1.8), which gives the torsion-freeness, and for KW it is Lemma 7.1 (/222). That lemma shows that the p-torsion of the cokernel of S_{k,ψ}(U_i, 𝒪)² → S_{k,ψ}(U′_i, 𝒪) has only Eisenstein maximal ideals in its support (p. 77). KW leave the congruence at the place w_{i+1} of F_i above v_{i+1} (v_{i+1} not above p) implicit. It holds because ρ̄_F is unramified at the places not above p (Lemma 8.1, p. 70), and the lifting data at v_{i+1} have the form (γ_vχ_p ∗; 0 γ_v) with γ_v unramified. So ρ̄(Frob_w) has eigenvalues γ̄_v(Frob_w)N(w) and γ̄_v(Frob_w), with γ̄_v(Frob_w)² = ψ̄(w) since det ρ̄ = ψ̄χ̄_p. (2) Kisin [36], Lemma 3.5.3: a tower F = F₀ ⊂ F₁ ⊂ … ⊂ F_r of quadratic totally real extensions, in which the places above v_j are inert except at step j, where they split; with Jacquet–Langlands it adds Steinberg places in pairs. KW assert that in 3.1.11 Σ may contain the places above p in case (C) with k(ρ̄) = 2, and that the restriction to weight 2 may be replaced by 2 ≤ k ≤ p + 1.
items.locator: §8.4, proof of Theorem 8.4, pp. 76–77, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Routed with Theorem 8.4 to SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.6 (route 9). The former route to GL2ModularityLifting R22.4 lay downstream of R20.6 (R20.6 → R22.1 → R22.2 → R22.3 → R22.4) and closed a cycle (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/1). The GL2ModularityLifting--R22.1 packet requests Kisin's Annals (3.1.6), (3.5.2), (3.5.3) level/type changes from R20.6 (open); Corollary 3.1.11 is in no node. Its Ihara input, Lemma 7.1 (/222), is planned at HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.3–R18.6, upstream of R20.6. The classical analogue is SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.2/level-raising-diamond (over ℚ). The statement was corrected by RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/8. Kisin's hypotheses and conclusion follow the verifier's reading of Annals 170 (2009), p. 1151, and KW's use was re-read on pp. 76–77.

items.name: External: existence of the definite quaternion algebra with prescribed ramification
items.statement: If F is totally real and Σ is a finite set of finite places of F with [F : ℚ] + |Σ| even, there is a quaternion algebra over F, unique up to isomorphism, ramified exactly at the infinite places and at Σ. (Used as 'the definite quaternion algebra over F ramified at exactly the infinite places and Σ' after base changes making the parity right.)
items.locator: §8.2, proof of Theorem 8.2, p. 72; §8.4, proof of Theorem 8.4, p. 77, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: R17.3: 'Record the parity condition on the ramification set of a quaternion algebra'; existence is the right exactness of 0 → Br(F) → ⊕_v Br(F_v) → ℚ/ℤ → 0 (exists_br_of_sum_eq_zero, ClassFieldTheory Layer 10) plus period = index for number fields, which neither stage states for quaternion algebras.

items.name: §9 standing hypotheses (ρ̄, F, ψ, lifting data)
items.statement: Throughout §9, ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝔽) is the fixed representation of §8 (of S-type, 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1 if p > 2, non-solvable image if p = 2, ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ(μ_p)}} absolutely irreducible if p > 2), F is a totally real field as in Lemma 8.1, ρ̄_F := ρ̄|_{G_F}, ψ is the arithmetic character of §8.1 and lifting data are fixed as in §8.3. It is assumed that ρ̄_F satisfies (α) and (β) if p ≠ 2, (α) when p = k(ρ̄) = 2, and (β) if p = 2 (§8.2). After possibly an allowable base change (Definition 7.9), Theorem 8.4 gives a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL₂(𝔸_F) with ρ_π fitting the lifting data; when weight p + 1 liftings are considered (only when k(ρ̄) = p + 1) one may assume, by Theorems 6.1 and 8.4, that F is split at p.
items.locator: §9, opening paragraph, p. 78, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/kw-deformation-data states the data; GL2ModularityLifting:R22.1/minimal-level-data records π; R22.5/kw-residual-modularity states (α), (β). Propositions 9.2 and 9.3 assume exactly these conditions ('the conditions stated at the beginning of this section').

items.name: §9.1.1: minimal-level quaternionic data (Σ, S, D, U, 𝔪)
items.statement: Σ is the set of places of F not above p at which the lifting data is ramified, together with all places above p if the lifting data is in case (C) or if p = 2 and k(ρ̄) = 4; S := Σ ∪ {v | ∞} ∪ {v | p}. After an allowable base change, |Σ| and [F : ℚ] are even. D is the definite quaternion algebra over F ramified exactly at Σ and at all infinite places. U = ∏_v U_v ⊂ (D ⊗_F 𝔸_F^∞)^× with: U_v maximal compact for v ∉ S; U_v = (𝒪_D)_v^× (resp. D_v^× when p = 2) for v ∈ Σ; for v | p not in Σ, U_v maximal compact in case (A) (including p = k(ρ̄) = 2) and U_v = U_1(v) in case (B). When p = 2 (so k = 2), with U⁰ the maximal compact subgroup of U, the U⁰(𝔸_F^∞)^×-module W₂ is extended to U(𝔸_F^∞)^× in the unique way that allows an eigenform in S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪) with the Hecke eigenvalues of π at the places not in S. The existence of π gives a maximal ideal 𝔪 of the Hecke algebra 𝕋_ψ(U) acting on S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪).
items.locator: §9.1.1, pp. 78–79, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.1/minimal-level-data states exactly this datum (including D_v^× at Σ for p = 2 and the extended W₂); the spaces S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪) and 𝕋_ψ(U) are HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:R18.3.

items.name: §9.1.1: the deformation ring R̄^{□,ψ}_S of the lifting data
items.statement: R̄^{□,ψ}_S := R^{□,ψ}_S ⊗̂_{R^{□,loc,ψ}_S} R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S with R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S := ⊗̂_{v∈S} R̄^{□,ψ}_v, where R̄^{□,ψ}_v classifies (Definition 2.4) the lifts of ρ̄_F|_{D_v} of determinant ψχ_p prescribed by the lifting data: at finite v ∈ S not above p, semistable lifts (γ_vχ_p ∗; 0 γ_v) with a fixed choice of unramified character γ_v (§3.3.4); at the infinite places, odd lifts (§3.1); at the places above p, uniformly one of (A) low-weight crystalline lifts ((ii) of §3.2.2; including p = 2 in weight 2), (B) weight-2 lifts ((i) of §3.2.2; p > 2 and k(ρ̄) ≤ p), (C) weight-2 semistable lifts ((i) of §3.2.2; including p = 2, k(ρ̄) = 4). R̄^ψ_S ⊂ R̄^{□,ψ}_S is the image of the unframed ring R^ψ_S (Proposition 4.1), and R̄^{□,ψ}_S is a (formally) smooth R̄^ψ_S-algebra; the universal representation over R̄^ψ_S is denoted ρ̄^univ_S.
items.locator: §9.1.1, pp. 79–80, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/kw-deformation-data (local conditions, completed tensor product) and R04.6/trace-subring-universal-representation (R̄^ψ_S as trace subring, power series in 4|S| − 1 variables).

items.name: §9.1.1: properties of R̄^{□,ψ}_v and R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S (recalled)
items.statement: For v ∈ S, R̄^{□,ψ}_v is a domain, flat over 𝒪, of relative dimension 3 if v ∤ p∞, 3 + [F_v : ℚ_p] if v | p, and 2 if v is infinite, and R̄^{□,ψ}_v[1/p] is regular (when k(ρ̄) = p and ρ̄ is unramified at p, the domain property uses that (ρ̄_F)|_{D_v} is trivial, by Lemma 8.1; §3.2.5). Consequently R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S is flat over 𝒪, a domain, of relative dimension 3|S|, and R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S[1/p] is regular (Theorem 3.1, Proposition 3.2).
items.locator: §9.1.1, p. 79, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/kw-deformation-data states these properties; LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-completed-tensor-product and the other R08.6 export nodes prove them. Recalled from Theorem 3.1 and Proposition 3.2 (outside this range).

items.name: §9.1.1: the Galois representation ρ_𝔪 over the Hecke algebra
items.statement: Using the Galois representations attached to Hilbert modular eigenforms and the Jacquet–Langlands correspondence (as in §1 of [59]) one gets a continuous representation G_F → GL₂(𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪 ⊗_𝒪 E); since its traces lie in 𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪, Théorème 2 of [11] gives a model ρ_𝔪 : G_F → GL₂(𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪). It is characterised by the Eichler–Shimura relation: for v ∉ S, the characteristic polynomial of ρ_𝔪(Frob_v) (Frob_v the arithmetic Frobenius) is X² − T_vX + N(v)ψ(π_v). Its reduction ρ̄_𝔪 modulo 𝔪 is isomorphic to ρ̄_F, so there is a unique map π′ : R^ψ_S → 𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪 taking the universal representation ρ^univ_S to ρ_𝔪.
items.locator: §9.1.1, p. 80, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.6 (representations over Hecke algebras under residual absolute irreducibility) and GL2ModularityLifting:R22.1/deformation-to-hecke-map (the map characterised by traces of Frobenius).

items.name: Framed Hecke algebras 𝕋^□_ψ(U)_𝔪 and 𝕋^□_{ψ,Q_n}(U_{Q_n})_𝔪
items.statement: 𝕋^□_ψ(U)_𝔪 := 𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪 ⊗_{R̄^ψ_S} R̄^{□,ψ}_S and, for the Taylor–Wiles sets Q_n, 𝕋^□_{ψ,Q_n}(U_{Q_n})_𝔪 := 𝕋_{ψ,Q_n}(U_{Q_n}) ⊗_{R̄^ψ_{S∪Q_n}} R̄^{□,ψ}_{S∪Q_n}.
items.locator: §9.1.1, Lemma 9.1, p. 80; proof of Proposition 9.2, p. 81, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.1/framed-hecke-module; the level-Q_n version is used through R22.2/taylor-wiles-module-system.

items.name: Lemma 9.1 (1): the surjection R̄^ψ_S → 𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪
items.statement: The map π′ : R^ψ_S → 𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪 induces a surjective map π : R̄^ψ_S → 𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪 that takes the universal representation ρ̄^univ_S to ρ_𝔪.
items.locator: §9.1.1, Lemma 9.1, p. 80 (proof pp. 80–81), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.1/deformation-to-hecke-map and /deformation-to-hecke-surjective; GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/factorization-through-local-conditions is the factorisation step. Proof: every 𝒪′-point x of 𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪 gives ρ_x satisfying the local conditions (local–global compatibility [10], [61] and Lemma 7.2 away from p, Lemma 7.7 at p); 𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪 flat and reduced gives ∩ ker x = 0 (Corollary 2.3); surjectivity from the Eichler–Shimura relation.

items.name: Lemma 9.1 (2): the framed surjection R̄^{□,ψ}_S → 𝕋^□_ψ(U)_𝔪
items.statement: π induces a surjective map π : R̄^{□,ψ}_S → 𝕋^□_ψ(U)_𝔪 = 𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪 ⊗_{R̄^ψ_S} R̄^{□,ψ}_S.
items.locator: §9.1.1, Lemma 9.1, p. 80, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.1/deformation-to-hecke-surjective (π^□).

items.name: Lemma 9.1 (3): the map at Taylor–Wiles level R̄^ψ_{S∪Q_n} → 𝕋_{ψ,Q_n}(U_{Q_n})_𝔪
items.statement: Pull 𝔪 back to a maximal ideal, again denoted 𝔪, of the Hecke algebra 𝕋_{ψ,Q_n}(U_{Q_n}) acting on S_{k,ψ}(U_{Q_n}, 𝒪) as in §7.4, so that U_v − α̃_v ∈ 𝔪 for v ∈ Q_n, with α̃_v a lift of a fixed one of the two distinct eigenvalues of ρ̄_𝔪(Frob_v). Then there is a map R̄^ψ_{S∪Q_n} → 𝕋_{ψ,Q_n}(U_{Q_n})_𝔪, compatible with the 𝒪[Δ′_{Q_n}]-actions and, when p = 2, with the actions of Hom(G_{Q_n,2}, 𝒪^×) of §§5.1 and 7.5, characterised by tr(ρ̄^univ_{S∪Q_n}(Frob_v)) ↦ T_v for almost all v; it takes γ_{α_v}(π_v) to U_v for v ∈ Q_n (notation of Proposition 5.11).
items.locator: §9.1.1, Lemma 9.1 and its proof, pp. 80–81, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.2/auxiliary-hecke-algebra (the map, γ_{α_v}(π_v) ↦ U_v, compatibility with Δ′ and with twists for p = 2) and R22.2/delta-actions-agree.

items.name: 𝕋^□_ψ(U)_𝔪 is flat over 𝒪 and reduced
items.statement: Since R̄^{□,ψ}_S is formally smooth over R̄^ψ_S and 𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪 is flat over 𝒪 and reduced, 𝕋^□_ψ(U)_𝔪 is again flat over 𝒪 and reduced.
items.locator: §9.1.1, after Lemma 9.1, p. 80, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.1/framed-hecke-module (power series ring over 𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪 in 4|S| − 1 variables, 𝒪-flat and reduced).

items.name: Remark after Lemma 9.1: surjectivity at level Q_n and 𝕋_ψ(U_{Q_n})_𝔪 ≅ 𝕋_{ψ,Q_n}(U_{Q_n})_𝔪
items.statement: The map R̄^ψ_{S∪Q_n} → 𝕋_{ψ,Q_n}(U_{Q_n})_𝔪 is surjective. Moreover, as the traces of G_F → GL₂(𝕋_{ψ,Q_n}(U_{Q_n})_𝔪) lie in the image of 𝕋_ψ(U_{Q_n}) → 𝕋_{ψ,Q_n}(U_{Q_n})_𝔪, so that the representation is defined over that image (Théorème 2 of [11]), the natural map 𝕋_ψ(U_{Q_n})_𝔪 → 𝕋_{ψ,Q_n}(U_{Q_n})_𝔪 is bijective.
items.locator: §9.1.1, Remark after Lemma 9.1, p. 81, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.2/auxiliary-hecke-algebra states both the surjection and the bijectivity.

items.name: Proposition 9.2 (I): patched ring and module for p odd
items.statement: Let p ≠ 2 and assume the conditions stated at the beginning of §9. Let d = 3|S|, h = dim_𝔽 H¹_{{L_v^⊥}}(S, (Ad⁰)*(1)) (§4.1.4) and j = 4|S| − 1. There are maps of R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S-algebras R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S[[x₁, …, x_{h+j−d}]] → R_∞ → R̄^{□,ψ}_S, with R_∞ an 𝒪[[y₁, …, y_{h+j}]]-algebra, and an R_∞-module M_∞, such that: (1) each of the maps is surjective and the right-hand map induces an isomorphism R_∞/(y₁, …, y_h)R_∞ ≅ R̄^{□,ψ}_S of R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S-algebras; (2) M_∞ is a finite free 𝒪[[y₁, …, y_{h+j}]]-module, and the action of R_∞ on M_∞/(y₁, …, y_h)M_∞ factors through 𝕋^□_ψ(U)_𝔪 and makes it a faithful 𝕋^□_ψ(U)_𝔪-module.
items.locator: §9.1.2, Proposition 9.2 (I), p. 81; proof pp. 81–83, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.3/patched-ring-and-module and /arithmetic-patching-data; the finite-level inputs are GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/taylor-wiles-deformation-system (Q_n from Lemma 5.3, generator count from Proposition 5.5, Δ′-structure from Proposition 5.11) and GL2ModularityLifting:R22.2/taylor-wiles-module-system (Corollary 7.5). The proof also records R_∞/(y₁, …, y_{h+j}) ≅ R̄^ψ_S.

items.name: Proposition 9.2 (II): finiteness of R̄^{□,ψ}_S and R̄^ψ_S for p odd
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 9.2, R̄^{□,ψ}_S is a finite 𝒪[[y_{h+1}, …, y_{h+j}]]-module and R̄^ψ_S is a finite 𝒪-module.
items.locator: §9.1.2, Proposition 9.2 (II), p. 81; proof p. 83, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.3/minimal-ring-finite.

items.name: Proof of Proposition 9.2 (II): R_∞ ≅ R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S[[x₁, …, x_{h+j−d}]]
items.statement: The image of R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S[[x₁, …, x_{h+j−d}]] in End(M_∞) is a finite faithful 𝒪[[y₁, …, y_{h+j}]]-module, hence of dimension ≥ h + j + 1; since R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S is a domain and dim R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S[[x₁, …, x_{h+j−d}]] = h + j + 1, the composite R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S[[x₁, …, x_{h+j−d}]] → R_∞ → End(M_∞) is injective. Hence R_∞ ≅ R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S[[x₁, …, x_{h+j−d}]], R_∞ is a finite 𝒪[[y₁, …, y_{h+j}]]-module, and R_∞[1/p] is a regular Noetherian domain.
items.locator: §9.1.2, proof of Proposition 9.2 (II), p. 83, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.3/patched-support (domain case: B⟦x⟧ → R_∞ → End(M_∞) injective, R_∞ ≅ B⟦x⟧); the dimension count is GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/patching-numerology.

items.name: Proposition 9.2 (III): R = T up to p-power torsion for p odd
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 9.2, the map π : R̄^{□,ψ}_S → 𝕋^□_ψ(U)_𝔪 of Lemma 9.1 is surjective with p-power torsion kernel.
items.locator: §9.1.2, Proposition 9.2 (III), p. 81; proof p. 83, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.3/generic-fibre-r-equals-t. The paper refers to 'Proposition 9.1' here (a misprint for Lemma 9.1, see sourceIssues). Proof: Kisin's Lemma 3.3.4 of [36] (Auslander–Buchsbaum) makes M_∞ ⊗ E finite projective and faithful over R_∞[1/p]; reduce modulo (y₁, …, y_h).

items.name: §9.1.3: dyadic set-up (Q_n, G_n, t, the torus T)
items.statement: For p = 2, fix n₀ and for each n ≥ n₀ + 1 a set Q_n of auxiliary primes as in Lemma 5.10, of fixed cardinality h¹(S, Ad) − 2. Let G_n be the Galois group of the maximal abelian extension of F of 2-power degree that is split at S and unramified outside S ∪ Q_n; it has a fixed number t = h¹_{S−split}(Q_n, 𝔽) of generators. T := Hom(𝐭, 𝔾_m) is the torus in the CNL_𝒪 category with character group the constant free abelian group 𝐭 of rank t, and T_{2^k} is its 2^k-torsion. For n > n₀ the quotient G′_n of G_n killed by 2^{n−2} is ≅ (ℤ/2^{n−2}ℤ)^t (Lemma 5.10); a chosen isomorphism G′_n ≅ 𝐭/2^{n−2}𝐭 identifies (G′_n)* with T_{2^{n−2}}, and n₀ may be enlarged.
items.locator: §9.1.3, pp. 83–84, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/dyadic-patching-data, R04.4/diagonalizable-groups and R04.5/dyadic-taylor-wiles-primes (Lemma 5.10).

items.name: Patching datum of level m (p = 2)
items.statement: Let B := R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S, s := rank_𝒪 S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪)_𝔪, r_m := s·m·2^m·(h + j), c_m := (π_E^m, (1 + y₁)^{2^m} − 1, …, (1 + y_h)^{2^m} − 1, y_{h+1}^{2^m}, …, y_{h+j}^{2^m}) ⊂ 𝒪[[y₁, …, y_{h+j}]]; for a CNL_𝒪-algebra A let 𝔪_A^{(r)} be the ideal generated by the r-th powers of elements of 𝔪_A; let b be the number of generators of the maximal ideal of B[[x₁, …, x_{h+j+t−d}]] and r′_m := b·r_m (so 𝔪_A^{r′_m} ⊂ 𝔪_A^{(r_m)} for quotients A of B[[x]]). Let R := R̄^{□,ψ}_S and M := S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪)_𝔪 ⊗_{R̄^ψ_S} R̄^{□,ψ}_S. For m ≥ 3 a patching datum of level m is (D_m, L_m, D′_m) with: (1) CNL_𝒪-algebra maps 𝒪[[y]]/c_m → D_m → R/(c_mR + 𝔪_R^{(r_m)}), the second a surjection of B-algebras, 𝔪_{D_m}^{(r_m)} = 0, inducing D_m/(y₁, …, y_h)D_m ≅ R/(c_mR + 𝔪_R^{(r_m)}) and inducing on R/(c_mR + 𝔪_R^{(r_m)}) its given 𝒪[[y]]-structure (y₁, …, y_h acting by 0, y_{h+1}, …, y_{h+j} through the framing); (2) a surjection of B-algebras B[[x₁, …, x_{h+j+t−d}]] → D′_m with D′_m a CNL_𝒪^{[r′_m]}-algebra (§2.6), a map d_m : Sp D′_m → T, a closed immersion Sp D_m ↪ Sp D′_m, and a free group action chunk in CNL_𝒪^{[r′_m]} of T_{2^m}^{[r′_m]} on Sp D′_m with d_m(lx) = l²d_m(x) for l ∈ T_{2^m}(A), x ∈ Sp D′_m(A); if Sp D″_m ↪ Sp D′_m is the closed immersion defined by d_m(x′) = 1, then Sp D_m ↪ Sp D′_m factors through Sp D″_m and ker(D″_m → D_m) ⊂ 𝔪^m_{D″_m}; (3) a D_m-module L_m, finite free of rank s over 𝒪[[y]]/c_m, with a surjection of D_m-modules L_m → M/c_mM.
items.locator: §9.1.3, proof of Proposition 9.3, pp. 84–85, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
