items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.3/arithmetic-patching-data states the level-m datum only in the odd-p form (D_m, L_m) and cites these pages. GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6/dyadic-patched-ring patches (D_m, L_m, D′_m). Its first proof step, as corrected by that packet's review (#4823), states the paper's condition (2): the determinant-one quotient D″_m surjects onto D_m with kernel in 𝔪^m_{D″_m}, and D_m is not identified with D″_m at finite level. Its third step uses the same condition. The red team read the earlier text, which set D_m = D′_m/(d_m − 1). No node spells out the truncation level r′_m. R22.6's layer plans the 2-adic patching, so the item stays planned there (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/7).

items.name: Level-(m, n) patching data from Taylor–Wiles level n + a (p = 2)
items.statement: Let R_n := R̄^{□,ψ}_{S∪Q_n} and R′_n := R̄^□_{S∪Q_n} (determinant fixed only on S, §4.1.1), X_n = Sp R_n, X′_n = Sp R′_n; y_i (1 ≤ i ≤ h, Q_n = {v₁, …, v_h}) acts on R_n as δ_i − 1 with δ_i a generator of Δ′_i (the maximal 2-quotient of k_{v_i}^×), and y_{h+1}, …, y_{h+j} through the framing. Put M_n := S_{k,ψ}(U_{Q_n}, 𝒪)_𝔪 ⊗_{R̄^ψ_{S∪Q_n}} R_n and b_n := Ann_{𝒪[[y]]}(M_n). Fix a ≥ 2 with 2^a > N (§7.4); then for n > a, M_n is finite free of rank s over 𝒪[[y]]/b_n, b_n ⊂ ((1 + y₁)^{2^{n−a}} − 1, …, (1 + y_h)^{2^{n−a}} − 1), and M_n/(y₁, …, y_h) ≅ M (Corollary 7.5). For n ≥ n₀ + 1 ≥ 3 and n ≥ m ≥ 3 set D_{m,n} := R_{n+a}/(c_mR_{n+a} + 𝔪^{(r_m)}_{R_{n+a}}), L_{m,n} := M_{n+a}/c_mM_{n+a}, D′_{m,n} := (R′_{n+a})^{[r′_m]}; d_{m,n} is the reduction of d_{R′_{n+a}} : X′_{n+a} → G*_{n+a} ↪ T, ρ_A ↦ det ρ_A · (χ_pψ)^{−1} (via a surjection 𝐭 → G_n compatible with 𝐭 → G′_n); the free T_{2^m}-chunk action comes from the free twisting action of G′*_{n+a} ⊇ T_{2^n} on X′_{n+a} (§5.1, Lemma 5.1). Then (D_{m,n}, L_{m,n}, D′_{m,n}) is a patching datum of level m; R′_n is generated over B by 2h + 1 = h + j + t − d elements (Lemma 5.10, t = 2 + h − |S|).
items.locator: §9.1.3, proof of Proposition 9.3, pp. 85–86, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/dyadic-patching-data (R′_n, R_n, d_n, twisting action, presentation, Δ′-structure: 'the level-n inputs to KW II's patching data (D_m, L_m, D′_m)'), R04.4/twist-action-free and R04.6/patching-numerology (2h + 1 = h + j + t − d).

items.name: Patched objects R′_∞, R_∞, M_∞, d and the T-action (p = 2)
items.statement: As B[[x₁, …, x_{h+j+t−d}]]^{[r′_m]} is finite there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of patching data of level m; after extracting a subsequence of (n) one gets patching data (D_m, L_m, D′_m) forming a projective system, with (D_m, L_m, D′_m) ≅ (D_{m,n}, L_{m,n}, D′_{m,n}) for the retained n ≥ m. Put R′_∞ := lim_m D′_m, R_∞ := lim_m D_m, M_∞ := lim_m L_m; there are surjections of B-algebras B[[x₁, …, x_{h+j+t−d}]] → R′_∞ → R_∞ (so both are CNL_𝒪-algebras), the d_m define d : X′_∞ → T, and the free chunk actions of T_{2^m}^{[r′_m]} on Sp D′_m define a free action of T on X′_∞ (Propositions 2.7 and 2.8).
items.locator: §9.1.3, proof of Proposition 9.3, pp. 86–87, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6/dyadic-patched-ring; the passage from truncated chunks to a torus action is GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/truncated-actions (Propositions 2.7, 2.8); the compactness/subsequence argument is DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.5 (stage description).

items.name: Proposition 9.3 (I)(1)–(2): patched rings and module for p = 2
items.statement: Let p = 2, assume the conditions at the beginning of §9, and let d = 3|S|, h = |Q_n|, j = 4|S| − 1 (t as in §9.1.3). There are maps of R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S-algebras R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S[[x₁, …, x_{h+j+t−d}]] → R′_∞ → R_∞ → R̄^{□,ψ}_S, with R_∞ an 𝒪[[y₁, …, y_{h+j}]]-algebra, and an R_∞-module M_∞, such that (1) each of the maps is surjective and the right-hand map induces an isomorphism R_∞/(y₁, …, y_h)R_∞ ≅ R̄^{□,ψ}_S of R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S-algebras; (2) M_∞ is a finite free 𝒪[[y₁, …, y_{h+j}]]-module, and the action of R_∞ on M_∞/(y₁, …, y_h)M_∞ factors through 𝕋^□_ψ(U)_𝔪 and makes it a faithful 𝕋^□_ψ(U)_𝔪-module.
items.locator: §9.1.3, Proposition 9.3 (I), pp. 83–84; proof pp. 84–87, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6/dyadic-patched-ring.

items.name: Proposition 9.3 (I)(3): the torus action and the determinant map
items.statement: Let X′_∞ and X_∞ be the functors on CNL_𝒪-algebras represented by R′_∞ and R_∞. There is a free action of the torus T on X′_∞ and a map d : X′_∞ → T such that the closed immersion X_∞ ↪ X′_∞ identifies X_∞ with the closed subfunctor defined by d(x′) = 1, and d(tx′) = t²d(x′) for x′ ∈ X′_∞ and t ∈ T.
items.locator: §9.1.3, Proposition 9.3 (I)(3), p. 84; proof p. 87, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6/dyadic-patched-ring (free T-action, d(λx) = λ²d(x), X_∞ = d^{−1}(1)); finite-level version GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/determinant-fixed-on-S.

items.name: Proposition 9.3 (II): finiteness of R̄^{□,ψ}_S and R̄^ψ_S for p = 2
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 9.3, R̄^{□,ψ}_S is a finite 𝒪[[y_{h+1}, …, y_{h+j}]]-module and R̄^ψ_S is a finite 𝒪-module.
items.locator: §9.1.3, Proposition 9.3 (II), p. 84; proof p. 88, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6/dyadic-r-equals-t; the deduction from Lemma 9.6(b) (R_∞ ↪ End_{𝒪[[y]]}(M_∞)) is also recorded in DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.4/finiteness-of-deformation-rings-criteria.

items.name: Proposition 9.3 (III): R = T up to 2-power torsion
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 9.3, the map π : R̄^{□,ψ}_S → 𝕋^□_ψ(U)_𝔪 of Lemma 9.1 is surjective with 2-power torsion kernel.
items.locator: §9.1.3, Proposition 9.3 (III), p. 84; proof pp. 88–89, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6/dyadic-r-equals-t. Printed reference 'Proposition 9.1' is a misprint for Lemma 9.1 (sourceIssues). Proof: Kisin's Lemma 3.3.4 of [36] on each connected component of R_∞[1/2].

items.name: R^inv_∞: the ring of T-orbits on X′_∞
items.statement: R^inv_∞ is the CNL_𝒪-algebra representing the orbits of the free action of T on X′_∞ (Proposition 2.5); X′_∞ → Sp R^inv_∞ is a trivial T-torsor.
items.locator: §9.1.3, proof of Proposition 9.3, p. 87, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6/dyadic-patched-torsor; GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/free-action-quotient (Propositions 2.5, 2.6).

items.name: Lemma 9.4: R_∞ is a T₂-torsor over R^inv_∞
items.statement: The natural map R^inv_∞ → R_∞ makes R_∞ a torsor over R^inv_∞ with group T₂, the 2-torsion of the torus T.
items.locator: §9.1.3, Lemma 9.4, p. 87, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6/dyadic-patched-torsor; abstract form GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/determinant-twist-torsor. Proof: X′_∞ ×_T T = {(ρ, λ) : d(ρ) = λ²} is a T × T₂-torsor over Sp R^inv_∞ and (ρ, λ) ↦ (λ^{−1}ρ, λ) identifies it with X_∞ × T; quotient by T (Proposition 2.6).

items.name: Lemma 9.5: R′_∞ ≅ B[[x₁, …, x_{h+j+t−d}]]
items.statement: The surjective map B[[x₁, …, x_{h+j+t−d}]] → R′_∞ (B = R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S) is an isomorphism.
items.locator: §9.1.3, Lemma 9.5, p. 87, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6/dyadic-patched-torsor. Proof: B is a domain of absolute dimension d + 1; otherwise dim R′_∞ < h + j + t + 1, so dim R^inv_∞ < h + j + 1 (Proposition 2.5) and dim R_∞ < h + j + 1 (Lemma 9.4), contradicting the faithful action of 𝒪[[y₁, …, y_{h+j}]] on the finite module M_∞.

items.name: After Lemma 9.5: R′_∞, R^inv_∞ are flat domains and R^inv_∞ acts faithfully on M_∞
items.statement: R′_∞ and R^inv_∞ are domains flat over 𝒪, and the action of R^inv_∞ on M_∞ is faithful.
items.locator: §9.1.3, after Lemma 9.5, p. 87, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6/dyadic-patched-torsor ('R′_∞ and R^inv_∞ are 𝒪-flat domains … M_∞ is faithful over R^inv_∞').

items.name: Lemma 9.6 (a): R_∞[1/2] and R^inv_∞[1/2] are regular
items.statement: The rings R_∞[1/2] and R^inv_∞[1/2] are regular.
items.locator: §9.1.3, Lemma 9.6 (a), p. 88, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6/dyadic-patched-torsor. Proof: B[1/2] regular ⇒ B[[x]][1/2] regular; R^inv_∞ → R′_∞ ≅ B[[x]] is formally smooth, so R^inv_∞[1/2] is regular (Lemma (33.B) of [41]); R^inv_∞[1/2] → R_∞[1/2] is étale. The commutative-algebra inputs are the separate item 'Regularity inputs for Lemma 9.6(a)'.

items.name: Lemma 9.6 (b): M_∞ is a faithful R_∞-module
items.statement: M_∞ is a faithful R_∞-module.
items.locator: §9.1.3, Lemma 9.6 (b), p. 88, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6/dyadic-patched-torsor; the group-transitivity argument is DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.6/support-group-transitive and /faithful-group-transitive. Proof: Supp M_∞[1/2] contains an irreducible component of Spec R_∞[1/2]; T₂(𝒪) ≅ {±1}^t acts transitively on the components (Lemma 9.4); twisting (paragraph after Proposition 7.6; Lemma 5.12: χ·y_i = χ(δ_i)(1 + y_i) − 1 for i ≤ h, χ·y_i = y_i for i > h) keeps c_m and the annihilators of L_{m,n} stable, so Supp is T₂(𝒪)-stable.

items.name: Theorem 9.7: modularity lifting over totally real F
items.statement: Let F be a totally real field unramified at p, split at p if ρ̄|_{D_p} is locally irreducible or k(ρ̄) = p + 1, such that ρ̄_F has non-solvable image when p = 2 and ρ̄|_{G_{F(μ_p)}} is absolutely irreducible for p > 2, and assume that ρ̄_F satisfies (α) and (β) if p ≠ 2, (α) if p = 2 and k(ρ̄) = 2, and (β) if p = 2 (§8.2). Let ρ_F be a lift of ρ̄_F, ramified at only finitely many places, totally odd, and such that at all places above p it satisfies one of the conditions (A), (B), (C) of §8.3.3 when p > 2, and when p = 2 is either crystalline of weight 2 or semistable non-crystalline of weight 2, the latter considered only when the residual representation is not finite at the places above 2. Then ρ_F is modular.
items.locator: §9.2, Theorem 9.7, p. 89; proof pp. 89–90, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.5/kw-odd-prime-lifting (p > 2) and R22.6/kw-dyadic-lifting (p = 2) state the two cases. Proof: allowable base change F′/F via Lemma 2.2 of [60] to make ρ_{F′} fit lifting data (uniform type at p, semistable (γ_vχ_p ∗; 0 γ_v) where ramified away from p, ρ̄_{F′} trivial above p if ρ̄ unramified at p), Theorem 8.4 for π′, Propositions 9.2/9.3, and Langlands' solvable base change.

items.name: §10.1: deformation rings over ℚ with local conditions
items.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝔽) be the fixed representation (2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1 if p > 2; non-solvable image if p = 2; ρ̄|_{ℚ(μ_p)} absolutely irreducible if p > 2), S a finite set of places of ℚ containing p, ∞ and all places where ρ̄ is ramified, and ψ : G_ℚ → 𝒪^× an arithmetic character with ψχ_p lifting det ρ̄. For each v ∈ S let R̄^{□,ψ}_v be a ring of one of the types of Theorem 3.1: at p the representations ρ_x of the points x : R̄^{□,ψ}_p → 𝒪′ are of type (A) (including k(ρ̄) = p = 2), (B), or (C) (including p = 2, k(ρ̄) = 4), with case (C) considered for p > 2 only when k(ρ̄) = p + 1; at ∞ the deformations are odd; at finite v ≠ p any ring of Theorem 3.1 is allowed (it need not be a domain). R̄^{□,ψ}_S := R^{□,ψ}_S ⊗̂_{R^{□,loc,ψ}_S} R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S and R̄^ψ_S is the image of the universal deformation ring R^ψ_S in R̄^{□,ψ}_S.
items.locator: §10.1, p. 90, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.1/kw-ii-theorem-10-1-finiteness-of-the-unframed-global-ring ('ρ̄, S, ψ and local conditions as in 10.1'); GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6 for the rings.

items.name: Theorem 10.1: finiteness of R̄^ψ_S
items.statement: For ρ̄, S, ψ and local conditions as in §10.1 (with the R̄^{□,ψ}_v at finite v ≠ p any of the rings of Theorem 3.1, not necessarily domains), the ring R̄^ψ_S is finite as a ℤ_p-module.
items.locator: §10.1, Theorem 10.1, p. 90; proof pp. 90–92, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.1/kw-ii-theorem-10-1-finiteness-of-the-unframed-global-ring. Stated as a corollary of Theorem 8.2, Theorem 6.1 and Propositions 9.2, 9.3. The printed construction of the comparison map is only valid modulo p (sourceIssues, gap); the atlas node repeats the integral maps β, α.

items.name: Proof of Theorem 10.1: the auxiliary totally real field F
items.statement: There is a number field F such that: F/ℚ is totally real, im(ρ̄|_F) is non-solvable for p = 2 and ρ̄|_{F(μ_p)} is absolutely irreducible for p > 2, F is split at p if ρ̄|_{D_p} is irreducible and unramified at p otherwise, and ψ_F is unramified at all finite places not above p (so ψ_F is of the type fixed in §8.1); if ρ̄|_{D_p} is unramified then ρ̄|_{G_℘} is trivial for all places ℘ of F above p; strengthened (α), (β) hold: (assuming k(ρ̄) = 2 when p = 2) ρ̄|_{G_F} arises from a cuspidal π′ of GL₂(𝔸_F) unramified at all places and discrete series of weight k(ρ̄) at infinity, with central character ψ_F (used for (A)); and ρ̄|_{G_F} arises from a cuspidal π′ with π′_v unramified at finite v ∤ p, of conductor dividing v at v | p, of weight 2 at infinity, with central character ψ_F, and when p = 2, k(ρ̄) = 4 with ρ_{π′} at the places above 2 arising from R̄^{□,ψ}_v (used for (B), (C)); when weight p + 1 liftings are considered, F is split at p (Theorems 6.1, 8.2); and the reduction τ mod p of the universal representation attached to R̄^ψ_{ℚ,S}, restricted to G_F, is unramified outside the places above p and ∞. Such F exists by Theorem 6.1, Theorem 8.2 and Lemma 4.2 of [33].
items.locator: §10.1, proof of Theorem 10.1, pp. 90–91, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.1/auxiliary-totally-real-field-for-the-finiteness-argument. The printed reference 'part (c) of Theorem 6.1' should be (iii) b) (recorded as PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems/E2).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 10.1: the deformation ring R̄^{ψ_F}_F over F
items.statement: R̄^{ψ_F}_F is the deformation ring over F parametrising (minimal, odd) deformations of ρ̄_F that are unramified outside the places above p, of determinant ψ_Fχ_p, and satisfy uniformly at all places above p one of (A) (including k(ρ̄) = p = 2), (B) or (C) (including p = 2, k(ρ̄) = 4); the implied set of ramification places consists of the places above p and ∞. The representation ρ_{π′} (π′ chosen according to the case (A), (B) or (C)) prescribes lifting data for it.
items.locator: §10.1, proof of Theorem 10.1, p. 91, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Named in the proof steps of PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.1/kw-ii-theorem-10-1-finiteness-of-the-unframed-global-ring ('the ring over F described in the hypotheses').

items.name: Proof of Theorem 10.1: R̄^{ψ_F}_F is finite over ℤ_p
items.statement: Propositions 9.2 (p > 2) and 9.3 (p = 2) apply to R̄^{ψ_F}_F, which is therefore finite as a ℤ_p-module.
items.locator: §10.1, proof of Theorem 10.1, p. 91, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Proof step of PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.1/kw-ii-theorem-10-1-finiteness-of-the-unframed-global-ring; the finiteness itself is GL2ModularityLifting:R22.3/minimal-ring-finite and R22.6/dyadic-r-equals-t.

items.name: Proof of Theorem 10.1: the restriction morphism γ̄ : R̄^{ψ_F}_F → R̄^ψ_{ℚ,S}/(p) (printed integrally as γ; corrected by E29)
items.statement: As corrected by sourceIssues E29 (PROTOCOL §18). Let τ : G_ℚ → GL₂(R̄^ψ_{ℚ,S}/(p)) be the universal mod-p representation. By the choice of F (fourth bullet of the proof), τ|_{G_F} is unramified outside the places above p and ∞, so it is classified by β̄ : R^{ψ_F}_F → R̄^ψ_{ℚ,S}/(p). In framed form (R^{□,ψ_F}_F → R̄^{□,ψ}_{ℚ,S}/(p), the frames at w | p, ∞ taken from those at p, ∞) it factors through R̄^{□,ψ_F}_w at each w | p. This is because every 𝒪′-point of R̄^{□,ψ}_p restricts to a lift of the same type (A), (B) or (C) over the unramified F_w (Corollary 2.3), and oddness is preserved at the infinite places. Hence β̄ induces a CNL_𝒪-algebra morphism γ̄ : R̄^{ψ_F}_F → R̄^ψ_{ℚ,S}/(p), carrying the universal mod-p representation of G_F to τ|_{G_F}. That is all the finiteness argument uses. Printed: CNL_𝒪-morphisms π₁ : R^{ψ_F}_F → R̄^{□,ψ_F}_F, π₂ : R^ψ_{ℚ,S} → R̄^{□,ψ}_{ℚ,S}, β : R^{ψ_F}_F → R^ψ_{ℚ,S} and α : R̄^{□,ψ_F}_F → R̄^{□,ψ}_{ℚ,S} with απ₁ = π₂β, and 'β induces a CNL_O-algebra morphism γ : R̄^{ψ_F}_F → R̄^ψ_{Q,S}'. These integral maps do not exist in general (E29).
items.locator: §10.1, proof of Theorem 10.1, pp. 91–92, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Planned at PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.1, whose layer plans Theorem 10.1's restriction argument ('comparison with the modular deformation problem', 'the finiteness of the restriction map'). No node states γ̄. R24.1/kw-ii-theorem-10-1-finiteness-of-the-unframed-global-ring repeats the printed integral β, α. GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/restriction-ring-map ('res descends to the rings with local conditions … (KW II's γ)') gives the integral map only under a local-containment hypothesis, which fails here at the places above ℓ ≠ p (E29), so R04.4 is no longer listed as planning it. The item takes E29's corrected map, as §18 requires (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/7).

items.name: Finite-image criterion for finiteness of deformation rings (3.14 of [31], Lemma 3.6 of [34])
items.statement: (As used) If the universal mod-p representation ρ̄^univ_{ℚ,S} : G_ℚ → GL₂(R̄^ψ_{ℚ,S}/(p)) has finite image, then R̄^ψ_S = R̄^ψ_{ℚ,S} is finite as a ℤ_p-module. (Black box: de Jong 3.14 of [31] or Khare–Wintenberger Lemma 3.6 of [34].)
items.locator: §10.1, end of proof of Theorem 10.1, p. 92, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.4/finiteness-of-deformation-rings-criteria (KW Annals Lemma 3.6: R_F finite iff η_F(G) finite, applied mod p).

items.name: Lemma 4.2 of [33]: killing the ramification of τ away from p
items.statement: (As used) For each of the finitely many primes ℓ_i ≠ p at which the mod-p universal representation τ attached to R̄^ψ_{ℚ,S} is ramified, there is a finite extension F_{ℓ_i}/ℚ_{ℓ_i} such that τ|_{G_{F_{ℓ_i}}} is unramified. (Black box from Khare [33].)
items.locator: §10.1, proof of Theorem 10.1, fourth bullet, p. 91, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: No node states it. PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.1/auxiliary-totally-real-field-for-the-finiteness-argument uses it as a hypothesis for its condition (4) and notes that 'Lemma 4.2 of [33] could not be located' in the arXiv copy read; R03.4/finiteness-of-deformation-rings-criteria covers only the finite-image criterion. The needed fact is that a continuous representation of G_{ℚ_ℓ} (ℓ ≠ p) into GL₂ of a complete local ring of characteristic p has finite image on inertia.

items.name: Theorem 4.1 (1) of [35] (KW I), proved in §10.2
items.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝔽), 𝔽 finite of characteristic 2, be modular with non-solvable image. Let ρ be an odd 2-adic lift of ρ̄, unramified outside a finite set of primes, that is either crystalline of weight 2 at 2, or semistable of weight 2 at 2, the latter only when k(ρ̄) = 4. Then ρ is modular. (Statement as in KW I; this range gives its proof.)
items.locator: §10.2, p. 92 (statement: [35] Theorem 4.1(1), p. 7), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.4/kw-theorem-4-1 assembles it; GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6/kw-dyadic-lifting is Theorem 9.7 for p = 2. Proof: (α) (k(ρ̄) = 2) and (β) from the weight part of Serre's conjecture, then Theorem 9.7 (after an allowable base change, with solvable descent).

items.name: Theorem 4.1 (2) of [35] (KW I), proved in §10.2
items.statement: Let p > 2 and ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝔽) be modular with ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ(μ_p)}} absolutely irreducible. Let ρ be a p-adic lift of ρ̄, unramified outside a finite set of primes, that is either (i) crystalline of weight k at p with 2 ≤ k ≤ p + 1, or (ii) potentially semistable of weight 2 at p. Then ρ is modular. (Statement as in KW I; §10.2 proves the cases not already in the literature: (2)(i) with k = p.)
items.locator: §10.2, p. 92 (statement: [35] Theorem 4.1(2), p. 7), author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.4/kw-theorem-4-1 states all of Theorem 4.1(2). But its proof goes only through Theorem 9.7 after an allowable base change F/ℚ, which needs F unramified at p and lifting data of type (A), (B) or (C); (A) allows weight p + 1 only when F is split at p and k(ρ̄) = p + 1 (p. 75). So the planned coverage is split by case, as in §10.2 (p. 92) and its Remark: (2)(i), 2 ≤ k ≤ p − 1: /316 (GL2ModularityLifting R22.5; Theorem 9.7 covers it too). (2)(i), k = p, and the weight-two lifts of (2)(ii) that are of type (B) or (C) up to twist: Theorem 9.7, i.e. GL2ModularityLifting:R22.5/kw-odd-prime-lifting through R24.4/kw-theorem-4-1. (2)(i), k = p + 1 and ordinary: /318 (R22.5/ordinary-overlap and OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.4). (2)(i), k = p + 1 and non-ordinary, including k(ρ̄) = 2: /317 (OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.5/blz-reduction-theorem, with GL2ModularityLifting:R32.2/odd-prime-de-rham-lifting standing in for Kisin [38], which no node states). (2)(ii), potentially Barsotti–Tate: /319 (GL2ModularityLifting:R22.5/kisin-potentially-bt-lifting, part (3)). (2)(ii), potentially semistable but not potentially crystalline: a finite-order twist makes it semistable of weight 2, which is /318. R22.5, R21.4 and R21.5 precede R24.4 on the atlas. R32.2 is unrelated to R24.4 on the atlas and its links, but once packet prerequisites are counted R24.4 already reaches R32.2 (through ClassicalSerreModularity R26.6, R27.1 and R33.3). So R32.2 is not listed here: the k = p + 1 non-ordinary case rests on /317, and the R24.4 node's prerequisites are a note for the maintainer (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/9). §10.2 cites [20] (k ≤ p − 1), [38] with [3] (k = p + 1 non-ordinary), [16] (k = p + 1 ordinary), [36] ((ii), potentially Barsotti–Tate), and [66], [64], [16] ((ii), semistable weight 2), and proves k = p via Theorem 9.7.

items.name: Residual hypotheses (α), (β) from the weight part of Serre's conjecture
items.statement: If ρ̄ is modular (with the image hypotheses of Theorem 4.1 of [35]) then, by the weight part of Serre's conjecture (Theorem 13.10 of [27], [12], and Propositions 8.13 and 8.18 of [27]), ρ̄ satisfies (α) and (β) for p > 2, (α) when k(ρ̄) = p = 2, and (β) for p = 2 (over a suitable allowable F). The hypothesis N > 4 of [27] may be assumed, since optimal prime-to-p level is not needed; [27] is not needed when k = p.
items.locator: §10.2, p. 92, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.4/alpha-beta-from-residual-modularity; the weight theorem itself is planned in SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.3 and R20.6 (and AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.4).

items.name: Cited: Diamond–Flach–Guo [20], Theorem 4.1(2)(i) for k ≤ p − 1
items.statement: (Black box) For p > 2 and ρ̄ modular with ρ̄|_{ℚ(μ_p)} absolutely irreducible, a lift ρ that is crystalline of weight k at p with 2 ≤ k ≤ p − 1 (Fontaine–Laffaille range) is modular ([20]).
items.locator: §10.2, p. 92, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.5/fontaine-laffaille-lifting plans Gee's version (p > 3, HT weights differing by ≤ p − 2, ρ̄(G_F) ⊇ SL₂(𝔽_p)), which does not cover p = 3; the whole range 2 ≤ k ≤ p + 1 (k = p + 1 only with k(ρ̄) = p + 1) is covered by R22.5/kw-odd-prime-lifting (Theorem 9.7).

items.name: Cited: weight p + 1 non-ordinary case (Kisin [38], Berger–Li–Zhu [3], Hasse invariant [32]/[24])
items.statement: (Black box) If ρ is crystalline of weight p + 1 at p and non-ordinary, then ρ̄|_{D_p} is irreducible of Serre weight 2 (Berger–Li–Zhu [3]); ρ̄ arises from a newform of level prime to p and weight p + 1 (weight part of Serre's conjecture with multiplication by the Hasse invariant, 12.4 of [32], or Corollary 1 of §2 of [24]); and then ρ is modular (Kisin [38]).
items.locator: §10.2, p. 92, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.5/blz-reduction-theorem (for k ≤ p + 1 and v_p(a_p) > 0, V̄_{k,a_p} ≅ V̄_{k,0}); the lifting step is covered by GL2ModularityLifting:R32.2/odd-prime-de-rham-lifting (Kisin, Emerton, Hu–Tan, Tung), not by a node for [38]. Per the Remark in §10.2 this is the one case of 4.1(2)(i) (k = p + 1 with k(ρ̄) = 2) that KW II do not treat self-containedly. The Hasse-invariant step has no node over ℚ (Lemma 8.3 is its Hilbert analogue).

items.name: Cited: Diamond [16], weight p + 1 ordinary case and semistable weight 2 ([66], [64], [16])
items.statement: (Black box) A lift that is crystalline of weight p + 1 and ordinary at p is modular ([16]); a lift that is semistable of weight 2 at p is modular ([66], [64], [16]).
items.locator: §10.2, p. 92, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.5/ordinary-overlap (type (C) and weight p + 1 with k(ρ̄) = p + 1 are ordinary and lie in OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.4).

items.name: Cited: Kisin [36], potentially Barsotti–Tate case of Theorem 4.1(2)(ii)
items.statement: (Black box) For p > 2 and ρ̄ modular with ρ̄|_{ℚ(μ_p)} absolutely irreducible, a lift that is potentially Barsotti–Tate at p is modular ([36]).
items.locator: §10.2, p. 92, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.5/kisin-potentially-bt-lifting, part (3) over ℚ (whose hypothesis is irreducibility over ℚ(√((−1)^{(p−1)/2}p)), equivalent by R32.1/quadratic-cyclotomic-irreducibility).

items.name: Remark in §10.2: self-contained coverage
items.statement: The arguments of KW II treat in a self-contained manner all cases of Theorem 4.1(2)(i) of [35] except k = p + 1 with k(ρ̄) = 2, and treat Theorem 4.1(2)(ii) when ρ|_{ℚ_p(μ_p)} is semistable of weight 2.
items.locator: §10.2, Remark, p. 92, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.5/kw-odd-prime-lifting ('when k = p + 1, with k(ρ̄) = p + 1'; types (B), (C)).

items.name: Lifting of the required type (Theorem 5.1 of [35])
items.statement: A lifting of the required type is a p-adic deformation ρ = ρ_p of ρ̄ as asserted in Theorem 5.1 of [35] (types (1)–(4) there), of determinant ψχ_p; for the corresponding local conditions, the 𝒪′-valued points of Spec R̄^ψ_S (§10.1), for 𝒪′ the rings of integers of finite extensions of ℚ_p, correspond exactly to the p-adic deformations of required type.
items.locator: §10.3.1, p. 92, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.3/required-lift-types (the four types, and 'lifts of required type are the 𝒪′-points of R̄^ψ_S').

items.name: §10.3.1: existence of p-adic lifts of the required type
items.statement: ρ̄ has a p-adic lift ρ_p of the required type: R̄^ψ_S is finite as an 𝒪-module (Theorem 10.1), so Corollary 4.7 (with Proposition 4.5) gives a local 𝒪-algebra map R̄^ψ_S → 𝒪′ for 𝒪′ the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p.
items.locator: §10.3.1, p. 92, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.2/characteristic-zero-points-of-R-bar-S-psi-give-lifts-of-required-type; the four constructions are R24.3/theorem-5-1-part-1-minimal-crystalline, -part-2-weight-two, -part-3-level-one-type-at-q and -part-4-level-two-type-at-q.

items.name: §10.3.2: the virtual representations ρ_ι by Brauer induction
items.statement: Let F and π′ be as in the proof of Theorem 10.1, with F/ℚ Galois; by Theorem 9.7, ρ_F := ρ|_{G_F} arises from a holomorphic cuspidal π of GL₂(𝔸_F) with respect to ι_p. Let G = Gal(F/ℚ). By Brauer's theorem there are subextensions F_i of F with G_i = Gal(F/F_i) solvable, characters χ_i of G_i with values in ℚ̄ (embedded in ℚ̄_p via ι_p) and n_i ∈ ℤ such that 1_G = Σ_i n_i Ind_{G_i}^G χ_i. Langlands' base change gives holomorphic cuspidal π_i of GL₂(𝔸_{F_i}) with ρ_{π_i,ι_p} = ρ|_{G_{F_i}}, so ρ = Σ_i n_i Ind_{G_{F_i}}^{G_ℚ}(χ_i ⊗ ρ_{π_i,ι_p}). For each prime ℓ and embedding ι : ℚ̄ → ℚ̄_ℓ define the virtual representation ρ_ι := Σ_i n_i Ind_{G_{F_i}}^{G_ℚ}(χ_i ⊗ ρ_{π_i,ι}) of G_ℚ (χ_i now ℓ-adic via ι).
items.locator: §10.3.2, p. 93, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/brauer-induction-system.

items.name: §10.3.2: ρ_ι is a true representation, with automorphic restrictions to solvable subfields
items.statement: ρ_ι is a true representation (as in the proof of Theorem 5.1 of [33]). For all primes outside a finite set, the traces of Frob_q in ρ and ρ_ι coincide. Consequently, if F′ ⊂ F is a subfield with F/F′ solvable and π_{F′} is the automorphic form associated to ρ|_{G_{F′}}, then ρ_ι|_{G_{F′}} is associated to π_{F′}.
items.locator: §10.3.2, p. 93, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/brauer-induction-system (true representation, trace agreement, restrictions to F′ with F/F′ solvable).

items.name: §10.3.2: almost strict compatibility of (ρ_ι) at q ≠ ℓ
items.statement: Let q be a prime, F(q) ⊂ F the fixed field of the decomposition group of Gal(F/ℚ) at a chosen prime Q | q, π_q the local component at Q of the automorphic form attached to ρ|_{G_{F(q)}}, and r_q the Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne parameter attached to π_q by local Langlands. For ι : ℚ̄ → ℚ̄_ℓ let r_{q,ι} be the Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne parameter of ρ_ι|_{D_q}. If q ≠ ℓ then r_{q,ι} ≅ r_q (Carayol [10], Taylor [61]).
items.locator: §10.3.2, p. 93, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/almost-strict-compatibility (a); AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.4 (local–global compatibility away from p).

items.name: §10.3.2: almost strict compatibility at q = ℓ ≠ 2 with r_q unramified
items.statement: If q = ℓ ≠ 2 and r_q is unramified, then r_{q,ι} ≅ r_q (Breuil [6], Berger [2]).
items.locator: §10.3.2, p. 94, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/almost-strict-compatibility (b); AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.5.

items.name: §10.3.2: almost strict compatibility at q = ℓ with ρ̄_ι irreducible
items.statement: Let q = ℓ and suppose ρ̄_ι irreducible. Choosing a totally real Galois F′/ℚ with ρ|_{G_{F′}} associated to an automorphic π′ and F′ linearly disjoint from the field fixed by ker(ρ̄_ι) (Theorem 6.1 (iii) d)), one has π_q ≅ π′_q (both correspond to ρ_{ι′}|_{D_q} for ι′ into ℚ̄_{ℓ′}, ℓ′ ≠ ℓ), and since ρ̄_ι|_{G_{F′(q)}} is irreducible, Kisin's result ([39]) gives that r_{q,ι} corresponds to π′_q, hence to π_q.
items.locator: §10.3.2, p. 94, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/almost-strict-compatibility (c); AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.5/hilbert-local-behaviour-at-p.

items.name: Theorem 5.1 of [35] (KW I): almost strictly compatible lifts, proved in §10.3
items.statement: ρ̄ lifts to an almost strictly compatible system (ρ_ι) whose p-adic member is the lift ρ_p of the required type constructed in §10.3.1 (statement: [35] Theorem 5.1). The system is only almost strictly compatible: the strict compatibility claimed in [67] would need the corollary in the introduction of [39] without its hypothesis of residual irreducibility.
items.locator: §10.3.2, pp. 93–94, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/kw-theorem-5-1-systems; the correction of [67] is recorded in R24.5/almost-strict-compatibility.

items.name: Theorem 5.1 (3) of [35]: Serre weight of ρ̄_q (Savitt, Corollary 6.15(1))
items.statement: In case (3) of Theorem 5.1 of [35], if the residual representation ρ̄_q is irreducible, its Serre weight is computed from the almost strict compatibility and Corollary 6.15 (1) of Savitt [54] (KW I: up to twist by a power of χ_q it is i + 2 or q + 1 − i).
items.locator: §10.3.2, (3), p. 94, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/kw-theorem-5-1-systems (weights, Savitt Corollary 6.15 and Remark 6.17).

items.name: Theorem 5.1 (4) of [35]: Serre weight of ρ̄_q (Savitt, Corollary 6.15(2), or Saito)
items.statement: In case (4) of Theorem 5.1 of [35], the claimed information on k(ρ̄_q) follows from the almost strict compatibility of (ρ_ι), or from the main theorem of Saito [53] applied to ρ_q|_{G_{F(q)}} (which does not need the irreducibility of ρ̄_q|_{G_{F(q)}}), together with Corollary 6.15 (2) of Savitt [54] and Serre's definition of weights (§2 of [56]).
items.locator: §10.3.2, (4), p. 94, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/kw-theorem-5-1-systems ('Savitt (and Saito for (4))'); Saito's theorem is AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.5 / PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/hilbert-modular-form-compatibility-at-p.

items.name: Kisin–Taylor–Wiles patching (Proposition 3.3.1 of [36]; [64]; Diamond [17] and Fujiwara; §1.3 of [37]; Proposition 1.3 and Corollary 1.4 of [38])
items.statement: (Black box, as used) Let B be a complete local flat 𝒪-algebra which is a domain of dimension d + 1 with B[1/p] regular (formally smooth over E in Kisin's formulation). Given, for each n, surjections of B-algebras B[[x₁, …, x_{h+j−d}]] ↠ R_n ↠ R with R_n an 𝒪[[y₁, …, y_{h+j}]]-algebra, R_n/(y₁, …, y_h) ≅ R, and R_n-modules M_n with M_n/(y₁, …, y_h) ≅ M, M_n finite free over 𝒪[[y]]/b_n with b_n ⊂ ((1 + y₁)^{p^n} − 1, …, (1 + y_h)^{p^n} − 1), a diagonal-subsequence argument produces R_∞, M_∞ as in Proposition 9.2 (I); then R is finite over 𝒪[[y_{h+1}, …, y_{h+j}]] and M ⊗_𝒪 E is a finite projective faithful R[1/p]-module.
items.locator: §9.1, p. 78; proof of Proposition 9.2, pp. 81–83; proof of Proposition 9.3, p. 84, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.5/kisin-patching-criterion (Kisin's Proposition (3.3.1)); GL2ModularityLifting:R22.3 applies it.

items.name: Kisin's Lemma 3.3.4 of [36] (Auslander–Buchsbaum)
items.statement: (Black box, as recorded in the atlas from Kisin) For a map A → D of Noetherian domains of the same finite dimension and a nonzero D-module L that is finite projective over A, A → D is finite; if A and D are regular, L is finite projective and faithful over D. Used with A = 𝒪[[y₁, …, y_{h+j}]][1/p] and D = R_∞[1/p] (p odd), resp. D a connected component of R_∞[1/2] (p = 2), L = M_∞ ⊗_𝒪 E.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 9.2 (III), p. 83; proof of Proposition 9.3 (III), p. 88, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3/depth-auslander-buchsbaum-and-dimension-bounds (last sentence, sourced to Kisin (3.3.4)). Mathlib has IsRegularLocalRing (definitions only) and no Auslander–Buchsbaum formula.

items.name: Carayol, Théorème 2 of [11]: representations with traces in a subring
items.statement: (Black box, in the form used) Let A be a complete Noetherian local ring with finite residue field (here A = 𝕋_ψ(U)_𝔪, or the image of 𝕋_ψ(U_{Q_n}) in 𝕋_{ψ,Q_n}(U_{Q_n})_𝔪) and B ⊇ A (here B = A ⊗_𝒪 E, resp. 𝕋_{ψ,Q_n}(U_{Q_n})_𝔪). A continuous representation ρ : G → GL₂(B) whose traces lie in A and whose residual representation is absolutely irreducible is defined over A, i.e. has a model ρ_A : G → GL₂(A) (precise hypotheses as in [11]).
items.locator: §9.1.1, p. 80; Remark after Lemma 9.1, p. 81, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.2/carayol-trace-theorem (3) states the local-ring case (traces in a closed subring S ⊆ R); AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.6 plans representability over the Hecke algebra under residual absolute irreducibility.

items.name: Brauer's induction theorem (as used in §10.3.2)
items.statement: (Black box) For a finite group G there are subgroups G_i (elementary, in particular solvable), one-dimensional characters χ_i of G_i and integers n_i with 1_G = Σ_i n_i Ind_{G_i}^G χ_i.
items.locator: §10.3.2, p. 93, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: tauceti InductionRestriction layer 6 plans Brauer's theorem as surjectivity of ⊕_{E elementary} R(E) → R(G); the form with one-dimensional χ_i also needs that elementary (nilpotent) groups are monomial, which that layer does not state. PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/brauer-induction-system states the decomposition 1_G = Σ n_i Ind χ_i with G_i solvable. Not in Mathlib (only the Brauer group).

items.name: Compatible systems attached to Hilbert modular forms, with irreducible members ([61], [6], [62])
items.statement: (Black box) A holomorphic cuspidal π of GL₂(𝔸_F), F totally real, gives rise to a compatible system (ρ_{π,ι}) of two-dimensional representations of G_F ([61], [6]), each member of which is irreducible ([62]).
items.locator: §10.3.2, p. 93, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.2/hilbert-modular-compatible-system-carayol-theorem-A and R19.3 (compatible systems); the stage R19.2 includes 'the required irreducibility'.

items.name: Breuil [6] and Berger [2]: crystallinity at an unramified coefficient prime
items.statement: (Black box, as used) If q = ℓ ≠ 2 and the local parameter r_q of π at q is unramified, then ρ_ι|_{D_q} is crystalline and its Weil–Deligne parameter is r_q.
items.locator: §10.3.2, p. 94, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.5 (compatibility at the coefficient prime) and PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/almost-strict-compatibility (b).

items.name: Savitt, Corollary 6.15 of [54]: Serre weights of tamely potentially Barsotti–Tate reductions
items.statement: (Black box, as used) Corollary 6.15 (1), resp. (2), of [54] describes the reduction of a potentially Barsotti–Tate representation of G_{ℚ_q} with tame inertial type of level 1 (principal series), resp. level 2 (cuspidal); combined with Serre's definition of weights this gives the weights of the irreducible ρ̄_q in Theorem 5.1 (3), resp. (4), of [35].
items.locator: §10.3.2, (3) and (4), p. 94, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/kw-theorem-5-1-systems states the weights with Savitt's Corollary 6.15; LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.4/savitt-weight-two-rings plans Savitt's deformation rings (not the corollary itself).

items.name: Saito's theorem [53]: local–global compatibility at the coefficient prime for Hilbert modular forms
items.statement: (Black box) For a Hilbert eigenform (under Carayol's parity hypothesis), ρ_{f,μ}|_{G_{F_𝔭}} at 𝔭 | ℓ is potentially semistable and its Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representation corresponds to π_{f,𝔭} under local Langlands; this needs no residual irreducibility.
items.locator: §10.3.2, (4), p. 94, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/hilbert-modular-form-compatibility-at-p; AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.5/potential-semistability-and-compatibility-at-the-coefficient-prime. The bibliography entry [53] has the wrong title (recorded as AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations/E2).

items.name: Dieulefait [22], Wintenberger [67]: propagating a lift to a compatible system
items.statement: (Black box) A lift ρ_p that is potentially modular over a totally real Galois field lies in an (almost strictly) compatible system (the method of [22] and [67], carried out in §10.3.2).
items.locator: §10.3.2, p. 93, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/dieulefait-families and /brauer-induction-system.

items.name: Regularity inputs for Lemma 9.6 (a) (Lemma (33.B) of [41])
items.statement: (Black box, as used) (i) If B[1/2] is regular then B[[x₁, …, x_r]][1/2] is regular; (ii) if R^inv → R′ is formally smooth (here R′ ≅ R^inv[[T₁, …, T_t]], a trivial T-torsor) and R′[1/2] is regular, then R^inv[1/2] is regular (Lemma (33.B) of Matsumura [41]).
items.locator: proof of Lemma 9.6 (a), p. 88, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6/dyadic-patched-torsor states the conclusion (R_∞[1/2], R^inv_∞[1/2] regular) but no node states these commutative-algebra facts; DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3 has regular local rings, global dimension and localisation, not descent of regularity or regularity of B[[x]][1/2]. Mathlib has IsRegularLocalRing and IsRegularRing (Mathlib/RingTheory/RegularLocalRing/Defs.lean) and polynomial ascent, Polynomial.isRegularRing_of_isRegularRing and MvPolynomial.isRegularRing_of_isRegularRing (Mathlib/RingTheory/RegularLocalRing/Polynomial.lean:78, :108). It lacks the power-series case (i) and the flat descent (ii) (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/10).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 6.1: local points of Taylor's moduli problem X at 2 and at the auxiliary primes for p = 2
items.statement: For p = 2, Taylor's moduli problem X has points with values in ℚ₂ and in ℚ_{p_i}, p_i the auxiliary primes, as for p ≠ 2. Together with the real points (/193), these are the local points from which Moret-Bailly's theorem gives F and a point x ∈ X(F).
items.locator: §6, proof of Theorem 6.1, p. 55, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: KW assert this without argument (p. 55: 'For p = 2 one proves the existence of points with values in Q2 or Qpi, pi auxiliary prime, as for p ≠ 2'). R23.2's text plans 'every prescribed finite local point', and HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves H6 plans 'nonempty real and finite local open loci by explicit abelian varieties'. So the item takes the status of the parallel real-point step /193. But every node that states Taylor's local points assumes an odd residual characteristic: R23.2/taylor-auxiliary-data-p-L-psi-N-M ('l an odd prime'), R23.2/taylor-lemmas-1-3-1-4-local-points-at-p-and-at-infinity ('for l, p odd') and R23.2/taylor-2006-lemmas-4-4-4-5-descent-and-the-cm-point ('l > 2'). And R23.3/kw-ii-theorem-6-1-potential-modularity-of-rho-bar-over-a-controlled-F has proof steps for the p = 2 real points and for k(ρ̄) = 4, but none for these points. So no node states the residual-characteristic-2 versions of Taylor's Lemmas 1.2–1.3. The p = 2 cases of Theorem 6.1(i)–(ii) (/185, /186) and of the Taylor results behind them (/204) depend on them (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/4).

items.name: External (Matsumura [41] 28.M): regularity is detected on completions
items.statement: A Noetherian ring whose completions at all maximal ideals are regular is regular. In KW's use, the completions of R̂[1/p] at its maximal ideals are power series rings E′[[X₁, …, X_d]] over finite extensions E′ of E.
items.locator: §2.3 proof of Proposition 2.2(ii), p. 9, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Split from /34 (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/10). Tau Ceti ModularCurves Layer 4D plans 'preservation and reflection of regularity and dimension under completion of noetherian local rings', and a Noetherian ring is regular when its localisations at maximal ideals are. The accepted PAPER-BOCKLE-IYENGAR-PASKUNAS-23/052 plans the same statement at Layer 4D and DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3. Mathlib has IsRegularLocalRing (Mathlib/RingTheory/RegularLocalRing/Defs.lean) without the completion theorem.

items.name: External: Kummer theory for a field, applied to F^{nr}
items.statement: For a field K and an integer n invertible in K, the Kummer map K^×/(K^×)^n → H¹(G_K, μ_n) is an isomorphism: it is injective with kernel (K^×)^n, and surjective by Hilbert 90. KW apply it with K = F^{nr}, the maximal unramified extension of F_v (so G_K = I_v), and n a power of p.
items.locator: §3.2.5, definition of Z¹_f and proof of Lemma 3.7, pp. 25–26, author copy proofs.pdf (98 pp., PDF dated 30 May 2009)
items.note: Split from /98 (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/10). Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9 plans the Kummer isomorphism with coefficients KummerCoeff K n = μ_n for any field K with n invertible, which covers K = F^{nr}. Tau Ceti at f790474 already has the Kummer map and its kernel for any field: TauCeti.kummerMap (TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisCohomology/Kummer.lean:187) and TauCeti.ker_kummerMap (:260, kernel (K^×)^n). Only surjectivity, which is Hilbert 90, is absent, as that file says. The coefficient change and completion that KW need are /98.

prerequisites.citation: Gebhard Böckle, Presentations of universal deformation rings, in: L-functions and Galois representations (Durham 2004), London Math. Soc. Lecture Note Ser. 320 (2007), 24–58
prerequisites.why: Theorem 5.2 gives the presentations over local deformation rings behind Proposition 4.5; the atlas cites only Böckle's appendix to Khare's paper.

prerequisites.citation: Mark Dickinson, On the modularity of certain 2-adic Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 109 (2001), 319–382
prerequisites.why: Lemma 42 is Lemma 4.3(5)(i), H¹(SL₂(𝔽_{2^r}), M₂(𝔽)) = 0; the paper also gives the earlier results towards KW I Theorem 4.1(1).

prerequisites.citation: Christopher Skinner and Andrew Wiles, Base change and a problem of Serre, Duke Math. J. 107 (2001), 15–25
prerequisites.why: The reduction of modularity to solvable base change, used throughout §§8–9.

prerequisites.citation: Richard Taylor, On icosahedral Artin representations II, Amer. J. Math. 125 (2003), 549–566
prerequisites.why: Lemma 2.2 (solvable totally real extensions with prescribed local behaviour) is used in §7.6 and in the proof of Theorem 9.7; the atlas plans the statement but no roadmap takes the paper as a source.

prerequisites.citation: Emil Artin and John Tate, Class Field Theory (AMS Chelsea reprint, 2009), Chapter X (the Grunwald–Wang theorem)

prerequisites.citation: Jean-Pierre Wintenberger, On p-adic geometric representations of G_ℚ, Doc. Math. Extra Volume: John H. Coates' Sixtieth Birthday (2006), 819–827
prerequisites.why: The propagation of lifts to compatible systems in §10.3.2; KW II withdraw its claim of strict compatibility.

routes.reason: §2 of KW II is the commutative algebra of complete Noetherian local 𝒪-algebras that the deformation theory rests on, and DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1–R03.4 owns exactly that: coefficient categories and completed tensor products (R03.1), representability, hulls and obstructions (R03.2), dimension, regularity and complete intersections (R03.3), finiteness and characteristic-zero points (R03.4). The missing items are general facts these layers need but do not yet state: relative tangent spaces, the tangent space of a completed tensor product, and Proposition 2.2(ii), that a completed tensor product of domains with an 𝒪-point and regular generic fibre is again one (R03.1); Proposition 2.1 for a non-Schur ρ̄ (framed rings formally smooth over the hull) and its use for deformation conditions (R03.2); the regularity descent along faithfully flat local maps (Matsumura 33.B; the completion half, 28.M, is planned at Tau Ceti ModularCurves Layer 4D, /342), including regularity of R^inv_∞[1/2] in Lemma 9.6(a), Chevalley's comparison of ideal topologies, and the excellence of finitely generated 𝒪-algebras with the equidimensionality of completions (Grothendieck; Matsumura §34) (R03.3); the maximal ideals of R[1/p], the Jacobson property of R′[1/p] (EGA IV 10.5.8) and Corollary 2.3, that a flat reduced quotient is determined by its 𝒪′-points (R03.4). Corollary 2.3 is already invoked, unstated, by LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/kw-local-conditions and GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/factorization-through-local-conditions.

Lemma 3.8 is the algebraisation step in the proof of Proposition 3.6 (ordinary deformation rings, §3.2.5); R08.6/export-ordinary asserts the smooth resolution without it. Its inputs, Weierstrass preparation and division over 𝒪[[T]], are in Mathlib, so it belongs with the local ring it serves. Kummer theory over F^{nr} with 𝒪-module coefficients (/98), which defines the finite cocycles Z¹_f of §3.2.5, is the other deformation-specific input of Lemma 3.7 and R08.6/export-ordinary. It comes here from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.5, whose text leaves 'the deformation-specific calculations' to R08; its μ_n core (/343) is planned at Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9 (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/10).

Lemma 3.5 is the ordinarity of three kinds of lift over an unramified F: (i) crystalline of weight 2 ≤ k ≤ p with ordinary reduction, (ii) semistable non-crystalline of weight 2, and (iii) weight 2 and crystalline over ℚ_p^{nr}(μ_p) with ordinary reduction. It belongs to PadicHodgeTheory R06.4, whose text asks for 'the ordinary and crystalline criteria actually invoked in those branches', with p = 2 and the modular weights p and p + 1 stated separately. PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/two-dimensional-ordinarity-criterion proves the criteria for ℚ_p only; KW II need them for unramified F_v/ℚ_p (§3.2.2(i), k(ρ̄_v) = p + 1, and §3.2.6). They are the same filtered-module computations, so the paper is a source for stating them over unramified F. All three parts are planned at R06.4 and consumed by LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.6 (kw-local-conditions, export-ordinary); R06.4 → R08.6 closes no cycle (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/7).

The Grunwald–Wang theorem (/210) and Lemma 7.10 (/252), whose p = 2 case finds a square root of a character after a solvable totally real base change, go where three accepted extractions send the same theorem and the same kind of argument (roots of characters and local–global obstructions): PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/84 (Lemma 5.3.1, from Artin–Tate, Chapter X, Theorem 5, as here), PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21/189 and PAPER-ALLEN-ETAL-23/328, all at ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2/R02.4. KW use Grunwald–Wang for the local conditions of Theorem 6.1(iii)(b) (p. 57) and, for p = 2, in the proof of Lemma 7.10 (p. 69), whose consumer is Theorem 8.2 (p. 73). R02.2 and R02.4 close no cycle with the consumers, PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.3 and SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.6. This replaces the earlier routes of /210 to InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.4 and of /252 to GL2ModularityLifting R22.1 (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/1, /2). The InverseGalois packet and PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23/130 still place Grunwald–Wang at IG.4, so the choice of a single owner is left to the maintainer. This route formerly took Kummer theory over F^{nr} (/98) to R02.5; that item now goes to LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.6 (route 2, RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/10).

These are the finite-group facts for residual images in characteristic 2 that R01.4 owns ('the finite-subgroup facts of GL₂/PGL₂ used in the source arguments … Isolate characteristic two'). GlobalGaloisDeformations already has an open request to R01.4 for both; no R01.4 node states them.

Used in Lemma 5.10(g) to count Taylor–Wiles primes for p = 2 (t = h¹_{S−split}(Q_n, 𝔽)); R04.5/dyadic-taylor-wiles-primes uses it implicitly. For p = 2 it follows from H⁰(G_F, Ad/Z) = 0. The arithmetic character ψ of §8.1 with its kinds (i)–(iii) (/254) is a datum of the deformation problems of KW II §§8–10, which R04.6 supplies ('Supply the deformation problems used in KW II §§9–10'); R04.6/kw-deformation-data already takes 'ψ as in KW II §8.1' by reference. R04.6 precedes GL2ModularityLifting R22.1 and PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.1, and R04.6 → SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.6 (Theorems 8.2 and 8.4) closes no cycle. The earlier route of /254 to GL2ModularityLifting R22.1 lay downstream of R20.6 (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/1).

Two inputs of the potential-modularity and finiteness arguments that R23–R24 use without stating them. The dihedral-image step keeps ρ̄|_{F(μ_p)} irreducible along the field choices, which is R23.5's 'control of the extension'. Khare's Lemma 4.2 (a representation of G_{ℚ_ℓ}, ℓ ≠ p, into GL₂ of a characteristic-p ring becomes unramified over a finite extension) is a hypothesis of R24.1/auxiliary-totally-real-field-for-the-finiteness-argument, which notes it could not be located. Khare's Lemma 2.2 (/209), which the R23.3 node kw-ii-theorem-6-1-potential-modularity-of-rho-bar-over-a-controlled-F imports, was routed here. It is also used in the proof of Theorem 8.2 (p. 73) at SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.6, which that node imports, so here it closed a cycle. It now goes to HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.3 (route 8) (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/1).

R18.3 owns definite quaternionic forms and their stabilisers; Taylor's neatness lemma (reduction S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝒪) → S_{k,ψ}(U, 𝔽) surjective, perfect pairings) is the property of those spaces that §§7–8 use. Khare's Lemma 2.2 (/209) goes with it. KW use it to take the level of Lemma 8.3 neat in the sense of Taylor's Lemma 1.1 (p. 73), and to lift the restriction p ≠ 3 of [59] §5 in the proof of Theorem 6.1 (pp. 56–57). R18.3 precedes SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.6, and R18.3 → PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.3 closes no cycle; at R23.3 the lemma closed one, through the R23.3 node's import of Theorem 8.2 (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/1).

R20.6 is to 'supply the optimisation inputs used inside KW', and the GL2ModularityLifting--R22.1 packet has an open request to R20.6 for Theorems 8.2 and 8.4. Its nodes so far work over ℚ; these results are the totally real versions after an allowable base change (level lowering, minimal-at-p lifts, the weight-2 to weight-(p + 1) passage of Lemma 8.3 through 𝔽[ℙ¹(k_w)] ≅ 𝟙 ⊕ V, and lifts with prescribed local types). Kisin's Corollary 3.1.11 and Lemma 3.5.3 (/273), the method of proof of Theorem 8.4, come here too; at GL2ModularityLifting R22.4, downstream of R20.6, they closed a cycle (RT-PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/1). The other inputs of Theorems 8.2 and 8.4 come from layers that close no cycle with R20.6: ψ (/254) from GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.6; Lemma 7.10 (/252) and Grunwald–Wang (/210) from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2/R02.4; Khare's Lemma 2.2 (/209) and Taylor's neatness lemma (/272) from HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.3; and Lemma 7.1 (/222) from R18.3–R18.6.

sourceIssues.locator: §3.1, proof of Proposition 3.3, p. 21 of the author copy proofs.pdf (Invent. Math. 178 (2009) not compared)
sourceIssues.printed: The proof deduces O-flatness of R from smoothness of R0 over O and flatness of Spec(R∞^{□,ψ}) → M2.
sourceIssues.correction: “… and Spec(R_∞^{□,ψ}) → M(X² − 1) is flat”; since f₀ factors through the closed subscheme M(X² − 1), ℛ = ℛ₀ ×_{M(X²−1)} Spec(R_∞^{□,ψ}) is flat over ℛ₀, hence over 𝒪.
sourceIssues.reason: R_∞^{□,ψ} is the completion of the local ring of M(X² − 1) (defined two sentences earlier), a closed subscheme of M₂. For ρ̄(c) = id, O_{M₂,ξ_M} → R_∞^{□,ψ} kills tr(M), which is nonzero in O_{M₂,ξ_M} (the 𝒪-point M = I of M₂ passes through ξ_M and has trace 2); a flat local homomorphism is faithfully flat, hence injective, so the map to M₂ is not flat in the case M = id where the resolution is needed.

sourceIssues.locator: §3.2.1, proof of Lemma 3.5(i), p. 22 of the author copy proofs.pdf (Invent. Math. 178 (2009) not compared)
sourceIssues.printed: The proof asserts existence of a non-trivial subobject N of M with Fil1 (N ) = 0. For k = p, it says failure would force Filp−1 (M ) = M by 0.9. of [26], a contradiction. It repeats the assertion, pointing to a non-trivial OF -summand with invertible semilinear Frobenius φ : M → M, and citing [46].
sourceIssues.correction: The first sentence should concern the mod p Fontaine–Laffaille module: “Therefore M/pM has a non-trivial subobject N̄ with Fil¹(N̄) = 0”; the second (“It follows that M has …”) is then the lift to the lattice M via the unit-root summand of φ, which gives an unramified quotient of V.
sourceIssues.reason: The two sentences are verbatim identical, so the step “It follows that …” derives a statement from itself. The first is deduced from the unramified quotient of the Fp[G_F]-module V(M) (mod p information), which by Fontaine–Laffaille theory concerns the reduction of M; the second invokes the invertible-φ summand of the integral M ([46]).

sourceIssues.locator: §3.2.2(i), p. 23 of the author copy proofs.pdf (Invent. Math. 178 (2009) not compared)
sourceIssues.printed: The source additionally requires ρv |Iv to be crystalline of weight 2 whenever ρ̄v is finite flat at v, stating that this can happen only when k = 2.
sourceIssues.correction: “when ρ̄_v is ramified and finite flat at v (which forces k(ρ̄_v) = 2), ρ_v is crystalline of weight 2”; an unramified ρ̄_v is finite flat but has k(ρ̄_v) = p, and for it no crystallinity condition is imposed (in §3.2.5 finite cocycles are used only when k(ρ̄_v) = 2).
sourceIssues.reason: The paper itself records that an unramified ρ̄_v has k(ρ̄_v) = p (p. 23: “If ρ̄v is unramified (this implies that k(ρ̄) = p)”; p. 24: “if ρ̄v is unramified, we have k(ρ̄v) = p”), and unramified representations are finite flat (étale group schemes). For p > 2 the weight-2 lifts of an unramified ρ̄_v have inertial type ω_p^{p−2} ⊕ 1, which is ramified for every p ≥ 3, so imposing crystallinity would empty the ring; the proof of Proposition 3.6 uses χ₁ = χ_pω_p^{k−2} with Z¹_f = Z¹ in this case.

sourceIssues.locator: §3.3.3, case p = 2, p. 36 of the author copy proofs.pdf (Invent. Math. 178 (2009) not compared)
sourceIssues.printed: The proof chooses ρ(σ) so that e1 + λe2 together with ρ(F )(e1 + λe2 ) are its eigenspaces, with respective eigenvalues ε and ε−1.
sourceIssues.correction: Take the eigenvalues ε and ε^q on e₁ + λe₂ and ρ(F)(e₁ + λe₂) (so that ρ|_{I_q} ≅ χ′ ⊕ χ′^q as required), replacing ε − ε^{−1} by ε − ε^q in the matrix and valuation conditions; this coincides with the printed choice only when χ′^{q+1} = 1 (automatic for p odd, since then the p-part of q² − 1 divides q + 1), which could alternatively be added as a hypothesis for p = 2.
sourceIssues.reason: ρ(F) = (−1 z; 0 1) is an involution swapping the two eigenlines, so int(ρ(F))(ρ(σ)) has eigenvalue ε^{−1} on e₁ + λe₂ and ε on ρ(F)(e₁ + λe₂), i.e. equals ρ(σ)^{−1}; the tame relation FσF^{−1} = σ^q requires ρ(σ)^q, so ε^{q+1} = 1 is needed. For p = 2 and q ≡ 1 mod 4, a character of 𝔽_{q²}^× of 2-power order not factoring through the norm has order 2^{v₂(q−1)+1}, which does not divide q + 1 (v₂(q + 1) = 1); e.g. q = 5, ε a primitive 8th root of unity, ε⁶ ≠ 1. The stated hypotheses (level 2, 2-power order, 2 | q + 1) do not exclude this.

sourceIssues.locator: §4.2, proof of Lemma 4.6 (independence of the choice of the g̃_v), p. 44 of the author copy proofs.pdf (Invent. Math. 178 (2009) not compared)
sourceIssues.printed: The proof claims independence from g̃_v: replacing it by g̃_v(1 + h_v) changes a_v to g ↦ a_v(g) − (ad(g)(h_v) − h_v) and changes (x_v ∪ a_v) to (x_v ∪ a_v − x_v ∪ δ(h_v)). It invokes x_v ∪ δ(h_v) = −δ(x_v ∪ h_v) to assert that inv((x_v ∪ a_v) + z_v) is unchanged.
sourceIssues.correction: For p > 2 one may replace h_v by its trace-zero part (δ kills scalars) and the displayed identity applies. For p = 2 argue instead: δ(h_v) is a 1-cocycle of D_v with values in Ad⁰ whose class is the image of h_v mod Ad⁰ ∈ H⁰(D_v, Ad/Ad⁰) under the connecting map, i.e. lies in L_v (Case 1); since [x] ∈ H¹_{{L_v^⊥}}, x_v ∈ L_v^⊥ and inv(x_v ∪ δ(h_v)) = ⟨[x_v], [δ(h_v)]⟩ = 0 by local Tate duality. So the value of (x, u) is unchanged.
sourceIssues.reason: The cup product ∪ is defined only through the pairing (Ad⁰)^*(1) × Ad⁰ → 𝔽(1) → 𝔽_p(1). The lifts of g_v ∈ GL₂(R^{□,ψ}_S)₁ to GL₂(R_u) differ by factors 1 + I_u·M₂(𝔽), so h_v ranges over Ad = M₂(𝔽) (the proof itself later takes "h_v ∈ Ad"), and ad(g)(h_v) − h_v ∈ Ad⁰ for every h_v. For p = 2, Ad⁰ ⊃ Z has no G_F-stable complement in Ad (Lemma 4.3(5)(ii)), so x_v ∪ h_v is not defined when tr h_v ≠ 0 and the identity x_v ∪ δ(h_v) = −δ(x_v ∪ h_v) has no meaning. As printed, the hypothesis [x] ∈ H¹_{{L_v^⊥}}(S, (Ad⁰)^*(1)) — a genuine condition only when p = 2, since L_v = 0 for p > 2 — is never used in showing that (x, u) is well defined; this step is exactly where it is needed. Lemma 4.6 remains true with the correction.

sourceIssues.locator: §7.6.1, Corollary 7.8(ii), p. 68 of the author copy proofs.pdf (Invent. Math. 178 (2009) not compared)
sourceIssues.printed: Part (ii), for k = 2, assumes πv^{U1(v)} non-trivial, πv^{U0(v)} trivial, and the character of kv∗ factoring through the norm to F∗p. It asserts that ρπ|Dv has weight 2 and becomes crystalline over Qp^nr(µp); if πv is ordinary, it writes ρπ|Iv as (ωp^{k−2}χp ∗ ; 0 1).
sourceIssues.correction: … then ρπ|Iv is of the form (εvχp ∗ ; 0 1), where εv = ωp^j is the character of Iv corresponding by local class field theory to the (non-trivial) character of kv∗ ≅ U0(v)/U1(v) through which U0(v) acts on πv^{U1(v)} (the nebentypus at v). In the paper's application (type (B), ψ of kind (ii)) j = k(ρ̄) − 2, so the 'k' of the exponent is the Serre weight of §8.3.3 (B), not the weight 2 of π.
sourceIssues.reason: Case (ii) fixes k = 2, so ωp^{k−2} = 1 and the printed form is (χp ∗ ; 0 1), of determinant χp on Iv. But πv has no U0(v)-fixed vector, so the character of kv∗ by which U0(v) acts on πv^{U1(v)}, which is the restriction of the central character to 𝒪v∗, is non-trivial; hence det ρπ|Iv = χp·εv with εv ≠ 1, contradicting the printed form. For an ordinary πv the unramified quotient carries the unit root, so the sub-character on Iv is εvχp. As intended — with the exponent the one of §8.3.3 (B), j = k(ρ̄) − 2 — the statement is right, so the slip affects nothing downstream.

sourceIssues.locator: §7.1, proof of Lemma 7.2, case (i) (p > 2), p. 61 of the author copy proofs.pdf (Invent. Math. 178 (2009) not compared)
sourceIssues.printed: For p > 2, the source justifies independence of γv,f from f by asserting that the residual representation associated with each f ∈ Sk,ψ(U, O)m remains the same.
sourceIssues.correction: Add the hypothesis that for each v ∈ Σ not above p either ρ̄m is ramified at v or N(v) ≢ −1 (mod p) (if N(v) ≡ −1 mod p, a base change in which v acquires even residue degree gives N(v′) ≡ 1 mod p), or fix γv by localising also at an eigenvalue of the operator given by a uniformiser of Dv∗, as the case p = 2 does by taking Uv = Dv∗.
sourceIssues.reason: The residual representation determines γ̄v only up to the swap allowed by ρ̄m|Dv. If ρ̄m is unramified at v and N(v) ≡ −1 mod p, let η be the unramified quadratic character of G_{Fv}. Then γ and γη both square to ψv, and ρ̄(Frobv) has eigenvalues {N(v)γ̄(Frobv), γ̄(Frobv)} = {−γ̄(Frobv), γ̄(Frobv)} for both, while γ̄η̄ ≠ γ̄ since p is odd. So the stated fact does not force γv,f = γv,f′. 𝕋ψ(U) contains no operator at v ∈ Σ, so localising at 𝔪 does not fix the eigenvalue of a uniformiser of Dv∗, which determines γv,f by the Remark after Lemma 7.2. Lemma 8.1 makes ρ̄F unramified at every v ∤ p, so in KW's setting the only case left open is N(v) ≡ −1 mod p. Lemma 9.1's map R̄^ψ_S → 𝕋ψ(U)_𝔪, with a fixed γv in the local ring, relies on Lemma 7.2.

sourceIssues.locator: §7.6.2, Definition 7.9 and the following paragraph, p. 68 of the author copy proofs.pdf (Invent. Math. 178 (2009) not compared)
sourceIssues.printed: The source defines an allowable base change as a totally real solvable F′/F of even degree, unramified above p and split there if ρ̄|Dp is irreducible, satisfying im(ρ̄) = im(ρ̄|F′) and absolute irreducibility of ρ̄|F′(µp).

sourceIssues.reason: The field F of §7.6.2 is assumed only to give non-solvable image (p = 2) or absolute irreducibility over F(µp) (p > 2). sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 10.1, p. 91 (the morphisms π₁, π₂, β, α, γ), with the definition of R̄^{ψ_F}_F on the same page of the author copy proofs.pdf (Invent. Math. 178 (2009) not compared)
sourceIssues.printed: The proof defines R̄^{ψ_F}_F over F for minimal odd deformations of ρ̄_F unramified away from p. Absolute irreducibility of ρ̄ and ρ̄|G_F is said to give CNL_O-algebra maps π₁ : R^{ψ_F}_F → R̄^{□,ψ_F}_F, π₂ : R^ψ_{Q,S} → R̄^{□,ψ}_{Q,S}, β : R^{ψ_F}_F → R^ψ_{Q,S}, α : R̄^{□,ψ_F}_F → R̄^{□,ψ}_{Q,S}, satisfying απ₁ = π₂β. Using π₁(R^{ψ_F}_F) = R̄^{ψ_F}_F together with π₂(R^ψ_{Q,S}) = R̄^ψ_{Q,S}, it obtains the induced CNL_O-algebra map γ : R̄^{ψ_F}_F → R̄^ψ_{Q,S}.
sourceIssues.correction: Construct the comparison map only modulo p. By the fourth bullet, τ|_{G_F} (τ the mod-p universal representation over R̄^ψ_{ℚ,S}/(p)) is unramified outside the places above p and ∞, so it is classified by a map β̄ : R^{ψ_F}_F → R̄^ψ_{ℚ,S}/(p); in framed form R^{□,ψ_F}_F → R̄^{□,ψ}_{ℚ,S}/(p), with the frames at w | p, ∞ taken from those at p, ∞. At w | p this factors through R̄^{□,ψ_F}_w, because the restriction R^□_{F_w} → R^□_{ℚ_p} → R̄^{□,ψ}_p kills the ideal of R̄^{□,ψ_F}_w: every 𝒪′-point of the flat reduced ring R̄^{□,ψ}_p restricts to a lift of the same type (A), (B) or (C) over the unramified F_w (Corollary 2.3). At the infinite places oddness is preserved. Hence β̄ factors through γ̄ : R̄^{ψ_F}_F → R̄^ψ_{ℚ,S}/(p), which carries the universal mod-p representation of G_F to τ|_{G_F}. The rest of the proof (finite image of τ, then 3.14 of [31] or Lemma 3.6 of [34]) is unchanged.
sourceIssues.reason: R^{ψ_F}_F and R̄^{□,ψ_F}_F classify deformations of ρ̄_F that are unramified outside the places above p. β and α would send the universal deformation over R^ψ_{ℚ,S}, resp. each 𝒪′-point x of R̄^{□,ψ}_{ℚ,S}, to its restriction to G_F, which need not be unramified above primes ℓ ≠ p in S. Theorem 10.1 allows at such ℓ any ring of Theorem 3.1, including the semistable ring of §3.3.4, whose points are (γχ_p ∗; 0 γ). Suppose ρ̄|_{D_ℓ} ≅ (γ̄χ̄_p ∗; 0 γ̄) with ∗ ramified, for example ρ̄ = ρ̄_{E,p} for an elliptic curve E with multiplicative reduction at ℓ and p ∤ v_ℓ(Δ_E), and take the §3.3.4 ring at ℓ. Then every 𝒪′-point x has ρ_x|_{I_ℓ} = γ|_{I_ℓ} ⊗ (1 c; 0 1) with c ≢ 0 mod π. So ρ_x(I_ℓ) is infinite, and ρ_x stays ramified over every finite extension of ℚ_ℓ. Such points exist: R̄^ψ_S is finite (Theorem 10.1) of dimension ≥ 1 (Proposition 4.5), so Corollary 4.7 applies. Composing α with one of them would give an 𝒪′-point of R̄^{□,ψ_F}_F that is ramified above ℓ, which is impossible. So α and β do not exist in this case. The fourth bullet only makes the mod-p representation τ unramified outside p (Lemma 4.2 of [33]), and that is all the correction needs.

sourceIssues.locator: §3.2.4, p. 24 of the author copy proofs.pdf (Invent. Math. 178 (2009) not compared)
sourceIssues.printed: Section 3.2.4 treats irreducible ρ̄v and weight 2 deformations. It sends p = 2, k(ρ̄v) = 2 to the preceding crystalline case, then assumes p ≠ 2. Citing Savitt, item 3 of th. 6.22 of [54], it identifies the ring as O[[T1, T2]]/(T1T2 − p) when O is sufficiently big.
sourceIssues.correction: Add the hypothesis 3 ≤ k(ρ̄_p) ≤ p. When p ≠ 2 and k(ρ̄_p) = 2, the required type (ω_p^{k(ρ̄)−2} ⊕ 1, 0) is trivial, so the weight-two lifts are the crystalline weight-2 lifts of §3.2.3. Their fixed-determinant ring is formally smooth, 𝒪[[T]] (framed: 𝒪[[T₁, …, T₄]]), as in the case p = 2 that §3.2.4 already sends to §3.2.3.
sourceIssues.reason: For p odd, §3.2.2(i) (p. 23) gives the weight-two lifts the inertial Weil–Deligne parameter (ω_p^{k(ρ̄)−2} ⊕ 1, 0). At k(ρ̄_p) = 2 this is the trivial type with N = 0, so the lifts are crystalline of weight 2. The case occurs for irreducible ρ̄_p: ρ̄_p|I_p ≅ ω₂ ⊕ ω₂^p, for instance E[p] for an elliptic curve with supersingular reduction at p, has Serre weight 2. Savitt's Theorem 6.22(3) concerns a principal-series type ω̃^i ⊕ ω̃^j with i ≢ j mod p − 1 (as the node LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.4/savitt-weight-two-rings records). Here i = k(ρ̄_p) − 2 and j = 0, and k(ρ̄_p) ≤ p for irreducible ρ̄_p, so it applies exactly when 3 ≤ k(ρ̄_p) ≤ p. The two rings differ. The special fibre of 𝒪[[T]] is 𝔽[[T]], a regular domain, while that of 𝒪[[T₁, T₂]]/(T₁T₂ − p) is 𝔽[[T₁, T₂]]/(T₁T₂), which is not a domain. Both are flat domains over 𝒪 of relative dimension 1 with regular generic fibre, which is all Theorem 3.1 asserts, and the paper uses Savitt's explicit form nowhere else. So nothing downstream is affected.
